Grammar & commentary

Prathama Carita · प्रथमचरितम् · Chapter 1 of 13

मधुकैटभवधःThe Slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha

madhukaiṭabhavadhaḥ

104 mantras · 1.1–1.104

❁

Overview

Mārkaṇḍeya promises the story of Sāvarṇi, the eighth Manu (1.1–3). King Suratha, betrayed by his ministers, rides alone into the forest and reaches the hermitage of the sage Medhas (1.4–11). Still brooding over his lost city, elephant and treasury (1.12–16), he meets Samādhi, a merchant thrown out by his own wife and sons, who cannot stop worrying about them either (1.17–34). Together they ask Medhas why their minds cling to what has rejected them, though they see the fault (1.35–45). Medhas answers that every creature has knowledge, yet all are bound by mamatā, and that the cause is Mahāmāyā, who deludes even the wise, who is the knowledge that liberates and the cause of bondage (1.46–58). Asked who she is (1.59–62), he tells how, at the end of an age, the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha, born from the wax of Viṣṇu’s ears while he slept, rose to kill Brahmā; Brahmā praised the Goddess as Viṣṇu’s Yoganidrā (1.63–87); she left Viṣṇu’s body, he woke, fought them for five thousand years, and, when the deluded demons offered him a boon, chose their death and slew them on his thighs, where the flood had not reached (1.88–104).

  • Mamatā and moha: knowing and still clinging
  • Mahāmāyā as bondage and as liberation
  • Yoganidrā: the Goddess within Viṣṇu
  • Praise (stuti) as the act that turns events
  • The frame of the Manvantara: grace inside history
About this chapter
Forms of the Devī
Mahāmāyā, the power that binds and releases (1.55–58); Yoganidrā, the sleep of Viṣṇu (1.54, 1.66–71); Tāmasī, the dark Goddess who leaves Viṣṇu’s body (1.89); and, in Brahmā’s hymn, Svāhā, Svadhā and the syllable (1.73–74), the night of dissolution — Kālarātri, Mahārātri, Moharātri (1.79) — and the mild and the terrible at once (1.80–82).
Significance of the events
The frame story poses the question the whole text answers: why knowing is not enough to be free. The first battle is not fought by the Goddess at all: her act is to withdraw from Viṣṇu, so that the god who sustains the world can wake. The demons are destroyed by the same delusion that held the king and the merchant: they offer their enemy a boon.
Sanskrit patterns to watch
Narrative perfects (उवाच, बभूव, ददर्श) and aorists (अभूत्, अद्राक्षीत्); long sentences carried over verse boundaries in the dialogue (1.12–16, 1.22–24, 1.51–55); genitives of the speaker with verbs of hearing (गदतो मम, 1.2); gerundives (कार्यः, 1.54); passives of causatives (सम्मोह्यते, 1.55); and, in Brahmā’s hymn, the second person: त्वम् with nominative predicates, vocatives, and feminine stems in -ā, -ī and -ti.
The teaching, as distinct from the narrative
Literally, a king and a merchant are consoled by a sage, and a god wakes to kill two demons. As teaching, the chapter says that attachment (mamatā) is not a private weakness but the working of the power that keeps the world in being; that the same power, as knowledge (vidyā), is the cause of liberation (1.57); and that she is not reached by argument but by praise and surrender — Brahmā, helpless on the lotus, does not fight; he praises.
Carita
Prathama Carita (the first episode). In the recitation tradition its presiding form is Mahākālī; this is the Gita Press viniyoga, not a statement of the Purāṇa text.
Recited before the chapter

These lines belong to the recitation (the Gita Press pāṭha), not to the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa text, and are kept apart from the numbered mantras.

Verse 1.1

Speaker
‹›

ॐ ऐंमार्कण्डेय उवाच॥⁠१⁠॥

mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

मार्कण्डेयः · उवाच

mārkaṇḍeyaḥ · uvāca

Word by word

  1. मार्कण्डेयःmārkaṇḍeyaḥMārkaṇḍeya, the sagem. nom. sg. of मार्कण्डेय (taddhita: ‘descendant of Mṛkaṇḍu’); subject of उवाच
  2. उवाचuvācasaid√वच् (adādi, 2P ‘to speak’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, kartari prayoga

Translation

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

In readable EnglishMārkaṇḍeya said:

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • मार्कण्डेय उवाच mārkaṇḍeya uvāca → मार्कण्डेयः + उवाच

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17), लोपः शाकल्यस्य (8.3.19)

    -aḥ before a vowel other than a: the visarga becomes y, the y is dropped, and the two vowels stand apart (मार्कण्डेय | उवाच). The gap is not closed again.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • उवाच uvāca

    Perfect of √वच्: reduplication उ-वाच with samprasāraṇa of the reduplicated syllable (व → उ). The perfect is the narrative past of the Purāṇas: ‘(he) said’.

Anvaya · prose order

मार्कण्डेयः उवाच।

mārkaṇḍeyaḥ uvāca |

Subject and verb: a speaker label.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The speaker label that opens the Devī Māhātmya. In the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa the sage Mārkaṇḍeya is answering his pupil Krauṣṭuki’s questions about the ages of the Manus; the whole of the Devī Māhātmya is a story told inside that answer.

Traditional interpretation

The Gita Press pāṭha counts every uvāca line as a mantra, which is how the text reaches seven hundred (the chapter colophons count them separately: 57 uvāca mantras in all). In recitation this first mantra carries the bījas ॐ ऐं, which belong to the pāṭha, not to the Purāṇa.

Verse 1.2

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

सावर्णिः सूर्यतनयो यो मनुः कथ्यतेऽष्टमः।निशामय तदुत्पत्तिं विस्तराद् गदतो मम॥⁠२⁠॥

sāvarṇiḥ sūryatanayo yo manuḥ kathyate'ṣṭamaḥ |niśāmaya tadutpattiṃ vistarād gadato mama ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

सावर्णिः · सूर्यतनयः · यः · मनुः · कथ्यते · अष्टमःनिशामय · तदुत्पत्तिम् · विस्तरात् · गदतः · मम

sāvarṇiḥ · sūryatanayaḥ · yaḥ · manuḥ · kathyate · aṣṭamaḥniśāmaya · tadutpattim · vistarāt · gadataḥ · mama

Word by word

  1. सावर्णिःsāvarṇiḥSāvarṇim. nom. sg. of सावर्णि, a metronymic: ‘son of Savarṇā’ (Chāyā, the Sun’s consort)
  2. सूर्यतनयःsūryatanayaḥthe son of the Sunm. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to सावर्णिः
  3. यःyaḥwhorelative pronoun यद्, m. nom. sg.
  4. मनुःmanuḥManu, the progenitor who presides over an agem. nom. sg. of मनु (u-stem); predicate of कथ्यते
  5. कथ्यतेkathyateis called, is spoken of√कथ् (curādi, 10, ‘to tell’), karmaṇi prayoga, laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  6. अष्टमःaṣṭamaḥthe eighthordinal of अष्टन्, m. nom. sg.; qualifies मनुः
  7. निशामयniśāmayahear, listen toनि + √शम् (causative stem निशामय- ‘to perceive’), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  8. तदुत्पत्तिम्tadutpattimhis originf. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); object of निशामय
  9. विस्तरात्vistarātin detail, at lengthm. abl. sg. of विस्तर, used adverbially
  10. गदतःgadataḥtelling, as (I) tellpresent participle (śatṛ) of √गद् ‘to speak’, m. gen. sg.; agrees with मम
  11. ममmamaof me, from mefirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg.; ‘hear from me’ (the speaker heard is in the genitive)

Translation

Sāvarṇi, the son of the Sun, who is called the eighth Manu — hear his origin from me as I tell it in detail.

In readable EnglishSāvarṇi, the Sun’s son, is spoken of as the eighth Manu. Listen as I tell you at length how he came to be.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सूर्यतनयो यो sūryatanayo yo → सूर्यतनयः + यः

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o: the visarga (as रु) turns to u, and a + u gives o. The same change gives यो मनुः and गदतो मम.

  • कथ्यतेऽष्टमः kathyate'ṣṭamaḥ → कथ्यते + अष्टमः

    vowel sandhi (pūrvarūpa) · एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    A word-final e before initial a: the a is absorbed into the e. The avagraha (ऽ) marks the lost a.

  • विस्तराद् गदतो vistarād gadato → विस्तरात् + गदतः

    consonant sandhi (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    Final t becomes d before a voiced sound (here g). The Gita Press writes the d with a virāma and a space.

  • तदुत्पत्तिं tadutpattiṃ → तद् + उत्पत्तिम्

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    The pronoun stem tat ends in d before the vowel of उत्पत्ति. The final m of the compound becomes anusvāra before the next word’s v (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • सूर्यतनयः sūryatanayaḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    सूर्य + तनय
    Vigraha
    सूर्यस्य तनयः sūryasya tanayaḥ
    Literally
    “son of the Sun”
    In the verse
    Sāvarṇi, whose father is Sūrya

  • तदुत्पत्तिम् tadutpattim

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    तद् + उत्पत्ति
    Vigraha
    तस्य उत्पत्तिः (ताम्) tasya utpattiḥ (tām)
    Literally
    “the origin of him”
    In the verse
    how Sāvarṇi came to be — the story that follows
Morphology & anvaya

  • कथ्यते kathyate

    Passive present: stem कथ्य- (√कथ् + yak) with the ātmanepada ending -ते. ‘Is called’; the Manu is the grammatical subject.

  • निशामय niśāmaya

    Imperative of the causative stem of नि + √शम्, a Purāṇic idiom for ‘listen’ (literally ‘perceive’).

  • गदतः gadataḥ

    Present participle गदत् (√गद् + śatṛ), genitive singular: ‘of (me) telling’. With verbs of hearing the source is put in the genitive.

Anvaya · prose order

यः सूर्यतनयः सावर्णिः अष्टमः मनुः कथ्यते, तदुत्पत्तिं विस्तरात् गदतः मम निशामय।

yaḥ sūryatanayaḥ sāvarṇiḥ aṣṭamaḥ manuḥ kathyate, tadutpattiṃ vistarāt gadataḥ mama niśāmaya |

A relative clause (यः … कथ्यते) names the subject; the main clause is the imperative निशामय with its object तदुत्पत्तिम्, and गदतः मम gives the speaker.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Mārkaṇḍeya announces his subject: the origin of Sāvarṇi, the eighth Manu. The frame closes in the last mantra of the text (13.29), where King Suratha is promised rebirth from the Sun as Sāvarṇi. The glory of the Goddess is told as the answer to a question about a Manu.

Traditional interpretation

The chapter colophons place the text in the Purāṇa’s account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara (सावर्णिके मन्वन्तरे). Each Manu presides over one age of the world; the eighth age is still to come.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the Goddess first appears inside an ordinary story of loss and succession. Grace, in this text, works through history, not around it.

Word by word

  1. महामायानुभावेनmahāmāyānubhāvenaby the power of Mahāmāyām. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); instrument of बभूव
  2. यथाyathāhow, in what wayindeclinable (relative adverb of manner)
  3. मन्वन्तराधिपःmanvantarādhipaḥlord of a manvantaram. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate nominative with बभूव
  4. सःsaḥhepronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.
  5. बभूवbabhūvabecame√भू (bhvādi, 1P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  6. महाभागःmahābhāgaḥthe greatly fortunatem. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies सावर्णिः

Translation

How, by the power of Mahāmāyā, that greatly fortunate Sāvarṇi, son of Ravi, became lord of a manvantara —

In readable EnglishHear how, by the grace of Mahāmāyā, that blessed Sāvarṇi, son of the Sun, came to rule an age of the world.

The verse continues the sentence of 1.2; ‘Hear’ is supplied from निशामय there.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • महामायानुभावेन mahāmāyānubhāvena → महामाया + अनुभावेन

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    ā + a: two like vowels merge into one long ā.

  • मन्वन्तराधिपः manvantarādhipaḥ → मनु + अन्तर + अधिपः

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (yaṇ and savarṇa-dīrgha) · इको यणचि (6.1.77); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    u before a vowel becomes v (मनु + अन्तर → मन्वन्तर); a + a → ā (अन्तर + अधिप → अन्तराधिप).

  • स बभूव sa babhūva → सः + बभूव

    visarga sandhi (special rule for सः) · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132)

    The visarga of सः (and एषः) is dropped before any consonant.

  • सावर्णिस्तनयो sāvarṇistanayo → सावर्णिः + तनयः

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s; then तनयः before the voiced r of रवेः becomes तनयो (हशि च, 6.1.114).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (its first member महामाया is itself a karmadhāraya: महती चासौ माया च)

    Members
    महामाया + अनुभाव
    Vigraha

    Literally

    In the verse

  • मन्वन्तराधिपः manvantarādhipaḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (मन्वन्तर = मनोः अन्तरम्, also ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa)

    Members

Morphology & anvaya

  • बभूव babhūva

    Perfect of √भू with the reduplicated syllable ब (bh → b). With a predicate nominative it means ‘became’: स … मन्वन्तराधिपः बभूव.

Anvaya · prose order

रवेः तनयः महाभागः सः सावर्णिः महामायानुभावेन यथा मन्वन्तराधिपः बभूव, (तत् शृणु)।

raveḥ tanayaḥ mahābhāgaḥ saḥ sāvarṇiḥ mahāmāyānubhāvena yathā manvantarādhipaḥ babhūva, (tat śṛṇu) |

A dependent clause of manner (यथा … बभूव) still governed by निशामय in 1.2: ‘(hear) how he became …’.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The cause of Sāvarṇi’s rise is stated at once: the power (अनुभाव) of Mahāmāyā. The story of Suratha that follows (1.4 onward) explains how.

Traditional interpretation

Mahāmāyā is the name under which the first carita knows the Goddess: the power that binds beings in attachment (1.55–58) and the power that releases them. The same name returns in Medhas’s teaching (1.55) and in Brahmā’s hymn.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also names her Mahāmāyā (name 215, महामाया). The shared name is a shared idea in Śākta thought; the two texts remain separate works.

Word by word

  1. स्वारोचिषेsvārociṣein the Svārociṣa (age)n. loc. sg. of स्वारोचिष (taddhita from स्वरोचिस्, the second Manu); qualifies अन्तरे
  2. अन्तरेantarein the interval, in the manvantaran. loc. sg. of अन्तर; here short for मन्वन्तरे
  3. पूर्वम्pūrvamformerly, long agoindeclinable (adverbial acc. of पूर्व)
  4. चैत्रवंशसमुद्भवःcaitravaṃśasamudbhavaḥborn in the line of Caitram. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies सुरथः
  5. सुरथःsurathaḥSuratham. nom. sg.; proper name; subject
  6. नामnāmaby name, namedindeclinable
  7. राजाrājāa kingm. nom. sg. of राजन्; predicate
  8. अभूत्abhūtwas√भू, luṅ (aorist), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  9. समस्तेsamasteover the wholen. loc. sg. of समस्त; qualifies क्षितिमण्डले
  10. क्षितिमण्डलेkṣitimaṇḍaleearth’s circle, the whole earthn. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)

Translation

Formerly, in the Svārociṣa interval, there was over the whole circle of the earth a king named Suratha, born in Caitra’s line.

In readable EnglishLong ago, in the age of Svārociṣa Manu, there lived a king named Suratha, of the line of Caitra, who ruled the whole earth.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • स्वारोचिषेऽन्तरे svārociṣe'ntare → स्वारोचिषे + अन्तरे

    vowel sandhi (pūrvarūpa) · एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -e + a- → -e’-: the initial a is elided (avagraha).

  • सुरथो नाम suratho nāma → सुरथः + नाम

    visarga sandhi · हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced n becomes -o.

  • राजाभूत् rājābhūt → राजा + अभूत्

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    ā + a → ā.

  • राजाभूत्समस्ते rājābhūtsamaste → राजा + अभूत् + समस्ते

    no change · खरि च (8.4.55)

    After राजा + अभूत् → राजाभूत्, the final t of अभूत् stays unvoiced before the unvoiced s; the words are only written together.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • चैत्रवंशसमुद्भवः caitravaṃśasamudbhavaḥ

    bahuvrīhi containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (चैत्रवंश)

    Members
    चैत्र + वंश + समुद्भव
    Vigraha
    चैत्रस्य वंशः चैत्रवंशः; चैत्रवंशे समुद्भवः यस्य सः caitrasya vaṃśaḥ caitravaṃśaḥ; caitravaṃśe samudbhavaḥ yasya saḥ
    Literally
    “whose birth is in Caitra’s line”
    In the verse
    a king of the Caitra dynasty
    Alternative
    Also read as a saptamī tatpuruṣa, चैत्रवंशे समुद्भवः, ‘one born in Caitra’s line’; the sense is the same.

  • क्षितिमण्डले kṣitimaṇḍale

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    क्षिति + मण्डल
    Vigraha
    क्षितेः मण्डलम्, तस्मिन् kṣiteḥ maṇḍalam, tasmin
    Literally
    “in the circle of the earth”
    In the verse
    over the whole earth
Morphology & anvaya

  • अभूत् abhūt

    Root aorist of √भू with augment a-: ‘was, came to be’. Used alongside the perfect for narrative past.

  • स्वारोचिषे svārociṣe

    Taddhita derivative: स्वारोचिष ‘belonging to Svarocis’, i.e. the age of the second Manu, Svārociṣa.

Anvaya · prose order

पूर्वं स्वारोचिषे अन्तरे चैत्रवंशसमुद्भवः सुरथः नाम राजा समस्ते क्षितिमण्डले अभूत्।

pūrvaṃ svārociṣe antare caitravaṃśasamudbhavaḥ surathaḥ nāma rājā samaste kṣitimaṇḍale abhūt |

Time (पूर्वं स्वारोचिषे अन्तरे), subject with its epithet (चैत्रवंशसमुद्भवः सुरथः नाम राजा), place (समस्ते क्षितिमण्डले), verb (अभूत्).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Suratha is introduced: a universal king of an earlier age. The story will take everything from him, in order (1.5–9).

Traditional interpretation

Suratha is the king who, at the end of the text, receives his kingdom back and is promised birth as Sāvarṇi (13.25–29). His companion, the merchant Samādhi, will ask for knowledge instead. The tradition reads the pair as the two goals the Goddess grants: enjoyment (bhoga) and liberation (mokṣa).

Verse 1.5

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

तस्य पालयतः सम्यक् प्रजाः पुत्रानिवौरसान्।बभूवुः शत्रवो भूपाः कोलाविध्वंसिनस्तदा॥⁠५⁠॥

tasya pālayataḥ samyak prajāḥ putrānivaurasān |babhūvuḥ śatravo bhūpāḥ kolāvidhvaṃsinastadā ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

तस्य · पालयतः · सम्यक् · प्रजाः · पुत्रान् · इव · औरसान्बभूवुः · शत्रवः · भूपाः · कोलाविध्वंसिनः · तदा

tasya · pālayataḥ · samyak · prajāḥ · putrān · iva · aurasānbabhūvuḥ · śatravaḥ · bhūpāḥ · kolāvidhvaṃsinaḥ · tadā

Word by word

  1. तस्यtasyaof him (Suratha)pronoun तद्, m. gen. sg.; with पालयतः
  2. पालयतःpālayataḥprotecting, while (he) was rulingpresent participle (śatṛ) of √पाल् (curādi, 10, stem पालय- ‘to protect’), m. gen. sg.; agrees with तस्य
  3. सम्यक्samyakrightly, wellindeclinable (adverb of manner)
  4. प्रजाःprajāḥthe subjects, his peoplef. acc. pl. of प्रजा; object of पालयतः
  5. पुत्रान्putrānsonsm. acc. pl. of पुत्र; the standard of comparison
  6. इवivalike, asindeclinable (particle of comparison)
  7. औरसान्aurasānhis own (lit. ‘born of the breast’, legitimate)m. acc. pl. of औरस (taddhita from उरस् ‘breast’); qualifies पुत्रान्
  8. बभूवुःbabhūvuḥbecame, arose (as)√भू (bhvādi, 1P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana
  9. शत्रवःśatravaḥenemiesm. nom. pl. of शत्रु (u-stem); predicate with बभूवुः
  10. भूपाःbhūpāḥkings (lit. ‘protectors of the earth’)m. nom. pl. of भूप (upapada compound भू + प); subject
  11. कोलाविध्वंसिनःkolāvidhvaṃsinaḥthe Kolāvidhvaṃsins, lit. ‘destroyers of Kolā’m. nom. pl. of कोलाविध्वंसिन्; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies भूपाः
  12. तदाtadāthen, at that timeindeclinable (adverb of time)

Translation

Of him, as he protected his subjects rightly like his own sons, the kings, the Kolāvidhvaṃsins, then became enemies.

In readable EnglishWhile he ruled his people justly, as though they were his own children, the kings called the Kolāvidhvaṃsins rose against him as enemies.

‘Rose against him’ renders बभूवुः शत्रवः (‘became enemies’) with the genitive तस्य.

Textual verification / uncertain: कोलाविध्वंसिनः: whether a proper name of a people or dynasty or a description (‘destroyers of Kolā’), and what Kolā refers to (a city is often assumed), cannot be settled from the text.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • पुत्रानिवौरसान् putrānivaurasān → पुत्रान् + इव + औरसान्

    vowel sandhi (vṛddhi) · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88)

    a + au → au: इव and औरसान् fuse into इवौरसान्. The final n of पुत्रान् is unchanged before the vowel; the three words are only written together.

  • शत्रवो भूपाः śatravo bhūpāḥ → शत्रवः + भूपाः

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before a voiced consonant (bh) becomes -o.

  • कोलाविध्वंसिनस्तदा kolāvidhvaṃsinastadā → कोलाविध्वंसिनः + तदा

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • कोलाविध्वंसिनः kolāvidhvaṃsinaḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (the genitive of the object with an agent noun in -in)

    Members
    कोला + विध्वंसिन्
    Vigraha
    कोलायाः विध्वंसिनः kolāyāḥ vidhvaṃsinaḥ
    Literally
    “destroyers of Kolā”
    In the verse
    a group of kings so called; most translators keep it as a name
    Alternative
    It may be a proper name of a people or dynasty (the Kolāvidhvaṃsins) rather than a description. The text uses it again in 1.6 as if a known name, which favours the name; the analysis of the compound is the same either way.

  • भूपाः bhūpāḥ

    upapada tatpuruṣa

    Members
    भू + प
    Vigraha
    भुवं पान्ति इति भूपाः bhuvaṃ pānti iti bhūpāḥ
    Literally
    “earth-protectors”
    In the verse
    kings
Morphology & anvaya

  • पालयतः pālayataḥ

    Present participle of the curādi stem पालय- (+ śatṛ → पालयत्), genitive singular. With तस्य it gives the circumstance: ‘while he was ruling’. The genitive can be read simply as possessive (‘his enemies’) or as the genitive absolute of disregard (‘though he ruled well, kings became his enemies’); the narrative supports both.

  • बभूवुः babhūvuḥ

    Perfect of √भू, third person plural (-उः). With a predicate nominative, ‘became’: भूपाः शत्रवः बभूवुः ‘kings became (his) enemies’.

  • औरसान् aurasān

    Taddhita in -a with vṛddhi of the first syllable: उरस् ‘breast’ → औरस ‘born of the breast’, i.e. a son of one’s own body, as opposed to an adopted son.

Anvaya · prose order

प्रजाः औरसान् पुत्रान् इव सम्यक् पालयतः तस्य तदा कोलाविध्वंसिनः भूपाः शत्रवः बभूवुः।

prajāḥ aurasān putrān iva samyak pālayataḥ tasya tadā kolāvidhvaṃsinaḥ bhūpāḥ śatravaḥ babhūvuḥ |

The genitive phrase (तस्य पालयतः …) frames the clause; the subject is भूपाः with its epithet कोलाविध्वंसिनः, शत्रवः is the predicate, बभूवुः the verb.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The first loss begins. Suratha is a good king — he rules his subjects ‘like his own sons’ — and still enemies arise. The text gives no fault on his side as the cause.

Traditional interpretation

Ruling one’s people as one’s own children is the classical ideal of kingship in the epics and Purāṇas; the verse states it in a single simile and moves on.

Verse 1.6

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

तस्य तैरभवद् युद्धमतिप्रबलदण्डिनः।न्यूनैरपि स तैर्युद्धे कोलाविध्वंसिभिर्जितः॥⁠६⁠॥

tasya tairabhavad yuddhamatiprabaladaṇḍinaḥ |nyūnairapi sa tairyuddhe kolāvidhvaṃsibhirjitaḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

तस्य · तैः · अभवत् · युद्धम् · अतिप्रबलदण्डिनःन्यूनैः · अपि · सः · तैः · युद्धे · कोलाविध्वंसिभिः · जितः

tasya · taiḥ · abhavat · yuddham · atiprabaladaṇḍinaḥnyūnaiḥ · api · saḥ · taiḥ · yuddhe · kolāvidhvaṃsibhiḥ · jitaḥ

Word by word

  1. तस्यtasyahis (Suratha’s)pronoun तद्, m. gen. sg.; with अतिप्रबलदण्डिनः
  2. तैःtaiḥwith thempronoun तद्, m. instr. pl. (instrumental of association: ‘a battle with them’)
  3. अभवत्abhavatthere was, took place√भू (bhvādi, 1P), laṅ (imperfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  4. युद्धम्yuddhama battlen. nom. sg. of युद्ध; subject of अभवत्
  5. अतिप्रबलदण्डिनःatiprabaladaṇḍinaḥwho wielded a very mighty force (daṇḍa: the rod of rule, an army)m. gen. sg. of अतिप्रबलदण्डिन्; compound (see Samāsa); agrees with तस्य
  6. न्यूनैःnyūnaiḥinferior (in strength)m. instr. pl. of न्यून; qualifies तैः … कोलाविध्वंसिभिः
  7. अपिapieven, thoughindeclinable (particle: concessive ‘even’)
  8. सःsaḥhepronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; subject of जितः
  9. तैःtaiḥby thempronoun तद्, m. instr. pl.; agent
  10. युद्धेyuddhein battlen. loc. sg. of युद्ध
  11. कोलाविध्वंसिभिःkolāvidhvaṃsibhiḥby the Kolāvidhvaṃsinsm. instr. pl. of कोलाविध्वंसिन्; compound (as in 1.5); agent of जितः
  12. जितःjitaḥwas defeatedpast passive participle (kta) of √जि (bhvādi, 1P ‘to conquer’), m. nom. sg.; used as the finite verb

Translation

A battle took place between him, who had a very strong force, and them; even though they were weaker, he was defeated in battle by those Kolāvidhvaṃsins.

In readable EnglishWar broke out between them and the king, mighty as his forces were; and though they were the weaker side, the Kolāvidhvaṃsins defeated him in battle.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तैरभवद् tairabhavad → तैः + अभवत्

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    After a vowel other than a/ā (here ai), the visarga stands as r before a vowel or voiced consonant. The same gives न्यूनैरपि, तैर्युद्धे and कोलाविध्वंसिभिर्जितः.

  • अभवद् युद्धम् abhavad yuddham → अभवत् + युद्धम्

    consonant sandhi (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    Final t becomes d before the voiced y; the Gita Press writes the d with virāma and a space.

  • स तैर्युद्धे sa tairyuddhe → सः + तैः + युद्धे

    visarga sandhi (special rule for सः) · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132)

    The visarga of सः is dropped before the consonant t.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अतिप्रबलदण्डिनः atiprabaladaṇḍinaḥ

    karmadhāraya (अतिप्रबलदण्ड) with the possessive taddhita -in; अतिप्रबल is itself a prādi tatpuruṣa (अतिशयेन प्रबलः)

    Members
    अतिप्रबल + दण्ड + -इन्
    Vigraha
    अतिप्रबलः दण्डः अतिप्रबलदण्डः; सः अस्य अस्ति इति अतिप्रबलदण्डी, तस्य atiprabalaḥ daṇḍaḥ atiprabaladaṇḍaḥ; saḥ asya asti iti atiprabaladaṇḍī, tasya
    Literally
    “possessing an exceedingly strong rod”
    In the verse
    a king whose army and power of punishment were very great
    Alternative
    दण्ड can mean the army or the king’s power to punish (daṇḍanīti); both fit, and the contrast with न्यूनैः (‘weaker’) favours military strength.
Morphology & anvaya

  • जितः jitaḥ

    Past passive participle of √जि with the auxiliary ‘was’ understood: सः … जितः ‘he (was) defeated’. The agent is in the instrumental (कोलाविध्वंसिभिः).

  • अभवत् abhavat

    Imperfect of √भू with augment a-: ‘(a battle) took place’. The narrative moves between imperfect, aorist and perfect without difference of sense.

Anvaya · prose order

अतिप्रबलदण्डिनः तस्य तैः युद्धम् अभवत्। न्यूनैः अपि तैः कोलाविध्वंसिभिः सः युद्धे जितः।

atiprabaladaṇḍinaḥ tasya taiḥ yuddham abhavat | nyūnaiḥ api taiḥ kolāvidhvaṃsibhiḥ saḥ yuddhe jitaḥ |

Two sentences: a battle took place (युद्धम् अभवत्); he was defeated (सः जितः), with the agent and its concessive qualifier न्यूनैः अपि.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The paradox is in अपि: the strong king loses to the weaker side. The verse does not explain it; the following verses show his own ministers turning against him.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: strength on paper does not decide the outcome. The story strips Suratha of power that was never as secure as it looked.

Verse 1.7

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

ततः स्वपुरमायातो निजदेशाधिपोऽभवत्।आक्रान्तः स महाभागस्तैस्तदा प्रबलारिभिः॥⁠७⁠॥

tataḥ svapuramāyāto nijadeśādhipo'bhavat |ākrāntaḥ sa mahābhāgastaistadā prabalāribhiḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

ततः · स्वपुरम् · आयातः · निजदेशाधिपः · अभवत्आक्रान्तः · सः · महाभागः · तैः · तदा · प्रबलारिभिः

tataḥ · svapuram · āyātaḥ · nijadeśādhipaḥ · abhavatākrāntaḥ · saḥ · mahābhāgaḥ · taiḥ · tadā · prabalāribhiḥ

Word by word

  1. ततःtataḥthen, thereuponindeclinable (adverb, from तद् + tasil)
  2. स्वपुरम्svapuramto his own cityn. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); goal of आयातः
  3. आयातःāyātaḥhaving come (back)past participle (kta) of आ + √या (adādi, 2P ‘to go’; with आ ‘to come’), m. nom. sg.; active sense
  4. निजदेशाधिपःnijadeśādhipaḥthe ruler of his own country (only)m. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate with अभवत्
  5. अभवत्abhavatbecame, was√भू (bhvādi, 1P), laṅ (imperfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  6. आक्रान्तःākrāntaḥwas attacked, overrunpast passive participle (kta) of आ + √क्रम् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to step’), m. nom. sg.; used as the finite verb
  7. सःsaḥhepronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.
  8. महाभागःmahābhāgaḥthe illustrious (king)m. nom. sg.; compound (bahuvrīhi, as in 1.3); qualifies सः
  9. तैःtaiḥby thempronoun तद्, m. instr. pl.; agent
  10. तदाtadāthen, at that timeindeclinable (adverb of time)
  11. प्रबलारिभिःprabalāribhiḥby powerful enemiesm. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to तैः

Translation

Then, having come to his own city, he became ruler of his own country; then that illustrious one was attacked by them, the powerful enemies.

In readable EnglishThen he withdrew to his own city and ruled only his own land; and even there that noble king was assailed by those enemies, now grown strong.

‘Only’ and ‘even there’ make explicit the contrast with 1.4 (‘over the whole earth’), which the compound निजदेशाधिपः implies.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • आयातो निज āyāto nija → आयातः + निजदेशाधिपः

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced n becomes -o.

  • निजदेशाधिपोऽभवत् nijadeśādhipo'bhavat → निजदेशाधिपः + अभवत्

    visarga sandhi, then pūrvarūpa · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a- becomes -o, and the following a is absorbed (avagraha). Inside the compound, देश + अधिप → देशाधिप by अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101).

  • आक्रान्तः स महाभागस्तैस्तदा ākrāntaḥ sa mahābhāgastaistadā → आक्रान्तः + सः + महाभागः + तैः + तदा

    visarga sandhi · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132); विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    सः loses its visarga before m; महाभागः and तैः each turn their visarga to s before t.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • स्वपुरम् svapuram

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    स्व + पुर
    Vigraha
    स्वस्य पुरम् svasya puram
    Literally
    “the city of oneself”
    In the verse
    his own capital
    Alternative
    Also analysed as a karmadhāraya, स्वं च तत् पुरं च, ‘his own city’; the sense is the same.

  • निजदेशाधिपः nijadeśādhipaḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa containing a karmadhāraya

    Members
    निजदेश + अधिप
    Vigraha
    निजः देशः निजदेशः (karmadhāraya); निजदेशस्य अधिपः nijaḥ deśaḥ nijadeśaḥ (karmadhāraya); nijadeśasya adhipaḥ
    Literally
    “overlord of his own country”
    In the verse
    the universal king of 1.4 is now master only of his home territory

  • प्रबलारिभिः prabalāribhiḥ

    karmadhāraya

    Members
    प्रबल + अरि
    Vigraha
    प्रबलाः अरयः, तैः prabalāḥ arayaḥ, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by strong enemies”
    In the verse
    by enemies now grown powerful
Morphology & anvaya

  • आयातः āyātaḥ

    With verbs of motion the kta participle is active: आयातः ‘(he) having come’, not ‘having been reached’. Its goal stands in the accusative (स्वपुरम्).

  • आक्रान्तः ākrāntaḥ

    Here the kta is passive, with the agent in the instrumental (तैः … प्रबलारिभिः): ‘he was overrun by them’.

Anvaya · prose order

ततः स्वपुरम् आयातः (सः) निजदेशाधिपः अभवत्। तदा सः महाभागः तैः प्रबलारिभिः आक्रान्तः।

tataḥ svapuram āyātaḥ (saḥ) nijadeśādhipaḥ abhavat | tadā saḥ mahābhāgaḥ taiḥ prabalāribhiḥ ākrāntaḥ |

First sentence: participle + predicate nominative + verb. Second: passive participle as verb with an instrumental agent.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The second loss: the emperor of 1.4 is reduced to his home territory, and the enemies follow him there.

Traditional interpretation

The steps of Suratha’s fall — empire, country, city, treasury, army — are told in order, so that by 1.9 nothing royal is left to him but the name महाभाग.

Verse 1.8

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

अमात्यैर्बलिभिर्दुष्टैर्दुर्बलस्य दुरात्मभिः।कोशो बलं चापहृतं तत्रापि स्वपुरे ततः॥⁠८⁠॥

amātyairbalibhirduṣṭairdurbalasya durātmabhiḥ |kośo balaṃ cāpahṛtaṃ tatrāpi svapure tataḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

अमात्यैः · बलिभिः · दुष्टैः · दुर्बलस्य · दुरात्मभिःकोशः · बलम् · च · अपहृतम् · तत्र · अपि · स्वपुरे · ततः

amātyaiḥ · balibhiḥ · duṣṭaiḥ · durbalasya · durātmabhiḥkośaḥ · balam · ca · apahṛtam · tatra · api · svapure · tataḥ

Word by word

  1. अमात्यैःamātyaiḥby (his) ministersm. instr. pl. of अमात्य; agent of अपहृतम्
  2. बलिभिःbalibhiḥpowerfulm. instr. pl. of बलिन् (‘possessing strength’); qualifies अमात्यैः
  3. दुष्टैःduṣṭaiḥcorrupt, wickedpast participle (kta) of √दुष् (divādi, 4P ‘to be spoiled’), used as an adjective, m. instr. pl.; qualifies अमात्यैः
  4. दुर्बलस्यdurbalasyaof the weakened (king)m. gen. sg. of दुर्बल; compound (see Samāsa); possessor of कोशः and बलम्
  5. दुरात्मभिःdurātmabhiḥevil-mindedm. instr. pl. of दुरात्मन्; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies अमात्यैः
  6. कोशःkośaḥthe treasurym. nom. sg. of कोश; subject
  7. बलम्balamthe armyn. nom. sg. of बल; subject
  8. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  9. अपहृतम्apahṛtamwas carried off, seizedpast passive participle (kta) of अप + √हृ (bhvādi, 1U ‘to take’), n. nom. sg.; used as the finite verb
  10. तत्रtatrathereindeclinable (adverb of place)
  11. अपिapievenindeclinable (particle)
  12. स्वपुरेsvapurein his own cityn. loc. sg.; compound (as in 1.7); in apposition to तत्र
  13. ततःtataḥthen, after thatindeclinable (adverb)

Translation

Then, even there in his own city, the treasury and the army of the weakened one were carried off by his powerful, corrupt, evil-minded ministers.

In readable EnglishThen, in his own city too, his powerful ministers — corrupt and wicked men — seized the weakened king’s treasury and army.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • अमात्यैर्बलिभिर्दुष्टैर्दुर्बलस्य amātyairbalibhirduṣṭairdurbalasya → अमात्यैः + बलिभिः + दुष्टैः + दुर्बलस्य

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    After ai and i the visarga stands as r before the voiced b and d: three junctions in a row, which give the line its rolling sound.

  • कोशो बलं kośo balaṃ → कोशः + बलम्

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced b becomes -o.

  • चापहृतं cāpahṛtaṃ → च + अपहृतम्

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + a → ā. The final m of अपहृतम् becomes anusvāra before t (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

  • तत्रापि tatrāpi → तत्र + अपि

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + a → ā.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • दुर्बलस्य durbalasya

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    दुस् + बल
    Vigraha
    दुष्टं (अल्पं) बलं यस्य सः, तस्य duṣṭaṃ (alpaṃ) balaṃ yasya saḥ, tasya
    Literally
    “of one whose strength is poor”
    In the verse
    of the king, now weak

  • दुरात्मभिः durātmabhiḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    दुस् + आत्मन्
    Vigraha
    दुष्टः आत्मा येषां ते, तैः duṣṭaḥ ātmā yeṣāṃ te, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by those whose selves are bad”
    In the verse
    by the wicked-hearted ministers
Morphology & anvaya

  • अपहृतम् apahṛtam

    Passive participle as verb, neuter singular although it has a masculine (कोशः) and a neuter (बलम्) subject: it agrees with the nearer one, बलम्, or takes the neuter for a mixed pair. ‘The treasury and the army were seized.’

  • बलिभिः balibhiḥ

    Instrumental plural of बलिन्, an -in stem (बल + possessive -in): ‘having strength’. Contrast दुर्बलस्य in the same line: the ministers are strong, the king weak.

Anvaya · prose order

ततः तत्र स्वपुरे अपि बलिभिः दुष्टैः दुरात्मभिः अमात्यैः दुर्बलस्य (तस्य) कोशः बलं च अपहृतम्।

tataḥ tatra svapure api balibhiḥ duṣṭaiḥ durātmabhiḥ amātyaiḥ durbalasya (tasya) kośaḥ balaṃ ca apahṛtam |

The passive participle अपहृतम् is the verb; its subjects are कोशः बलं च, its agent the ministers with three adjectives, and दुर्बलस्य names whose treasury.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The third loss comes from inside: his own ministers take the treasury (कोश) and the army (बल), the two supports of kingship. The king is now called दुर्बल ‘weak’, the ministers बलिन् ‘strong’.

Traditional interpretation

Treasury and army are two of the classical ‘limbs’ of the state (rājyāṅga); Suratha will speak of his attachment to the limbs of his kingdom in 1.41.

Verse 1.9

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

ततो मृगयाव्याजेन हृतस्वाम्यः स भूपतिः।एकाकी हयमारुह्य जगाम गहनं वनम्॥⁠९⁠॥

tato mṛgayāvyājena hṛtasvāmyaḥ sa bhūpatiḥ |ekākī hayamāruhya jagāma gahanaṃ vanam ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

ततः · मृगयाव्याजेन · हृतस्वाम्यः · सः · भूपतिःएकाकी · हयम् · आरुह्य · जगाम · गहनम् · वनम्

tataḥ · mṛgayāvyājena · hṛtasvāmyaḥ · saḥ · bhūpatiḥekākī · hayam · āruhya · jagāma · gahanam · vanam

Word by word

  1. ततःtataḥthenindeclinable (adverb)
  2. मृगयाव्याजेनmṛgayāvyājenaunder the pretext of huntingm. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); instrumental of manner
  3. हृतस्वाम्यःhṛtasvāmyaḥrobbed of his sovereigntym. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies भूपतिः
  4. सःsaḥthatpronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; with भूपतिः
  5. भूपतिःbhūpatiḥking (lit. ‘lord of the earth’)m. nom. sg. of भूपति; subject
  6. एकाकीekākīalonem. nom. sg. of एकाकिन्; predicative adjective
  7. हयम्hayama horsem. acc. sg. of हय; object of आरुह्य
  8. आरुह्यāruhyahaving mountedabsolutive (lyap) of आ + √रुह् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to climb’)
  9. जगामjagāmawent√गम् (bhvādi, 1P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  10. गहनम्gahanamdense, deepn. acc. sg. of गहन; qualifies वनम्
  11. वनम्vanamforestn. acc. sg. of वन; goal of जगाम

Translation

Then that king, robbed of his sovereignty, on the pretext of hunting, alone, having mounted a horse, went to a dense forest.

In readable EnglishStripped of his kingdom, the king rode out alone on horseback under the pretext of a hunt, and went into a deep forest.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • ततो मृगया tato mṛgayā → ततः + मृगयाव्याजेन

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced m becomes -o.

  • स भूपतिः sa bhūpatiḥ → सः + भूपतिः

    visarga sandhi (special rule for सः) · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132)

    The visarga of सः is dropped before a consonant.

  • गहनं वनम् gahanaṃ vanam → गहनम् + वनम्

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • मृगयाव्याजेन mṛgayāvyājena

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    मृगया + व्याज
    Vigraha
    मृगयायाः व्याजः, तेन mṛgayāyāḥ vyājaḥ, tena
    Literally
    “by the pretext of the hunt”
    In the verse
    on the excuse of going hunting

  • हृतस्वाम्यः hṛtasvāmyaḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    हृत + स्वाम्य
    Vigraha
    हृतं स्वाम्यं यस्य सः hṛtaṃ svāmyaṃ yasya saḥ
    Literally
    “one whose lordship has been taken”
    In the verse
    the dispossessed king

  • भूपतिः bhūpatiḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    भू + पति
    Vigraha
    भुवः पतिः bhuvaḥ patiḥ
    Literally
    “lord of the earth”
    In the verse
    king — said with irony of a king who has lost his land
Morphology & anvaya

  • आरुह्य āruhya

    Absolutive with a prefix, so -य (lyap) instead of -त्वा: आ + √रुह् + ल्यप् → आरुह्य ‘having mounted’. Its subject is the subject of the main verb जगाम.

  • एकाकी ekākī

    Nominative singular of एकाकिन् ‘solitary’ (एक + -आकिन्); n-stems in -in lose the n in the nominative and lengthen the i.

  • जगाम jagāma

    Perfect of √गम्, with reduplication ज- (g → j) and vṛddhi of the root vowel in the third singular.

Anvaya · prose order

ततः हृतस्वाम्यः सः भूपतिः मृगयाव्याजेन एकाकी हयम् आरुह्य गहनं वनं जगाम।

tataḥ hṛtasvāmyaḥ saḥ bhūpatiḥ mṛgayāvyājena ekākī hayam āruhya gahanaṃ vanaṃ jagāma |

Subject with its bahuvrīhi epithet, the manner (मृगयाव्याजेन, एकाकी), the absolutive with its object, then the main verb with its goal.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The last step: the king leaves alone, keeping up appearances (‘as if to hunt’). The forest is where the story can turn.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the pretext matters. Even in defeat Suratha is guarding how he is seen — the attachment to position that he will confess in 1.12–16.

Verse 1.10

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

saḥ · tatra · āśramam · adrākṣīt · dvijavaryasya · medhasaḥpraśāntaśvāpadākīrṇam · muniśiṣyopaśobhitam

Word by word

  1. सःsaḥhe (the king)pronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; subject
  2. तत्रtatrathere (in the forest)indeclinable (adverb of place)
  3. आश्रमम्āśramama hermitagem. acc. sg. of आश्रम; object of अद्राक्षीत्
  4. अद्राक्षीत्adrākṣītsaw√दृश् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to see’), luṅ (s-aorist), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada

There he saw the hermitage of Medhas, best of the twice-born, filled with beasts of prey grown peaceful and graced by the sage’s disciples.

In readable EnglishThere he came upon the hermitage of Medhas, foremost of brahmins — a place where even the wild beasts had grown gentle, graced by the sage’s disciples.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • स तत्राश्रमम् sa tatrāśramam → सः + तत्र + आश्रमम्

    visarga sandhi (सः) and vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    सः drops its visarga before t; तत्र + आश्रमम्: a + ā → ā.

  • अद्राक्षीद् द्विज adrākṣīd dvija → अद्राक्षीत् + द्विजवर्यस्य

    consonant sandhi (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    Final t becomes d before the voiced d; printed with virāma and a space.

  • श्वापदाकीर्णं śvāpadākīrṇaṃ → श्वापद + आकीर्णम्

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + ā → ā. The final m becomes anusvāra before the m of मुनि- (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

  • शिष्योपशोभितम् śiṣyopaśobhitam → शिष्य + उपशोभितम्

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + u → o.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • द्विजवर्यस्य dvijavaryasya

    saptamī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    द्विज + वर्य
    Vigraha
    द्विजेषु वर्यः, तस्य dvijeṣu varyaḥ, tasya
    Literally
    “of the choicest among the twice-born”
    In the verse
    of that eminent brahmin
    Alternative
    Equally read as ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa द्विजानां वर्यः; the sense is the same.

  • प्रशान्तश्वापदाकीर्णम् praśāntaśvāpadākīrṇam

    tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a karmadhāraya

    Members
    प्रशान्तश्वापद + आकीर्ण
    Vigraha
    प्रशान्ताः श्वापदाः प्रशान्तश्वापदाः (karmadhāraya); प्रशान्तश्वापदैः आकीर्णम् praśāntāḥ śvāpadāḥ praśāntaśvāpadāḥ (karmadhāraya); praśāntaśvāpadaiḥ ākīrṇam
    Literally
    “strewn with calmed beasts of prey”
    In the verse
    a hermitage where even predators had become peaceful

  • मुनिशिष्योपशोभितम् muniśiṣyopaśobhitam

    tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    मुनिशिष्य + उपशोभित
    Vigraha
    मुनेः शिष्याः मुनिशिष्याः (ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa); मुनिशिष्यैः उपशोभितम् muneḥ śiṣyāḥ muniśiṣyāḥ (ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa); muniśiṣyaiḥ upaśobhitam
    Literally
    “adorned by the sage’s pupils”
    In the verse
    made beautiful by the presence of Medhas’s disciples
    Alternative
    मुनिशिष्य can also be a dvandva, मुनयश्च शिष्याश्च ‘sages and disciples’; the singular sage of the verse (द्विजवर्यस्य मेधसः) favours ‘the sage’s disciples’.
Morphology & anvaya

  • अद्राक्षीत् adrākṣīt

    s-aorist of √दृश्: augment अ-; the root takes an inserted a (दृश् → द्रश्), lengthened in this aorist (द्राश्); ś becomes k before the aorist s, which turns to ṣ (द्राक्ष्); ending -ईत्. The present uses the suppletive stem पश्य-; the aorist is built on the root itself.

  • मेधसः medhasaḥ

    Genitive singular of the s-stem मेधस्; the same form could be nominative/accusative plural of a different stem, but the sense here is ‘of Medhas’. The name means ‘intelligence, wisdom’.

Anvaya · prose order

सः तत्र द्विजवर्यस्य मेधसः प्रशान्तश्वापदाकीर्णं मुनिशिष्योपशोभितम् आश्रमम् अद्राक्षीत्।

saḥ tatra dvijavaryasya medhasaḥ praśāntaśvāpadākīrṇaṃ muniśiṣyopaśobhitam āśramam adrākṣīt |

Subject, place, the owner of the hermitage (genitive), two compound adjectives of the object, the object, and the verb.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The turning point of the frame story. In the forest the king finds Medhas, who will become his teacher; the rest of the Devī Māhātmya is Medhas’s answer to his question (1.40 onward).

Traditional interpretation

Predators living peacefully around a sage is a common sign, in epic and Purāṇic description, of the power of an ascetic’s calm. The setting shows what Suratha does not yet have.

Verse 1.11

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

तस्थौ कंचित्स कालं च मुनिना तेन सत्कृतः।इतश्चेतश्च विचरंस्तस्मिन्मुनिवराश्रमे॥⁠११⁠॥

tasthau kaṃcitsa kālaṃ ca muninā tena satkṛtaḥ |itaścetaśca vicaraṃstasminmunivarāśrame ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

तस्थौ · कंचित् · सः · कालम् · च · मुनिना · तेन · सत्कृतःइतः · च · इतः · च · विचरन् · तस्मिन् · मुनिवराश्रमे

tasthau · kaṃcit · saḥ · kālam · ca · muninā · tena · satkṛtaḥitaḥ · ca · itaḥ · ca · vicaran · tasmin · munivarāśrame

Word by word

  1. तस्थौtasthaustayed√स्था (bhvādi, 1P ‘to stand, stay’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  2. कंचित्kaṃcitsomeindefinite pronoun किम् + चित्, m. acc. sg.; qualifies कालम्
  3. सःsaḥhepronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; subject
  4. कालम्kālamtimem. acc. sg. of काल; accusative of duration
  5. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  6. मुनिनाmunināby the sagem. instr. sg. of मुनि; agent of सत्कृतः
  7. तेनtenaby that (sage)pronoun तद्, m. instr. sg.; with मुनिना
  8. सत्कृतःsatkṛtaḥhonoured, received with hospitalitypast passive participle (kta) of सत् + √कृ (tanādi, 8U), m. nom. sg.; qualifies सः
  9. इतःitaḥhere (lit. ‘from here’)indeclinable (adverb, इदम् + tasil)
  10. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  11. इतःitaḥthere (lit. ‘from here’)indeclinable (adverb)
  12. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction); इतश्चेतश्च ‘hither and thither’
  13. विचरन्vicaranwandering aboutpresent participle (śatṛ) of वि + √चर् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to move’), m. nom. sg.; qualifies सः
  14. तस्मिन्tasminin thatpronoun तद्, m. loc. sg.; with मुनिवराश्रमे
  15. मुनिवराश्रमेmunivarāśramein the hermitage of the excellent sagem. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)

Translation

And he stayed for some time, honoured by that sage, wandering here and there in that hermitage of the excellent sage.

In readable EnglishWelcomed with honour by the sage, he stayed there for a while, wandering here and there about the great sage’s hermitage.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • कंचित्स कालं kaṃcitsa kālaṃ → कंचित् + सः + कालम्

    visarga sandhi (सः); no change of t · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132); खरि च (8.4.55)

    सः loses its visarga before k. The t of कंचित् stays unvoiced before the unvoiced s; the words are only written together.

  • इतश्चेतश्च itaścetaśca → इतः + च + इतः + च

    visarga sandhi and vowel sandhi (guṇa) · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40); आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    Visarga before c becomes s, then palatal ś next to c; च + इतः → चेतः (a + i → e).

  • विचरंस्तस्मिन् vicaraṃstasmin → विचरन् + तस्मिन्

    consonant sandhi (n before t) · नश्छव्यप्रशान् (8.3.7)

    Final n before t becomes ṃs: विचरन् → विचरंस्.

  • मुनिवराश्रमे munivarāśrame → मुनिवर + आश्रमे

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + ā → ā.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • मुनिवराश्रमे munivarāśrame

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa containing a saptamī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    मुनिवर + आश्रम
    Vigraha
    मुनिषु वरः मुनिवरः (saptamī tatpuruṣa); मुनिवरस्य आश्रमः, तस्मिन् muniṣu varaḥ munivaraḥ (saptamī tatpuruṣa); munivarasya āśramaḥ, tasmin
    Literally
    “in the hermitage of the best among sages”
    In the verse
    in Medhas’s hermitage
Morphology & anvaya

  • तस्थौ tasthau

    Perfect of √स्था: reduplication त- (the s of the cluster is dropped, the stop kept and deaspirated) and the ending -औ of ā-roots in the first and third singular.

  • कंचित् kaṃcit

    Accusative of the interrogative किम् with the indefinite particle -चित्: कम् + चित् ‘some (one)’. With कालम् it is an accusative of duration: ‘for some time’.

  • विचरन् vicaran

    Present participle of वि + √चर्, nominative singular masculine (stem विचरत्): ‘while wandering’, simultaneous with तस्थौ.

Anvaya · prose order

तेन मुनिना सत्कृतः सः तस्मिन् मुनिवराश्रमे इतः च इतः च विचरन् कंचित् कालं तस्थौ च।

tena muninā satkṛtaḥ saḥ tasmin munivarāśrame itaḥ ca itaḥ ca vicaran kaṃcit kālaṃ tasthau ca |

Main verb तस्थौ with an accusative of time; the participles सत्कृतः and विचरन् describe the subject. च joins this to the previous verse’s action.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Suratha is received as a guest and stays. He has not yet asked anything; his wandering ‘here and there’ prepares the restless thoughts of the next verses.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the body is at rest in a peaceful place, the mind is not. Outer refuge does not by itself settle inner turmoil.

Verse 1.12

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

सोऽचिन्तयत्तदा तत्र ममत्वाकृष्टचेतनः।मत्पूर्वैः पालितं पूर्वं मया हीनं पुरं हि तत् ॥⁠१२⁠॥

so'cintayattadā tatra mamatvākṛṣṭacetanaḥ |matpūrvaiḥ pālitaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā hīnaṃ puraṃ hi tat ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

सः · अचिन्तयत् · तदा · तत्र · ममत्वाकृष्टचेतनःमत्पूर्वैः · पालितम् · पूर्वम् · मया · हीनम् · पुरम् · हि · तत्

saḥ · acintayat · tadā · tatra · mamatvākṛṣṭacetanaḥmatpūrvaiḥ · pālitam · pūrvam · mayā · hīnam · puram · hi · tat

Word by word

  1. सःsaḥhepronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; subject
  2. अचिन्तयत्acintayatthought, reflected√चिन्त् (curādi, 10P ‘to think’), laṅ (imperfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  3. तदाtadāthenindeclinable (adverb of time)
  4. तत्रtatrathereindeclinable (adverb of place)
  5. ममत्वाकृष्टचेतनःmamatvākṛṣṭacetanaḥhis mind drawn away by the sense of ‘mine’m. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies सः
  6. मत्पूर्वैःmatpūrvaiḥby my forefathersm. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); agent of पालितम्
  7. पालितम्pālitamprotected, ruledpast passive participle (kta) of √पाल् (curādi, 10 ‘to protect’), n. nom. sg.; qualifies पुरम्
  8. पूर्वम्pūrvamformerlyindeclinable (adverbial acc. of पूर्व)
  9. मयाmayāof me (lit. ‘by me’)first-person pronoun अस्मद्, instr. sg.; with हीनम् (instrumental of separation)
  10. हीनम्hīnambereft, deprived (of me)past participle (kta) of √हा (juhotyādi, 3P ‘to leave’), n. nom. sg.; qualifies पुरम्
  11. पुरम्puramcityn. nom. sg. of पुर; subject of पाल्यते in 1.13
  12. हिhiindeed, nowindeclinable (emphatic particle)
  13. तत्tatthatpronoun तद्, n. nom. sg.; with पुरम्

Translation

Then, there, he, his mind drawn by possessiveness, thought: ‘That city, protected formerly by my forefathers, now deprived of me —

In readable EnglishThen, his mind still held by the sense of ‘mine’, he brooded: ‘That city my forefathers once protected, now bereft of me —

‘Now’ is supplied for the contrast with पूर्वम्; the sentence is completed in 1.13.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सोऽचिन्तयत् so'cintayat → सः + अचिन्तयत्

    visarga sandhi, then pūrvarūpa · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    Before a vowel the special rule for सः (6.1.132) does not apply; सः behaves like any -aḥ: so + a → so’ with avagraha.

  • ममत्वाकृष्ट mamatvākṛṣṭa → ममत्व + आकृष्ट

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + ā → ā.

  • मत्पूर्वैः matpūrvaiḥ → मद् + पूर्वैः

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (devoicing) · खरि च (8.4.55)

    The compound stem मद् (‘I, my’) ends in t before the unvoiced p.

  • पालितं पूर्वं मया हीनं पुरं pālitaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā hīnaṃ puraṃ → पालितम् + पूर्वम् + मया + हीनम् + पुरम्

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra, four times in one line.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • ममत्वाकृष्टचेतनः mamatvākṛṣṭacetanaḥ

    bahuvrīhi (its first part ममत्वाकृष्ट is a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa: ममत्वेन आकृष्टा)

    Members
    ममत्व + आकृष्ट + चेतना
    Vigraha
    ममत्वेन आकृष्टा चेतना यस्य सः mamatvena ākṛṣṭā cetanā yasya saḥ
    Literally
    “one whose mind is pulled by mine-ness”
    In the verse
    possessed by the thought ‘this is mine’
    Alternative
    चेतन (n.) ‘mind’ may be the last member instead of चेतना (f.); the bahuvrīhi ends in -चेतनः either way.

  • मत्पूर्वैः matpūrvaiḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    मद् + पूर्व
    Vigraha
    मम पूर्वे, तैः mama pūrve, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by my predecessors”
    In the verse
    by my ancestors, the earlier kings of my line
Morphology & anvaya

  • ममत्वाकृष्टचेतनः mamatvākṛṣṭacetanaḥ

    ममत्व is the genitive मम ‘of me’ made into an abstract noun with -त्व: ‘mine-ness’, possessiveness. The word returns in 1.41 and 1.44 (ममत्वाकृष्टमानसौ), where the king and the merchant both confess it.

  • हीनम् hīnam

    Participle of √हा ‘to leave’ (हीन ‘left, lacking’). With an instrumental it means ‘deprived of’: मया हीनम् ‘deprived of me’.

Anvaya · prose order

तदा तत्र ममत्वाकृष्टचेतनः सः अचिन्तयत् — पूर्वं मत्पूर्वैः पालितं मया हीनं तत् पुरं हि …

tadā tatra mamatvākṛṣṭacetanaḥ saḥ acintayat — pūrvaṃ matpūrvaiḥ pālitaṃ mayā hīnaṃ tat puraṃ hi …

The first line introduces the king’s thought; the second line begins it (the thought runs to 1.16), with पुरम् the subject of पाल्यते in 1.13.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The cause of Suratha’s grief is named at once: ममत्व, the feeling of ‘mine’. His thoughts (1.12–16) are a list of things he no longer owns — city, elephant, servants, treasury.

Traditional interpretation

ममत्व is the theme of the frame story. At the end the merchant asks the Goddess for the knowledge that removes ‘mine’ and ‘I’ (13.18: ममेत्यहमिति … सङ्गविच्युतिकारकम्), while the king asks for his kingdom (13.17).

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names the Goddess as free of and destroying this very thing: names 164 निर्ममा and 165 ममताहन्त्री. The two texts are distinct; the shared idea is the possessiveness the Goddess removes.

Verse 1.13

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

मद्भृत्यैस्तैरसद्वृत्तैर्धर्मतः पाल्यते न वा।न जाने स प्रधानो मे शूरहस्ती सदामदः॥⁠१३⁠॥

madbhṛtyaistairasadvṛttairdharmataḥ pālyate na vā |na jāne sa pradhāno me śūrahastī sadāmadaḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

मद्भृत्यैः · तैः · असद्वृत्तैः · धर्मतः · पाल्यते · न · वान · जाने · सः · प्रधानः · मे · शूरहस्ती · सदामदः

madbhṛtyaiḥ · taiḥ · asadvṛttaiḥ · dharmataḥ · pālyate · na · vāna · jāne · saḥ · pradhānaḥ · me · śūrahastī · sadāmadaḥ

Word by word

  1. मद्भृत्यैःmadbhṛtyaiḥby my servantsm. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); agent of पाल्यते
  2. तैःtaiḥby thosepronoun तद्, m. instr. pl.; with मद्भृत्यैः
  3. असद्वृत्तैःasadvṛttaiḥof bad conductm. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies मद्भृत्यैः
  4. धर्मतःdharmataḥaccording to dharma, rightlyindeclinable (धर्म + tasil, adverb)
  5. पाल्यतेpālyateis (it) protected√पाल् (curādi, 10), karmaṇi prayoga, laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada
  6. नnanotindeclinable (negation)
  7. वाvāorindeclinable (disjunctive); न वा ‘or not’
  8. नnanotindeclinable (negation)
  9. जानेjāneI know√ज्ञा (kryādi, 9U ‘to know’), laṭ (present), uttama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada
  10. सःsaḥthatpronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; with शूरहस्ती
  11. प्रधानःpradhānaḥchiefm. nom. sg. of प्रधान; qualifies शूरहस्ती
  12. मेmemyfirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg. (enclitic form)
  13. शूरहस्तीśūrahastīwar-elephant (lit. ‘valiant elephant’)m. nom. sg. of शूरहस्तिन्; compound (see Samāsa); subject of यातः … उपलप्स्यते in 1.14
  14. सदामदःsadāmadaḥalways in rut (musth)m. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies शूरहस्ती

Translation

‘— whether it is protected according to dharma by those servants of mine of bad conduct, or not, I do not know. That chief war-elephant of mine, always in rut —

In readable Englishis it being ruled justly by those faithless servants of mine, or not? I cannot know. And my chief war-elephant, ever in rut —

न जाने is attached to the first question in the literal version; the readable one lets it stand between the two worries, as the line does.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • मद्भृत्यैस्तैरसद्वृत्तैर्धर्मतः madbhṛtyaistairasadvṛttairdharmataḥ → मद्भृत्यैः + तैः + असद्वृत्तैः + धर्मतः

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34); ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    Visarga before t becomes s (भृत्यैस्तैः); after ai it stands as r before a vowel (तैरसद्) and before the voiced dh (वृत्तैर्धर्मतः).

  • मद्भृत्यै madbhṛtyai → मद् + भृत्यैः

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    The stem मद् keeps its voiced d before bh; the same in असद्वृत्तैः (असत् + वृत्त).

  • स प्रधानो मे sa pradhāno me → सः + प्रधानः + मे

    visarga sandhi · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132); हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    सः loses its visarga before p; प्रधानः before the voiced m becomes प्रधानो.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • मद्भृत्यैः madbhṛtyaiḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    मद् + भृत्य
    Vigraha
    मम भृत्याः, तैः mama bhṛtyāḥ, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by my servants”
    In the verse
    by the officers he left behind — the ministers of 1.8

  • असद्वृत्तैः asadvṛttaiḥ

    bahuvrīhi (असत् is a nañ tatpuruṣa: न सत्)

    Members
    असत् + वृत्त
    Vigraha
    असत् वृत्तं येषां ते, तैः asat vṛttaṃ yeṣāṃ te, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by those whose conduct is not good”
    In the verse
    by men of bad character

  • शूरहस्ती śūrahastī

    karmadhāraya

    Members
    शूर + हस्तिन्
    Vigraha
    शूरः हस्ती śūraḥ hastī
    Literally
    “a valiant elephant”
    In the verse
    a battle-elephant

  • सदामदः sadāmadaḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    सदा + मद
    Vigraha
    सदा मदः यस्य सः sadā madaḥ yasya saḥ
    Literally
    “one whose rut is constant”
    In the verse
    an elephant always in musth — the sign of a prized war-elephant
Morphology & anvaya

  • पाल्यते pālyate

    Passive present of the curādi root √पाल्: the causative-type -अय- is dropped before the passive -य-, giving पाल्य-ते. The subject is पुरम् from 1.12.

  • जाने jāne

    Present ātmanepada first singular of √ज्ञा (kryādi): the weak stem जानी- loses its ī before a vowel ending, जान् + ए → जाने. न जाने ‘I do not know’ introduces the next worry, which runs into 1.14.

Anvaya · prose order

(तत् पुरं) तैः असद्वृत्तैः मद्भृत्यैः धर्मतः पाल्यते न वा (इति) न जाने। सः मे प्रधानः सदामदः शूरहस्ती …

(tat puraṃ) taiḥ asadvṛttaiḥ madbhṛtyaiḥ dharmataḥ pālyate na vā (iti) na jāne | saḥ me pradhānaḥ sadāmadaḥ śūrahastī …

न जाने governs the question पाल्यते न वा; the second line begins a new subject (the elephant), whose verbs are in 1.14.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Two worries: whether his city is ruled rightly, and what has become of his favourite elephant. The king still thinks as an owner — ‘my servants’, ‘my elephant’ (मे).

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the grief is real but oddly specific. Loss often attaches itself to one cherished thing — here an elephant — that stands for the whole of what was taken.

Verse 1.14

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

मम वैरिवशं यातः कान् भोगानुपलप्स्यते।ये ममानुगता नित्यं प्रसादधनभोजनैः॥⁠१४⁠॥

mama vairivaśaṃ yātaḥ kān bhogānupalapsyate |ye mamānugatā nityaṃ prasādadhanabhojanaiḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

मम · वैरिवशम् · यातः · कान् · भोगान् · उपलप्स्यतेये · मम · अनुगताः · नित्यम् · प्रसादधनभोजनैः

mama · vairivaśam · yātaḥ · kān · bhogān · upalapsyateye · mama · anugatāḥ · nityam · prasādadhanabhojanaiḥ

Word by word

  1. ममmamamyfirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg.; with वैरि- (‘my enemies’)
  2. वैरिवशम्vairivaśaminto the power of (my) enemiesm. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); goal of यातः
  3. यातःyātaḥhaving gonepast participle (kta) of √या (adādi, 2P ‘to go’), m. nom. sg.; active sense; qualifies the elephant of 1.13
  4. कान्kānwhat (kind of)interrogative pronoun किम्, m. acc. pl.; qualifies भोगान्
  5. भोगान्bhogāncomforts, enjoyments (fodder and care)m. acc. pl. of भोग; object of उपलप्स्यते
  6. उपलप्स्यतेupalapsyatewill it getउप + √लभ् (bhvādi, 1Ā ‘to obtain’), lṛṭ (simple future), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada
  7. येyethose whorelative pronoun यद्, m. nom. pl.; correlative to ते in 1.15
  8. ममmamamefirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg.; with अनुगताः (‘followers of me’)
  9. अनुगताःanugatāḥfollowed, were attached (to me)past participle (kta) of अनु + √गम् (bhvādi, 1P), m. nom. pl.; active sense
  10. नित्यम्nityamalwaysindeclinable (adverbial acc. of नित्य)
  11. प्रसादधनभोजनैःprasādadhanabhojanaiḥthrough favours, wealth and mealsn. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); instrumental of means

Translation

‘— having gone into the power of my enemies, what enjoyments will it obtain? Those who always followed me, through favours, wealth and meals —

In readable Englishnow fallen into my enemies’ hands, what comforts will it find? And those who always followed me, won by my favour, my gifts and my table —

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • वैरिवशं यातः vairivaśaṃ yātaḥ → वैरिवशम् + यातः

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

  • यातः कान् yātaḥ kān → यातः + कान्

    visarga before k · खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः (8.3.15)

    Before the unvoiced k the visarga stays a visarga. The final n of कान् is then unchanged before the bh of भोगान्.

  • ममानुगता नित्यं mamānugatā nityaṃ → मम + अनुगताः + नित्यम्

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) and visarga sandhi · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101); ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17)

    मम + अनुगताः: a + a → ā. Then -āḥ before the voiced n: the visarga becomes y, and y is lost before a consonant, leaving अनुगता.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • वैरिवशम् vairivaśam

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    वैरिन् + वश
    Vigraha
    वैरिणां वशः, तम् vairiṇāṃ vaśaḥ, tam
    Literally
    “the control of enemies”
    In the verse
    into enemy hands
    Alternative
    मम qualifies only the first member (‘my enemies’ control’). Strictly a word outside a compound should not qualify a member inside it, but such constructions are common in epic and Purāṇic verse. मम could also go with यातः loosely (‘gone from me’), but ‘my enemies’ is the natural reading.

  • प्रसादधनभोजनैः prasādadhanabhojanaiḥ

    dvandva (itaretara)

    Members
    प्रसाद + धन + भोजन
    Vigraha
    प्रसादः च धनं च भोजनं च, तैः prasādaḥ ca dhanaṃ ca bhojanaṃ ca, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by favour, wealth and food”
    In the verse
    by the patronage, gifts and meals the king gave them
Morphology & anvaya

  • उपलप्स्यते upalapsyate

    Simple future of उप + √लभ् (ātmanepada root): लभ् + स्य → लप्स्य- (bh → p before s), with the ending -ते. ‘Will it obtain?’

  • यातः yātaḥ

    With a verb of motion the kta is active: ‘having gone (into the enemies’ power)’. The subject is the elephant of 1.13.

  • अनुगताः anugatāḥ

    Active kta of अनु + √गम्, nominative plural: ‘(those who) followed (me)’. The relative clause ये … अनुगताः is answered by ते in 1.15.

Anvaya · prose order

(सः शूरहस्ती) मम वैरिवशं यातः कान् भोगान् उपलप्स्यते? ये प्रसादधनभोजनैः नित्यं मम अनुगताः, (ते …)

(saḥ śūrahastī) mama vairivaśaṃ yātaḥ kān bhogān upalapsyate? ye prasādadhanabhojanaiḥ nityaṃ mama anugatāḥ, (te …)

The first line completes the elephant sentence of 1.13; the second opens a relative clause whose main clause (ते … कुर्वन्ति) is in 1.15.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king pities his elephant, then turns to his retainers, who were bound to him by what he gave: favour, money and food. The next verse says where their loyalty has gone.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: loyalty bought with favour, wealth and food follows the giver of those things, not the person. Suratha half sees this, and still grieves.

Verse 1.15

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

अनुवृत्तिं ध्रुवं तेऽद्य कुर्वन्त्यन्यमहीभृताम्।असम्यग्व्ययशीलैस्तैः कुर्वद्भिः सततं व्ययम्॥⁠१५⁠॥

anuvṛttiṃ dhruvaṃ te'dya kurvantyanyamahībhṛtām |asamyagvyayaśīlaistaiḥ kurvadbhiḥ satataṃ vyayam ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

अनुवृत्तिम् · ध्रुवम् · ते · अद्य · कुर्वन्ति · अन्यमहीभृताम्असम्यग्व्ययशीलैः · तैः · कुर्वद्भिः · सततम् · व्ययम्

anuvṛttim · dhruvam · te · adya · kurvanti · anyamahībhṛtāmasamyagvyayaśīlaiḥ · taiḥ · kurvadbhiḥ · satatam · vyayam

Word by word

  1. अनुवृत्तिम्anuvṛttimservice, compliance (lit. ‘following after’)f. acc. sg. of अनुवृत्ति; object of कुर्वन्ति
  2. ध्रुवम्dhruvamsurelyindeclinable (adverbial acc. of ध्रुव)
  3. तेtetheypronoun तद्, m. nom. pl.; correlative of ये in 1.14
  4. अद्यadyanow, todayindeclinable (adverb of time)
  5. कुर्वन्तिkurvantido, render√कृ (tanādi, 8U ‘to do’), laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana, parasmaipada
  6. अन्यमहीभृताम्anyamahībhṛtāmof other kingsm. gen. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); dependent on अनुवृत्तिम्
  7. असम्यग्व्ययशीलैःasamyagvyayaśīlaiḥgiven to improper spendingm. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies तैः
  8. तैःtaiḥby them (the ministers)pronoun तद्, m. instr. pl.; instrumental of cause, construed with गमिष्यति in 1.16
  9. कुर्वद्भिःkurvadbhiḥmakingpresent participle (śatṛ) of √कृ, m. instr. pl.; agrees with तैः
  10. सततम्satatamconstantlyindeclinable (adverbial acc. of सतत)
  11. व्ययम्vyayamexpenditurem. acc. sg. of व्यय; object of कुर्वद्भिः

Translation

‘— they surely now render service to other kings. By those given to improper spending, constantly making expenditure —

In readable Englishsurely they now pay court to other kings. And by those wastrels, spending without pause —

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तेऽद्य te'dya → ते + अद्य

    vowel sandhi (pūrvarūpa) · एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -e + a- → -e’-: the a is absorbed (avagraha).

  • कुर्वन्त्यन्य kurvantyanya → कुर्वन्ति + अन्यमहीभृताम्

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Final i before a dissimilar vowel becomes y.

  • असम्यग्व्यय asamyagvyaya → असम्यक् + व्यय

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    Final k becomes g before the voiced v.

  • व्ययशीलैस्तैः vyayaśīlaistaiḥ → असम्यग्व्ययशीलैः + तैः

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अन्यमहीभृताम् anyamahībhṛtām

    karmadhāraya (महीभृत् is an upapada tatpuruṣa: महीं बिभर्ति इति)

    Members
    अन्य + महीभृत्
    Vigraha
    अन्ये महीभृतः, तेषाम् anye mahībhṛtaḥ, teṣām
    Literally
    “of other earth-bearers”
    In the verse
    of other kings — his rivals

  • असम्यग्व्ययशीलैः asamyagvyayaśīlaiḥ

    bahuvrīhi (असम्यक् is a nañ tatpuruṣa: न सम्यक्)

    Members
    असम्यक् + व्यय + शील
    Vigraha
    असम्यक् व्ययः शीलं येषां ते, तैः asamyak vyayaḥ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by those whose habit is improper spending”
    In the verse
    by spendthrift, dishonest managers of the treasury
Morphology & anvaya

  • कुर्वन्ति kurvanti

    Present third plural of √कृ (tanādi), weak stem कुरु- with u → v before the vowel ending: कुर्व्-अन्ति.

  • कुर्वद्भिः kurvadbhiḥ

    Present participle कुर्वत् (√कृ + śatṛ), instrumental plural: the t becomes d before bh. It agrees with तैः: ‘by them, making (expense)’.

  • ध्रुवम् dhruvam

    The adjective ध्रुव ‘fixed, certain’ in the neuter accusative, used as an adverb: ‘surely’. The king is guessing, but with conviction.

Anvaya · prose order

ते अद्य ध्रुवम् अन्यमहीभृताम् अनुवृत्तिं कुर्वन्ति। सततं व्ययं कुर्वद्भिः असम्यग्व्ययशीलैः तैः (1.16: …कोशः क्षयं गमिष्यति)।

te adya dhruvam anyamahībhṛtām anuvṛttiṃ kurvanti | satataṃ vyayaṃ kurvadbhiḥ asamyagvyayaśīlaiḥ taiḥ (1.16: …kośaḥ kṣayaṃ gamiṣyati) |

The first line completes the relative clause of 1.14 (ये … ते). The second line is a string of instrumentals whose verb, गमिष्यति, comes in 1.16.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king imagines his former followers serving his rivals, and his ministers squandering his treasury. Both thoughts are guesses; he has no news.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: anxiety supplies certainties (ध्रुवम्, ‘surely’) that the mind has no way of checking. Suratha suffers over events he can only imagine.

Verse 1.16

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

संचितः सोऽतिदुःखेन क्षयं कोशो गमिष्यति।एतच्चान्यच्च सततं चिन्तयामास पार्थिवः॥⁠१६⁠॥

saṃcitaḥ so'tiduḥkhena kṣayaṃ kośo gamiṣyati |etaccānyacca satataṃ cintayāmāsa pārthivaḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

संचितः · सः · अतिदुःखेन · क्षयम् · कोशः · गमिष्यतिएतत् · च · अन्यत् · च · सततम् · चिन्तयामास · पार्थिवः

saṃcitaḥ · saḥ · atiduḥkhena · kṣayam · kośaḥ · gamiṣyatietat · ca · anyat · ca · satatam · cintayāmāsa · pārthivaḥ

Word by word

  1. संचितःsaṃcitaḥamassed, accumulatedpast passive participle (kta) of सम् + √चि (svādi, 5U ‘to gather’), m. nom. sg.; qualifies कोशः
  2. सःsaḥthatpronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; with कोशः
  3. अतिदुःखेनatiduḥkhenawith great hardshipn. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); instrumental of manner
  4. क्षयम्kṣayamto ruin, to exhaustionm. acc. sg. of क्षय; goal of गमिष्यति
  5. कोशःkośaḥthe treasurym. nom. sg. of कोश; subject
  6. गमिष्यतिgamiṣyatiwill go√गम् (bhvādi, 1P), lṛṭ (simple future), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  7. एतत्etatthispronoun एतद्, n. acc. sg.; object of चिन्तयामास
  8. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  9. अन्यत्anyatother (things)pronominal adjective अन्य, n. acc. sg.; object of चिन्तयामास
  10. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction); एतच्च अन्यच्च ‘this and more’
  11. सततम्satatamconstantlyindeclinable (adverbial acc. of सतत)
  12. चिन्तयामासcintayāmāsathought over, brooded on√चिन्त् (curādi, 10P), liṭ (periphrastic perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  13. पार्थिवःpārthivaḥthe kingm. nom. sg. of पार्थिव (taddhita from पृथिवी: ‘lord of the earth’); subject

Translation

‘— that treasury, amassed with great hardship, will go to ruin.’ This and other things the king pondered constantly.

In readable Englishthe treasury I gathered with such toil will be drained away.’ These and other thoughts filled the king’s mind without rest.

‘I’ is supplied: the Sanskrit says only ‘amassed with great hardship’.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सोऽतिदुःखेन so'tiduḥkhena → सः + अतिदुःखेन

    visarga sandhi, then pūrvarūpa · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    सः before a: so’ with avagraha (as in 1.12).

  • कोशो गमिष्यति kośo gamiṣyati → कोशः + गमिष्यति

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced g becomes -o.

  • एतच्चान्यच्च etaccānyacca → एतत् + च + अन्यत् + च

    consonant sandhi (t → c) and vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    Final t before c becomes c (एतच्च, अन्यच्च); च + अन्यत् → चान्यत्.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अतिदुःखेन atiduḥkhena

    prādi tatpuruṣa

    Members
    अति + दुःख
    Vigraha
    अतिशयितं दुःखम्, तेन atiśayitaṃ duḥkham, tena
    Literally
    “by excessive pain”
    In the verse
    with great labour and hardship
Morphology & anvaya

  • चिन्तयामास cintayāmāsa

    Periphrastic perfect: roots with a derived stem (here the curādi चिन्तय-) form the perfect with -आम् + the perfect of √अस् (आस): चिन्तयाम् + आस. Compare अचिन्तयत् (imperfect) in 1.12, which opened the same train of thought.

  • गमिष्यति gamiṣyati

    Simple future of √गम् with connecting -इ-: गम् + इ + ष्य + ति. With क्षयम् ‘will go to ruin’.

  • संचितः saṃcitaḥ

    Participle of सम् + √चि: ‘gathered together’. Printed with anusvāra for the nasal of सम् before c.

Anvaya · prose order

(तैः) अतिदुःखेन संचितः सः कोशः क्षयं गमिष्यति। एतत् च अन्यत् च पार्थिवः सततं चिन्तयामास।

(taiḥ) atiduḥkhena saṃcitaḥ saḥ kośaḥ kṣayaṃ gamiṣyati | etat ca anyat ca pārthivaḥ satataṃ cintayāmāsa |

The first line completes the sentence begun in 1.15b (‘through them … the treasury will go to ruin’); the second closes the king’s thoughts (1.12–16) and is the narrator’s.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The last of the king’s worries is the treasury; the narrator then closes the passage: he thought of ‘this and other things’ ceaselessly. No इति marks the end of the thought; the change of verb (चिन्तयामास) does.

Traditional interpretation

Suratha’s monologue moves through city, elephant, retainers and treasury — the things of a kingdom. Medhas’s later teaching treats all of them as objects of ममत्व held in place by Mahāmāyā.

Verse 1.17

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

तत्र विप्राश्रमाभ्याशे वैश्यमेकं ददर्श सः।स पृष्टस्तेन कस्त्वं भो हेतुश्चागमनेऽत्र कः॥⁠१७⁠॥

tatra viprāśramābhyāśe vaiśyamekaṃ dadarśa saḥ |sa pṛṣṭastena kastvaṃ bho hetuścāgamane'tra kaḥ ||

tatra · viprāśramābhyāśe · vaiśyam · ekam · dadarśa · saḥsaḥ · pṛṣṭaḥ · tena · kaḥ · tvam · bhoḥ · hetuḥ · ca · āgamane · atra · kaḥ

Word by word

  1. तत्रtatrathereindeclinable (adverb of place)
  2. विप्राश्रमाभ्याशेviprāśramābhyāśenear the brahmin’s hermitagem. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)
  3. वैश्यम्vaiśyama merchant (a man of the vaiśya class)m. acc. sg. of वैश्य; object of ददर्श
  4. एकम्ekama certain, onenumeral adjective एक used as indefinite article, m. acc. sg.; qualifies वैश्यम्
  5. ददर्शdadarśasaw√दृश् (bhvādi, 1P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  6. सःsaḥhe (the king)pronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; subject of ददर्श
  7. सःsaḥhe (the merchant)pronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; subject of पृष्टः
  8. पृष्टःpṛṣṭaḥwas askedpast passive participle (kta) of √प्रच्छ् (tudādi, 6P ‘to ask’), m. nom. sg.; used as the finite verb
  9. तेनtenaby him (the king)pronoun तद्, m. instr. sg.; agent
  10. कःkaḥwhointerrogative pronoun किम्, m. nom. sg.
  11. त्वम्tvamyousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, nom. sg.
  12. भोःbhoḥsir, friendindeclinable (vocative particle of address)
  13. हेतुःhetuḥreasonm. nom. sg. of हेतु
  14. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)

Translation

There, near the brahmin’s hermitage, he saw a certain merchant. He was asked by him: ‘Who are you, sir? And what is the reason for your coming here?

In readable EnglishThere, near the sage’s hermitage, he saw a merchant, and asked him: ‘Who are you, friend? What has brought you here?

The passive (‘he was asked by him’) is turned into an active sentence.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • विप्राश्रमाभ्याशे viprāśramābhyāśe → विप्र + आश्रम + अभ्याशे

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha, twice) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + ā → ā and a + a → ā.

  • पृष्टस्तेन कस्त्वं pṛṣṭastena kastvaṃ → पृष्टः + तेन + कः + त्वम्

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s, twice.

  • भो हेतु bho hetu → भोः + हेतुः

    visarga sandhi (भोः) · भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17)

    The visarga of भोः becomes y before a voiced sound, and y is lost before a consonant: भो हेतुः.

  • हेतुश्चागमनेऽत्र hetuścāgamane'tra → हेतुः + च + आगमने + अत्र

    visarga sandhi, savarṇa-dīrgha and pūrvarūpa · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101); एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    Visarga before c → ś; च + आ → चा; आगमने + अत्र → आगमनेऽत्र.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • विप्राश्रमाभ्याशे viprāśramābhyāśe

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    विप्राश्रम + अभ्याश
    Vigraha
    विप्रस्य आश्रमः विप्राश्रमः; विप्राश्रमस्य अभ्याशः, तस्मिन् viprasya āśramaḥ viprāśramaḥ; viprāśramasya abhyāśaḥ, tasmin
    Literally
    “in the vicinity of the brahmin’s hermitage”
    In the verse
    near Medhas’s hermitage
Morphology & anvaya

  • पृष्टः pṛṣṭaḥ

    Passive participle of √प्रच्छ्: the root becomes पृच्छ्/प्रश्- and with -त gives पृष्ट (ś + t → ṣṭ). Verbs of asking take the person asked as the subject in the passive: ‘he was asked’.

  • ददर्श dadarśa

    Perfect of √दृश् with reduplication द- and guṇa of the root vowel (दृश् → दर्श्). Compare the aorist अद्राक्षीत् in 1.10.

Anvaya · prose order

तत्र विप्राश्रमाभ्याशे सः एकं वैश्यं ददर्श। सः तेन पृष्टः — भोः, त्वं कः? अत्र आगमने च हेतुः कः?

tatra viprāśramābhyāśe saḥ ekaṃ vaiśyaṃ dadarśa | saḥ tena pṛṣṭaḥ — bhoḥ, tvaṃ kaḥ? atra āgamane ca hetuḥ kaḥ?

Two narrative clauses (the king saw; the merchant was asked) and the direct question, which continues into 1.18.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The second figure of the frame story appears: a merchant, met by chance near the hermitage. The king, absorbed in his own losses until now, notices another man’s grief and speaks first.

Traditional interpretation

The meeting of the deposed king and the disowned merchant pairs two kinds of loss — power and family. The tradition reads the two as the seekers of enjoyment and of liberation, as their final requests in chapter 13 show.

Verse 1.18

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

सशोक इव कस्मात्त्वं दुर्मना इव लक्ष्यसे।इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्य भूपतेः प्रणयोदितम्॥⁠१८⁠॥

saśoka iva kasmāttvaṃ durmanā iva lakṣyase |ityākarṇya vacastasya bhūpateḥ praṇayoditam ||

saśokaḥ · iva · kasmāt · tvam · durmanāḥ · iva · lakṣyaseiti · ākarṇya · vacaḥ · tasya · bhūpateḥ · praṇayoditam

Word by word
