  2. इवivaas if, seeminglyindeclinable (particle of comparison; here ‘as it were’)
  3. कस्मात्kasmātwhy (lit. ‘from what’)interrogative pronoun किम्, n. abl. sg., used adverbially
  4. त्वम्tvamyousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, nom. sg.; subject
  5. दुर्मनाःdurmanāḥdejected, troubled in mindm. nom. sg. of दुर्मनस्; compound (see Samāsa); predicate with लक्ष्यसे
  6. इवivaas ifindeclinable (particle)
  7. लक्ष्यसेlakṣyasedo you appear, are you seen√लक्ष् (curādi, 10 ‘to mark, observe’), karmaṇi prayoga, laṭ (present), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada
  8. इतिitithus (closing the quotation)indeclinable (quotative particle)
  9. आकर्ण्यākarṇyahaving heardabsolutive (lyap) of आ + कर्णय- (denominative from कर्ण ‘ear’, curādi type: ‘to give ear to’)
  10. वचःvacaḥthe wordsn. acc. sg. of वचस्; object of आकर्ण्य
  11. तस्यtasyaof thatpronoun तद्, m. gen. sg.; with भूपतेः
  12. भूपतेःbhūpateḥof the kingm. gen. sg. of भूपति (i-stem)
  13. प्रणयोदितम्praṇayoditamspoken in friendshipn. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies वचः

Translation

‘Why do you appear as if sorrowful, as if downcast?’ Having heard thus the words of that king, spoken in friendship —

In readable EnglishWhy do you look so sorrowful, so heavy-hearted?’ Hearing these kindly words of the king,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सशोक इव saśoka iva → सशोकः + इव

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17), लोपः शाकल्यस्य (8.3.19)

    -aḥ before a vowel other than a: the visarga becomes y, the y is dropped, and the vowels stand apart (as in 1.1).

  • दुर्मना इव durmanā iva → दुर्मनाः + इव

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17), लोपः शाकल्यस्य (8.3.19)

    -āḥ before a vowel: the visarga becomes y and is dropped; the hiatus remains.

  • इत्याकर्ण्य ityākarṇya → इति + आकर्ण्य

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    i before ā becomes y.

  • वचस्तस्य vacastasya → वचः + तस्य

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

  • प्रणयोदितम् praṇayoditam → प्रणय + उदितम्

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + u → o.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • सशोकः saśokaḥ

    bahuvrīhi (saha-bahuvrīhi; सह becomes स-)

    Members
    सह + शोक
    Vigraha
    शोकेन सह वर्तते इति śokena saha vartate iti
    Literally
    “being with sorrow”
    In the verse
    grief-stricken

  • दुर्मनाः durmanāḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    दुस् + मनस्
    Vigraha
    दुष्टं (खिन्नं) मनः यस्य सः duṣṭaṃ (khinnaṃ) manaḥ yasya saḥ
    Literally
    “one whose mind is ill”
    In the verse
    downcast, heavy-hearted

  • प्रणयोदितम् praṇayoditam

    tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa

    Members
    प्रणय + उदित
    Vigraha
    प्रणयेन उदितम् praṇayena uditam
    Literally
    “spoken with affection”
    In the verse
    words said kindly, as to a friend
Morphology & anvaya

  • लक्ष्यसे lakṣyase

    Passive present, second singular, of √लक्ष्: ‘you are observed (as)’, i.e. ‘you look’. The predicates सशोकः and दुर्मनाः stand in the nominative with it.

  • दुर्मनाः durmanāḥ

    Nominative singular masculine of the s-stem दुर्मनस्: the vowel before the final s is lengthened (-अस् → -आः).

  • आकर्ण्य ākarṇya

    Absolutive of a denominative verb formed from कर्ण ‘ear’; with the prefix आ it takes -य (lyap), and the stem’s -अय- is dropped: आकर्णय- → आकर्ण्य.

Anvaya · prose order

त्वं कस्मात् सशोकः इव दुर्मनाः इव लक्ष्यसे? इति तस्य भूपतेः प्रणयोदितं वचः आकर्ण्य, (1.19: सः वैश्यः … प्रत्युवाच)।

tvaṃ kasmāt saśokaḥ iva durmanāḥ iva lakṣyase? iti tasya bhūpateḥ praṇayoditaṃ vacaḥ ākarṇya, (1.19: saḥ vaiśyaḥ … pratyuvāca) |

The first line ends the king’s question; इति closes it. The absolutive आकर्ण्य has as its subject the merchant of 1.19.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king’s question ends, and the narrator notes its tone: it was spoken with प्रणय, warmth or friendliness. The repeated इव (‘as if’) is courteous; the king does not presume to name the stranger’s grief.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: for the first time since 1.5 Suratha’s attention leaves his own losses. Concern for another’s sorrow opens the conversation that leads to the teaching.

pratyuvāca · saḥ · tam · vaiśyaḥ · praśrayāvanataḥ · nṛpam

Word by word

  1. प्रत्युवाचpratyuvācarepliedप्रति + √वच् (adādi, 2P ‘to speak’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  2. सःsaḥthatpronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; with वैश्यः
  3. तम्tamthatpronoun तद्, m. acc. sg.; with नृपम्
  4. वैश्यःvaiśyaḥmerchantm. nom. sg. of वैश्य; subject
  5. प्रश्रयावनतःpraśrayāvanataḥbowing in humilitym. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies वैश्यः

Translation

— that merchant, bowed with humility, replied to that king.

In readable Englishthe merchant bowed respectfully and answered him.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • प्रत्युवाच pratyuvāca → प्रति + उवाच

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) between prefix and verb · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    The prefix प्रति before the u of उवाच becomes प्रत्य्-.

  • स तं वैश्यः sa taṃ vaiśyaḥ → सः + तम् + वैश्यः

    visarga sandhi (सः) and anusvāra · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132); मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    सः loses its visarga before t; तम् becomes तं before v.

  • प्रश्रयावनतो नृपम् praśrayāvanato nṛpam → प्रश्रयावनतः + नृपम्

    visarga sandhi; savarṇa-dīrgha inside the compound · हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    -aḥ before the voiced n → -o; प्रश्रय + अवनत → प्रश्रयावनत.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • प्रश्रयावनतः praśrayāvanataḥ

    tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa

    Members
    प्रश्रय + अवनत
    Vigraha
    प्रश्रयेण अवनतः praśrayeṇa avanataḥ
    Literally
    “bent down with modesty”
    In the verse
    bowing respectfully
Morphology & anvaya

  • प्रत्युवाच pratyuvāca

    Perfect of √वच् (उवाच, as in 1.1) with the prefix प्रति: ‘spoke back, replied’. Verbs of speaking take the person addressed in the accusative (तं नृपम्).

  • प्रश्रयावनतः praśrayāvanataḥ

    अवनत is the kta of अव + √नम् ‘to bend’ (the nasal of नम् is lost before -त); active sense, ‘bowed’.

Anvaya · prose order

सः वैश्यः प्रश्रयावनतः तं नृपं प्रत्युवाच।

saḥ vaiśyaḥ praśrayāvanataḥ taṃ nṛpaṃ pratyuvāca |

Subject with its participle, the person addressed, and the verb. It completes the sentence of 1.18b (आकर्ण्य … प्रत्युवाच).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

A half-śloka that closes the narrative of the meeting. The merchant answers with deference to a man he recognises as a king; his own story follows after the speaker label (1.20).

    -aḥ before a vowel other than a: the visarga becomes y, the y is dropped, and the vowels stand apart (as in मार्कण्डेय उवाच, 1.1).

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

vaiśyaḥ uvāca |

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Speaker label: the merchant now answers the king’s questions of 1.17–18 (who he is, and why he has come). Mārkaṇḍeya is still the narrator of the whole exchange.

Padaccheda · the words separated

Translation

I am a merchant named Samādhi, born in a family of wealthy men.

In readable EnglishI am a merchant named Samādhi, born into a wealthy family.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • समाधिर्नाम samādhirnāma → समाधिः + नाम

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    After i the visarga stands as r before the voiced n.

  • वैश्योऽहमुत्पन्नो vaiśyo'hamutpanno → वैश्यः + अहम् + उत्पन्नः

    visarga sandhi, then pūrvarūpa · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a- → -o’; the m of अहम् is simply written together with the following vowel; उत्पन्नः before the voiced dh becomes उत्पन्नो (हशि च, 6.1.114).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • उत्पन्नः utpannaḥ

    kta of उत् + √पद् ‘to arise’: the root’s final d and the t of the suffix become -न्न- (पद् + त → पन्न). With an intransitive verb the participle is active: ‘born, arisen’.

  • धनिनाम् dhaninām

    Genitive plural of the -in stem धनिन् ‘having wealth’ (धन + possessive -in), like बलिन् in 1.8.

Anvaya · prose order

अहं समाधिः नाम वैश्यः धनिनां कुले उत्पन्नः।

ahaṃ samādhiḥ nāma vaiśyaḥ dhanināṃ kule utpannaḥ |

Name and class (समाधिः नाम वैश्यः), subject (अहम्), and a participle phrase giving his birth.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The merchant answers the first question (‘who are you?’): his name, his class, his family. The next verses answer the second (‘why have you come?’).

Traditional interpretation

The name समाधि — ‘composure, absorption’ — is often noticed as apt: he is the one who at the end asks the Goddess for knowledge rather than wealth (13.18), and receives it (13.25).

Verse 1.22

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

पुत्रदारैर्निरस्तश्च धनलोभादसाधुभिः।विहीनश्च धनैर्दारैः पुत्रैरादाय मे धनम्॥⁠२२⁠॥

putradārairnirastaśca dhanalobhādasādhubhiḥ |vihīnaśca dhanairdāraiḥ putrairādāya me dhanam ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

पुत्रदारैः · निरस्तः · च · धनलोभात् · असाधुभिःविहीनः · च · धनैः · दारैः · पुत्रैः · आदाय · मे · धनम्

putradāraiḥ · nirastaḥ · ca · dhanalobhāt · asādhubhiḥvihīnaḥ · ca · dhanaiḥ · dāraiḥ · putraiḥ · ādāya · me · dhanam

Word by word

  1. पुत्रदारैःputradāraiḥby my sons and wifem. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); agent of निरस्तः
  2. निरस्तःnirastaḥcast outpast passive participle (kta) of निर् + √अस् (divādi, 4P ‘to throw’), m. nom. sg.; predicate of (अहम्)
  3. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  4. धनलोभात्dhanalobhātout of greed for wealthm. abl. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); ablative of cause
  5. असाधुभिःasādhubhiḥwicked, unworthym. instr. pl. of असाधु (nañ tatpuruṣa: न साधुः); qualifies पुत्रदारैः
  6. विहीनःvihīnaḥdeprived (of)past participle (kta) of वि + √हा (juhotyādi, 3P ‘to leave’), m. nom. sg.; predicate of (अहम्)
  7. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  8. धनैःdhanaiḥof wealthn. instr. pl. of धन; instrumental of separation with विहीनः
  9. दारैःdāraiḥof wifem. instr. pl. of दार (always plural, ‘wife’); with विहीनः
  10. पुत्रैःputraiḥof sonsm. instr. pl. of पुत्र; with विहीनः
  11. आदायādāyahaving takenabsolutive (lyap) of आ + √दा (juhotyādi, 3U ‘to give’; with आ ‘to take’)
  12. मेmemyfirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg. (enclitic); with धनम्
  13. धनम्dhanamwealthn. acc. sg. of धन; object of आदाय

Translation

And I have been cast out by my wicked sons and wife out of greed for wealth, and am deprived of wealth, wife and sons; (they,) having taken my wealth —

In readable EnglishMy wicked sons and wife, greedy for my wealth, have driven me out. I am left without money, wife or sons; they have taken all I had,

‘All I had’ renders मे धनम् ‘my wealth’; the subject ‘they’ of आदाय is supplied.

Textual verification / uncertain: The construction of the second line admits two readings: (a) धनैः दारैः पुत्रैः all depend on विहीनः (‘deprived of wealth, wife and sons’), with आदाय मे धनम् referring to the relatives; (b) विहीनः धनैः only, with दारैः पुत्रैः as the agents of आदाय (‘deprived of wealth, my wife and sons having taken it’). Reading (a) is followed here as the more natural word order.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • पुत्रदारैर्निरस्तश्च putradārairnirastaśca → पुत्रदारैः + निरस्तः + च

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66); विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    After ai the visarga stands as r before the voiced n; निरस्तः before c becomes निरस्तश्.

  • धनलोभादसाधुभिः dhanalobhādasādhubhiḥ → धनलोभात् + असाधुभिः

    consonant sandhi (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    Final t becomes d before a vowel.

  • धनैर्दारैः पुत्रैरादाय dhanairdāraiḥ putrairādāya → धनैः + दारैः + पुत्रैः + आदाय

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66); खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः (8.3.15)

    After ai the visarga stands as r before the voiced d and before the vowel ā; before the unvoiced p (दारैः पुत्रैः) it remains a visarga.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • पुत्रदारैः putradāraiḥ

    dvandva (itaretara)

    Members
    पुत्र + दार
    Vigraha
    पुत्राः च दाराः च, तैः putrāḥ ca dārāḥ ca, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by sons and wife”
    In the verse
    by his own family

  • धनलोभात् dhanalobhāt

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    धन + लोभ
    Vigraha
    धनस्य लोभः, तस्मात् dhanasya lobhaḥ, tasmāt
    Literally
    “from greed of wealth”
    In the verse
    because they coveted his money
Morphology & anvaya

  • विहीनः vihīnaḥ

    Participle of वि + √हा ‘to leave’: ‘left without, deprived of’, construed with the instrumental (धनैः दारैः पुत्रैः).

  • आदाय ādāya

    Absolutive of आ + √दा ‘to take’. Its logical subject is not the speaker but those who wronged him — the sons and wife (or the kinsmen of 1.23): ‘having taken my wealth, (they cast me out)’. Such a shift of subject is common in epic narrative.

  • दारैः dāraiḥ

    दार ‘wife’ is masculine and used in the plural for a single wife — a fixed idiom.

Anvaya · prose order

धनलोभात् असाधुभिः पुत्रदारैः (अहं) निरस्तः च, धनैः दारैः पुत्रैः च विहीनः; (ते) मे धनम् आदाय (1.23: आप्तबन्धुभिः च निरस्तः) …

dhanalobhāt asādhubhiḥ putradāraiḥ (ahaṃ) nirastaḥ ca, dhanaiḥ dāraiḥ putraiḥ ca vihīnaḥ; (te) me dhanam ādāya (1.23: āptabandhubhiḥ ca nirastaḥ) …

Two predicates of an implied अहम् (निरस्तः, विहीनः); the absolutive phrase आदाय मे धनम् belongs with the agents who cast him out and runs into 1.23.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The merchant’s answer to ‘why have you come?’: his own family has thrown him out to take his wealth. His loss mirrors the king’s — Suratha was betrayed by ministers, Samādhi by sons and wife.

Traditional interpretation

Unlike the king, the merchant names his betrayers as his nearest kin; the point is made sharper in 1.31–34, where he confesses that his heart still goes out to them.

Verse 1.23

vanamabhyāgato duḥkhī nirastaścāptabandhubhiḥ |so'haṃ na vedmi putrāṇāṃ kuśalākuśalātmikām ||

  3. दुःखीduḥkhīin sorrowm. nom. sg. of दुःखिन् (‘having sorrow’); predicative

  5. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)

Translation

— and cast out by trusted kinsmen, I have come, sorrowful, to the forest. I, such as I am, do not know the (news), of good or ill, of my sons,

In readable Englishand, cast off by the kinsmen I trusted, I have come to this forest in grief. Now I do not know whether things go well or ill with my sons,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • वनमभ्यागतो दुःखी vanamabhyāgato duḥkhī → वनम् + अभ्यागतः + दुःखी

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    The m of वनम् is written together with the vowel; -aḥ before the voiced d becomes -o.

  • निरस्तश्चाप्तबन्धुभिः nirastaścāptabandhubhiḥ → निरस्तः + च + आप्तबन्धुभिः

    visarga sandhi and savarṇa-dīrgha · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    Visarga before c → ś; च + आ → चा.

  • सोऽहं so'haṃ → सः + अहम्

    visarga sandhi, then pūrvarūpa · अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    सः before a → so’ (as in 1.12).

  • कुशलाकुशलात्मिकाम् kuśalākuśalātmikām → कुशल + अकुशल + आत्मिका

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha, twice) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + a → ā and a + ā → ā.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • आप्तबन्धुभिः āptabandhubhiḥ

    karmadhāraya

    Members
    आप्त + बन्धु
    Vigraha
    आप्ताः बन्धवः, तैः āptāḥ bandhavaḥ, taiḥ
    Literally
    “by trusted relatives”
    In the verse
    by the kinsmen he relied on

  • कुशलाकुशलात्मिकाम् kuśalākuśalātmikām

    bahuvrīhi (with the suffix -क) containing a dvandva

    Members
    कुशलाकुशल + आत्मन् (+ क)
    Vigraha
    कुशलं च अकुशलं च कुशलाकुशले (dvandva; अकुशल is a nañ tatpuruṣa); कुशलाकुशले आत्मा (स्वरूपम्) यस्याः सा, ताम् kuśalaṃ ca akuśalaṃ ca kuśalākuśale (dvandva; akuśala is a nañ tatpuruṣa); kuśalākuśale ātmā (svarūpam) yasyāḥ sā, tām
    Literally
    “whose nature is well-being and ill-being”
    In the verse
    news, whether good or bad
Morphology & anvaya

  • वेद्मि vedmi

    Present first singular of √विद् (adādi), with guṇa (विद् → वेद्) before the strong ending -मि. न वेद्मि governs प्रवृत्तिम् in 1.24.

  • अभ्यागतः abhyāgataḥ

    Active kta of a verb of motion with two prefixes, अभि + आ: ‘(I) have come’ (to the forest).

  • कुशलाकुशलात्मिकाम् kuśalākuśalātmikām

    आत्मक ‘having the nature of, consisting of’ (आत्मन् + -क) makes its feminine in -इका: आत्मिका. It agrees with प्रवृत्तिम् (f.) in the next verse.

Anvaya · prose order

(अहं) दुःखी आप्तबन्धुभिः च निरस्तः वनम् अभ्यागतः। सः अहम् अत्र संस्थितः पुत्राणां … कुशलाकुशलात्मिकां (प्रवृत्तिं) न वेद्मि (1.24)।

(ahaṃ) duḥkhī āptabandhubhiḥ ca nirastaḥ vanam abhyāgataḥ | saḥ aham atra saṃsthitaḥ putrāṇāṃ … kuśalākuśalātmikāṃ (pravṛttiṃ) na vedmi (1.24) |

The first line ends the account of his expulsion; the second begins a sentence completed in 1.24 (न वेद्मि … प्रवृत्तिम्).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The merchant’s second answer: he came to the forest because his own people drove him out. Yet his first thought is not of his wrong but of their welfare, which he cannot learn.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: he has been thrown out and robbed, and still worries whether those who did it are well. The text shows the bond outliving the betrayal before it names it as a puzzle (1.31–34).

In readable Englishor with my kin and my wife, for I am here, far away. Is all well in their home now, or is it not?

‘Far away’ draws out अत्र संस्थितः (‘staying here’), which explains why he has no news.

Anvaya · prose order

अत्र संस्थितः (अहं) पुत्राणां स्वजनानां च दाराणां च प्रवृत्तिं न वेद्मि (1.23)। तेषां गृहे साम्प्रतं क्षेमं किं नु, अक्षेमं किं नु?

The first line completes न वेद्मि of 1.23 with its object; the second is a double question (किं नु … किं नु).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The sentence of 1.23 ends: he has no tidings of sons, kin or wife because he is here in the forest. He asks twice, with किं नु, whether they are well.

Translation

How are they? Are my sons, I wonder, of good conduct, or of bad conduct?

In readable EnglishHow are they? Are my sons living rightly now, or have they gone astray?

‘Now’ is supplied from साम्प्रतम् in 1.24.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सद्वृत्ता दुर्वृत्ताः sadvṛttā durvṛttāḥ → सद्वृत्ताः + दुर्वृत्ताः

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17)

    -āḥ before the voiced d: the visarga becomes y, and y is lost before a consonant.

  • सद्वृत्ता sadvṛttā → सत् + वृत्त

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    The t of सत् becomes d before the voiced v. (The digital source marked the half-form d with a joiner, removed as an encoding hint; the letters are unchanged.)

  • दुर्वृत्ताः किं durvṛttāḥ kiṃ → दुर्वृत्ताः + किम्

    visarga before k · खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः (8.3.15)

    Before the unvoiced k the visarga remains. Inside दुर्वृत्त, the prefix दुस् shows r before the voiced v (ससजुषो रुः, 8.2.66).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • सद्वृत्ताः sadvṛttāḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    सत् + वृत्त
    Vigraha
    सत् वृत्तं येषां ते sat vṛttaṃ yeṣāṃ te
    Literally
    “those whose conduct is good”
    In the verse
    well-behaved

  • दुर्वृत्ताः durvṛttāḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    दुस् + वृत्त
    Vigraha
    दुष्टं वृत्तं येषां ते duṣṭaṃ vṛttaṃ yeṣāṃ te
    Literally
    “those whose conduct is bad”
    In the verse
    ill-behaved, gone astray
Morphology & anvaya

  • कथम् katham

    कथम् ‘how?’ asks after their condition in general (‘how are they?’); the following किं नु … किं नु asks the narrower question of their conduct.

Anvaya · prose order

ते कथम्? मे सुताः सद्वृत्ताः किं नु, दुर्वृत्ताः किं नु?

te katham? me sutāḥ sadvṛttāḥ kiṃ nu, durvṛttāḥ kiṃ nu?

A short question (कथं ते) and a double question with किं नु … किं नु.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The merchant ends his answer with anxious questions about the very sons who robbed him. The king will ask next (1.27–28) why he still cares for them.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: he does not ask whether they regret what they did, only whether they are good. Attachment here takes the form of hope for those who caused the hurt.

rājovāca ||

rājā · uvāca

Translation

The king said:

In readable EnglishThe king said:

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • राजोवाच rājovāca → राजा + उवाच

    vowel sandhi (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • राजा rājā

    Nominative singular of the n-stem राजन्: the final n is dropped and the vowel lengthened (राजन् → राजा).

Anvaya · prose order

राजा उवाच।

rājā uvāca |

Subject and verb: a speaker label.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Suratha answers the merchant Samādhi, who has just told him (1.21–25) how his wife and sons took his wealth and drove him out, and how he still worries about them. The two exiles have met in the forest near the sage Medhas’s hermitage (1.17).

Verse 1.27

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

यैर्निरस्तो भवाँल्लुब्धैः पुत्रदारादिभिर्धनैः॥⁠२७⁠॥

yairnirasto bhavāँllubdhaiḥ putradārādibhirdhanaiḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

यैः · निरस्तः · भवान् · लुब्धैः · पुत्रदारादिभिः · धनैः

yaiḥ · nirastaḥ · bhavān · lubdhaiḥ · putradārādibhiḥ · dhanaiḥ

Word by word

  1. यैःyaiḥby whomrelative pronoun यद्, m. instr. pl.; agent of the passive participle निरस्तः; correlative तेषु in 1.28
  2. निरस्तःnirastaḥcast out, driven awayनिर् + √अस् (divādi, 4P ‘to throw’) + क्त (past passive participle), m. nom. sg.; predicate of भवान्
  3. भवान्bhavānyou, sirm. nom. sg. of भवत्, the respectful pronoun of address (construed with the third person)
  4. लुब्धैःlubdhaiḥgreedy√लुभ् (divādi, 4P ‘to covet’) + क्त, used as an adjective, m. instr. pl.; qualifies पुत्रदारादिभिः
  5. पुत्रदारादिभिःputradārādibhiḥby sons, wife and the restm. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to यैः
  6. धनैःdhanaiḥlit. ‘by riches’; here ‘for the sake of wealth’n. instr. pl. of धन; instrumental of cause (hetu)

Translation

Those greedy ones — sons, wife and the rest — by whom you were cast out on account of wealth,

In readable EnglishThose greedy ones — your sons, your wife and the rest — who drove you out for the sake of your wealth:

The sentence is completed in 1.28.

Textual verification / uncertain: धनैः: the instrumental plural is read here as cause (‘on account of wealth’). Some translators take it loosely as ‘(deprived) of your wealth’, echoing 1.22 (पुत्रैरादाय मे धनम्). The reading itself is not in doubt.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • यैर्निरस्तो yairnirasto → यैः + निरस्तः

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    After a vowel other than a/ā, the visarga (as रु) is sounded r before a voiced consonant: यैः → यैर् before n. The same change gives पुत्रदारादिभिर्धनैः.

  • निरस्तो भवाँल्लुब्धैः nirasto bhavāँllubdhaiḥ → निरस्तः + भवान् + लुब्धैः

    visarga sandhi; consonant sandhi (n + l) · हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87); तोर्लि (8.4.60)

    -aḥ before the voiced bh becomes -o. Then final n before l becomes a nasalised l: भवान् लुब्धैः → भवाँल्लुब्धैः. The Gita Press writes the nasal colour with candrabindu (ँ) on the vowel before the double l.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • पुत्रदारादिभिः putradārādibhiḥ

    bahuvrīhi containing an itaretara dvandva (पुत्रदार)

    Members
    पुत्र + दार + आदि
    Vigraha
    पुत्राश्च दाराश्च पुत्रदाराः; पुत्रदाराः आदयः येषां ते, तैः putrāśca dārāśca putradārāḥ; putradārāḥ ādayaḥ yeṣāṃ te, taiḥ
    Literally
    “those of whom sons and wife are the first”
    In the verse
    sons, wife and the other members of the household
Morphology & anvaya

  • निरस्तः nirastaḥ

    Past passive participle of निर् + √अस् ‘throw’: ‘thrown out’. With the instrumental यैः it makes a passive clause: ‘by whom you were cast out’.

  • भवान् bhavān

    The polite ‘you’: nominative of भवत्, a pronoun that takes the verb in the third person. Its final n meets the l of लुब्धैः and becomes a nasalised l (भवाँल्लुब्धैः).

  • धनैः dhanaiḥ

    Instrumental of cause: ‘because of (your) wealth’. The plural is idiomatic for ‘riches’. See Uncertain.

Anvaya · prose order

यैः लुब्धैः पुत्रदारादिभिः धनैः (हेतुभिः) भवान् निरस्तः, (तेषु …)

yaiḥ lubdhaiḥ putradārādibhiḥ dhanaiḥ (hetubhiḥ) bhavān nirastaḥ, (teṣu …)

A relative clause only: its correlative तेषु and the main verb come in the next half-verse (1.28).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king restates Samādhi’s own account (1.22: ‘cast out by sons and wife out of greed for wealth’). The question it leads to comes in the next half-verse.

Traditional interpretation

Read with 1.12–14, the question is ironic: Suratha has just been worrying, in the same way, about the kingdom, servants and elephant that were taken from him. He asks the merchant what he cannot yet answer for himself; he admits as much in 1.41–45.

Verse 1.28

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

तेषु किं भवतः स्नेहमनुबध्नाति मानसम्॥⁠२८⁠॥

teṣu kiṃ bhavataḥ snehamanubadhnāti mānasam ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

तेषु · किम् · भवतः · स्नेहम् · अनुबध्नाति · मानसम्

teṣu · kim · bhavataḥ · sneham · anubadhnāti · mānasam

Word by word

  1. तेषुteṣutoward thempronoun तद्, m. loc. pl. (locative of the object of feeling); correlative of यैः in 1.27
  2. किम्kimwhyindeclinable (interrogative adverb, the n. acc. of किम्)
  3. भवतःbhavataḥyourm. gen. sg. of भवत् (respectful ‘you’); qualifies मानसम्
  4. स्नेहम्snehamaffection, attachmentm. acc. sg. of स्नेह; object of अनुबध्नाति
  5. अनुबध्नातिanubadhnātibinds on, keeps formingअनु + √बन्ध् (kryādi, 9P ‘to bind’), laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  6. मानसम्mānasamthe mindn. nom. sg. of मानस; subject of अनुबध्नाति

Translation

— why does your mind bind affection to them?

In readable Englishwhy does your mind still hold to them in affection?

‘Still’ renders the force of the question in context; it is not a separate word.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • किं भवतः kiṃ bhavataḥ → किम् + भवतः

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra.

  • स्नेहमनुबध्नाति snehamanubadhnāti → स्नेहम् + अनुबध्नाति

    no change (m before a vowel) · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23) does not apply before a vowel

    Final m stays m before a vowel and is written together with the next word.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • अनुबध्नाति anubadhnāti

    Present of the ninth class: the root बन्ध् loses its nasal and takes the class sign ना (बध्ना-ति). With अनु: ‘to bind to, to attach’; स्नेहम् अनुबध्नाति ‘forms an attachment’.

  • मानसम् mānasam

    Taddhita from मनस् ‘mind’: मानस ‘belonging to the mind’, used as a noun for the mind itself.

Anvaya · prose order

भवतः मानसं तेषु स्नेहं किम् अनुबध्नाति?

bhavataḥ mānasaṃ teṣu snehaṃ kim anubadhnāti?

The main clause of the question begun in 1.27: subject मानसम्, object स्नेहम्, the locative तेषु for the persons loved.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king’s question: why love those who have wronged you? It is the question of the whole first carita, and the merchant will answer that he does not know (1.31–34).

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the question is easier to ask of another than of oneself. The text lets the king hear his own trouble in a stranger’s voice before he can name it.

Verse 1.30

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

एवमेतद्यथा प्राह भवानस्मद्गतं वचः॥⁠३०⁠॥

evametadyathā prāha bhavānasmadgataṃ vacaḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

एवम् · एतत् · यथा · प्राह · भवान् · अस्मद्गतम् · वचः

evam · etat · yathā · prāha · bhavān · asmadgatam · vacaḥ

Word by word

  1. एवम्evamso, just soindeclinable (adverb of manner); predicate of एतत्
  2. एतत्etatthisdemonstrative pronoun एतद्, n. nom. sg.; subject
  3. यथाyathāasindeclinable (relative adverb of manner)
  4. प्राहprāhasays, has saidप्र + आह; आह is the form substituted for √ब्रू (adādi, 2U ‘to speak’) in the present (laṭ), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada, with perfect-type endings
  5. भवान्bhavānyou, sirm. nom. sg. of भवत् (respectful ‘you’, with a third-person verb); subject of प्राह
  6. अस्मद्गतम्asmadgatamconcerning men. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies वचः
  7. वचःvacaḥword, what was saidn. acc. sg. of वचस् (s-stem); object of प्राह

Translation

This is so, as you, sir, have spoken the words concerning me.

In readable EnglishIt is just as you say about me.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • एवमेतद्यथा evametadyathā → एवम् + एतत् + यथा

    consonant sandhi (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    Final m stays m before the vowel e and is written joined; the final t of एतत् becomes d before the voiced y.

  • भवानस्मद्गतं bhavānasmadgataṃ → भवान् + अस्मद्गतम्

    no change (n before a vowel) · ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम् (8.3.32) does not apply

    Final n is doubled before a vowel only after a short vowel; after the long ā of भवान् it simply joins the next word.

  • अस्मद्गतं वचः asmadgataṃ vacaḥ → अस्मद्गतम् + वचः

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अस्मद्गतम् asmadgatam

    dvitīyā tatpuruṣa

    Members
    अस्मद् + गत
    Vigraha
    अस्मान् गतम् asmān gatam
    Literally
    “gone to us”
    In the verse
    about me, concerning my case
    Alternative
    Also glossed अस्मद्विषयकम् ‘having us as its subject’; the sense is the same. The plural stem अस्मद् is used of the one speaker, a usage the grammarians allow for the first person.
Morphology & anvaya

  • प्राह prāha

    आह looks like a perfect but is, for Pāṇini, a present: the first five present endings of √ब्रू are optionally replaced by perfect-type endings with आह for the root. With प्र: ‘says, declares’.

  • भवान् bhavān

    Nominative of भवत्, the pronoun of respect: ‘you’ in meaning, third person in grammar (प्राह, not a second-person form).

Anvaya · prose order

भवान् अस्मद्गतं वचः यथा प्राह, एतत् एवम् (अस्ति)।

bhavān asmadgataṃ vacaḥ yathā prāha, etat evam (asti) |

A relative clause of manner (यथा … प्राह) and a nominal main clause with the verb ‘is’ understood: एतत् एवम्.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Samādhi grants the king’s point at once: those he loves have treated him cruelly. What follows (1.31–34) is not a defence of them but a confession that his mind will not obey what he knows.

    “love of a father”
    In the verse
    the love owed to a father — the sons’ love for him
    Alternative
    Also read as a saptamī tatpuruṣa, पितरि स्नेहः ‘love toward the father’; the sense is the same. Read as ‘a father’s love (for his sons)’ it would not fit: the sons are the ones who cast it off.

  • धनलुब्धैः dhanalubdhaiḥ

    saptamī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    धन + लुब्ध
    Vigraha
    धने लुब्धाः, तैः dhane lubdhāḥ, taiḥ
    Literally
    “greedy in (the matter of) wealth”
    In the verse
    covetous of his money
    Alternative
    Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, धनस्य लुब्धाः; the sense is the same.
Morphology & anvaya

  • करोमि karomi

    Present of √कृ (stem करो- before the first-person ending -मि). In a question the present is deliberative: ‘what am I to do?’

  • संत्यज्य saṃtyajya

    Absolutive with ल्यप् (-य), the form used when the verb has a prefix (contrast त्यक्त्वा). Its subject is the agent of the main verb, here the kin (यैः).

  • निष्ठुरताम् niṣṭhuratām

    Abstract noun in -ता (taddhita तल्) from निष्ठुर ‘hard’. मनः निष्ठुरतां न बध्नाति: ‘the mind does not take on hardness’ — the merchant cannot make himself stop caring.

Anvaya · prose order

किं करोमि? मम मनः निष्ठुरतां न बध्नाति। यैः धनलुब्धैः पितृस्नेहं संत्यज्य (अहं) निराकृतः, …

kiṃ karomi? mama manaḥ niṣṭhuratāṃ na badhnāti | yaiḥ dhanalubdhaiḥ pitṛsnehaṃ saṃtyajya (ahaṃ) nirākṛtaḥ, …

A question, then a statement; the second line opens a relative clause (यैः … निराकृतः) whose correlative तेषु and main clause come in 1.32.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The merchant answers with a helpless question. He knows how he was treated and cannot stop loving: his mind refuses the hardness that reason would justify.

Traditional interpretation

The verb बन्ध् ‘to bind’ is the word the text will use for saṃsāra itself (संसारबन्ध, 1.58). Here it is turned around: the mind will not bind itself to hardness, because it is already bound by affection.

Verse 1.32

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

पतिस्वजनहार्दं च हार्दि तेष्वेव मे मनः।किमेतन्नाभिजानामि जानन्नपि महामते॥⁠३२⁠॥

patisvajanahārdaṃ ca hārdi teṣveva me manaḥ |kimetannābhijānāmi jānannapi mahāmate ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

पतिस्वजनहार्दम् · च · हार्दि · तेषु · एव · मे · मनःकिम् · एतत् · न · अभिजानामि · जानन् · अपि · महामते

patisvajanahārdam · ca · hārdi · teṣu · eva · me · manaḥkim · etat · na · abhijānāmi · jānan · api · mahāmate

Word by word

  1. पतिस्वजनहार्दम्patisvajanahārdamaffection for husband and kinsmann. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); second object of संत्यज्य in 1.31
  2. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  3. हार्दिhārdiloving, full of affectionn. nom. sg. of the adjective हार्दिन् (in-stem); predicate of मनः
  4. तेषुteṣutoward thempronoun तद्, m. loc. pl.; correlative of यैः in 1.31
  5. एवevastill, those very (people)indeclinable (emphatic particle), stressing तेषु
  6. मेmemyenclitic form of अस्मद्, gen. sg.
  7. मनःmanaḥmind, heartn. nom. sg. of मनस्; subject
  8. किम्kimwhatinterrogative pronoun किम्, n. nom. sg.; predicate of एतत्
  9. एतत्etatthisdemonstrative pronoun एतद्, n. nom. sg.
  10. नnanotindeclinable (negative particle)
  11. अभिजानामिabhijānāmiI understand, I see intoअभि + √ज्ञा (kryādi, 9U ‘to know’), laṭ (present), uttama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  12. जानन्jānanknowing√ज्ञा + शतृ (present participle), m. nom. sg.; agrees with the understood ‘I’
  13. अपिapieven thoughindeclinable (concessive particle, with the participle)
  14. महामतेmahāmateO wise onem. voc. sg. of महामति; compound (see Samāsa); addressed to the king

Translation

— and affection for husband and kinsman: toward those very ones my mind is loving. What this is I do not understand, though knowing, O great-minded one.

In readable Englishwho threw off all feeling for husband and kinsman — toward them, still, my heart is full of love. I know all this, wise king, and yet I cannot understand it.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तेष्वेव teṣveva → तेषु + एव

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Final u before a dissimilar vowel becomes v.

  • किमेतन्नाभिजानामि kimetannābhijānāmi → किम् + एतत् + न + अभिजानामि

    consonant sandhi (nasalisation); vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    Final t before the nasal n becomes n; then न + अभि- gives नाभि-. The m of किम् simply joins the vowel of एतत्.

  • जानन्नपि jānannapi → जानन् + अपि

    consonant sandhi (doubling of n) · ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम् (8.3.32)

    A final n after a short vowel is doubled before a vowel.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • पतिस्वजनहार्दम् patisvajanahārdam

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (objective genitive) containing an itaretara dvandva (पतिस्वजन)

    Members
    पति + स्वजन + हार्द
    Vigraha
    पतिश्च स्वजनश्च पतिस्वजनौ; पतिस्वजनयोः हार्दम्, तत् patiśca svajanaśca patisvajanau; patisvajanayoḥ hārdam, tat
    Literally
    “affection of (= toward) husband and kinsman”
    In the verse
    the love a wife owes her husband and kin owe a kinsman — which they too threw off
    Alternative
    स्वजन is itself a karmadhāraya, स्वः जनः ‘one’s own person, a kinsman’. The dvandva may also be taken as plural (पतिस्वजनाः).

  • महामते mahāmate

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    महत् + मति
    Vigraha
    महती मतिः यस्य सः, तत्सम्बोधने mahatī matiḥ yasya saḥ, tatsambodhane
    Literally
    “one whose understanding is great”
    In the verse
    a respectful address to the king
Morphology & anvaya

  • हार्दि hārdi

    Neuter nominative of हार्दिन् ‘having हार्द (affection)’, agreeing with मनः. The masculine nominative of the same word, हार्दी, comes in 1.43.

  • जानन् jānan

    Present participle of √ज्ञा (stem जानत्), nominative singular masculine. With अपि it is concessive: ‘though knowing’.

  • अभिजानामि abhijānāmi

    The prefix अभि sharpens ‘know’ to ‘understand, recognise’: the merchant knows the facts (जानन्) but cannot see into them (न अभिजानामि).

Anvaya · prose order

(यैः) पतिस्वजनहार्दं च (संत्यज्य अहं निराकृतः), तेषु एव मे मनः हार्दि (अस्ति)। महामते, जानन् अपि एतत् किं (इति) न अभिजानामि।

(yaiḥ) patisvajanahārdaṃ ca (saṃtyajya ahaṃ nirākṛtaḥ), teṣu eva me manaḥ hārdi (asti) | mahāmate, jānan api etat kiṃ (iti) na abhijānāmi |

The first half closes the relative sentence of 1.31: पतिस्वजनहार्दम् is a second object of संत्यज्य, and तेषु … हार्दि is the main clause. The second half is a new sentence: an indirect question (किम् एतत्) governed by न अभिजानामि.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The merchant states the paradox the sage will be asked to explain: he knows (जानन्) and yet does not understand (न अभिजानामि). The facts are clear to him; his heart does not follow them.

Traditional interpretation

This is the condition Medhas will name in 1.55: Mahāmāyā draws away the minds even of those who know (ज्ञानिनामपि चेतांसि). Knowledge of the facts is not freedom from delusion.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the text separates information from understanding. The merchant is not ignorant; he is attached — and he is honest enough to say that the two are different.

Verse 1.33

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

यत्प्रेमप्रवणं चित्तं विगुणेष्वपि बन्धुषु।तेषां कृते मे निःश्वासो दौर्मनस्यं च जायते॥⁠३३⁠॥

yatpremapravaṇaṃ cittaṃ viguṇeṣvapi bandhuṣu |teṣāṃ kṛte me niḥśvāso daurmanasyaṃ ca jāyate ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

यत् · प्रेमप्रवणम् · चित्तम् · विगुणेषु · अपि · बन्धुषुतेषाम् · कृते · मे · निःश्वासः · दौर्मनस्यम् · च · जायते

yat · premapravaṇam · cittam · viguṇeṣu · api · bandhuṣuteṣām · kṛte · me · niḥśvāsaḥ · daurmanasyam · ca · jāyate

Word by word

  1. यत्yatthat (namely)indeclinable use of यद् (n.), a conjunction introducing what एतत् in 1.32 refers to
  2. प्रेमप्रवणम्premapravaṇaminclined to loven. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate of चित्तम्
  3. चित्तम्cittamthe mind, the heartn. nom. sg. of चित्त; subject
  4. विगुणेषुviguṇeṣuworthless, without virtuem. loc. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies बन्धुषु
  5. अपिapievenindeclinable (particle)
  6. बन्धुषुbandhuṣutoward kinsfolkm. loc. pl. of बन्धु (u-stem); locative of the object of feeling
  7. तेषाम्teṣāmtheirpronoun तद्, m. gen. pl.; governed by कृते
  8. कृतेkṛtefor the sake of, on account ofindeclinable (the loc. sg. of कृत, used as a postposition with the genitive)
  9. मेmein me, myenclitic form of अस्मद्, gen. sg.
  10. निःश्वासःniḥśvāsaḥsighingm. nom. sg. of निःश्वास (निस् + √श्वस् + घञ्); subject of जायते
  11. दौर्मनस्यम्daurmanasyamdejection, heaviness of heartn. nom. sg. of दौर्मनस्य (abstract noun from दुर्मनस्); second subject of जायते
  12. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  13. जायतेjāyatearises√जन् (divādi, 4Ā ‘to be born’), laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada

Translation

— that the mind is inclined to love even toward worthless kinsfolk; that on their account sighing and dejection arise in me.

In readable English— that my heart leans in love toward kinsfolk who have shown no virtue, and that I sigh and grieve for their sake.

‘my’ with heart is supplied from मे in the second line; the verse explains the ‘this’ (एतत्) of 1.32.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • विगुणेष्वपि viguṇeṣvapi → विगुणेषु + अपि

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Final u before a dissimilar vowel becomes v.

  • निःश्वासो दौर्मनस्यं niḥśvāso daurmanasyaṃ → निःश्वासः + दौर्मनस्यम्

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced d becomes -o. The final m of दौर्मनस्यम् becomes anusvāra before च (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

  • यत्प्रेमप्रवणं yatpremapravaṇaṃ → यत् + प्रेमप्रवणम्

    no change (t before an unvoiced stop) · खरि च (8.4.55)

    The final t stays unvoiced before p; the two words are only written together.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • प्रेमप्रवणम् premapravaṇam

    saptamī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    प्रेमन् + प्रवण
    Vigraha
    प्रेम्णि प्रवणम् premṇi pravaṇam
    Literally
    “sloping toward love”
    In the verse
    naturally given to love
    Alternative
    Also read as a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa, प्रेम्णा प्रवणम् ‘bent by love’; the sense is close. प्रेमन् drops its final n as the first member of a compound.

  • विगुणेषु viguṇeṣu

    bahuvrīhi (prādi: the prefix वि stands for विगत)

    Members
    वि + गुण
    Vigraha
    विगताः गुणाः येभ्यः ते, तेषु vigatāḥ guṇāḥ yebhyaḥ te, teṣu
    Literally
    “from whom virtues have gone”
    In the verse
    worthless, who have behaved without virtue
Morphology & anvaya

  • जायते jāyate

    Present of √जन् in the fourth class (stem जाय-), ātmanepada. It is singular with two subjects joined by च (निःश्वासः, दौर्मनस्यम्), agreeing with the nearer or taking the pair as one experience.

  • दौर्मनस्यम् daurmanasyam

    Abstract noun with vṛddhi of the first syllable (taddhita ष्यञ्): दुर्मनस् ‘ill-minded, dejected’ → दौर्मनस्य ‘dejection’.

  • कृते kṛte

    Locative of कृत ‘done’, fixed as a postposition: तेषां कृते ‘for their sake, on their account’.

Anvaya · prose order

(एतत् किम्,) यत् चित्तं विगुणेषु अपि बन्धुषु प्रेमप्रवणम् (अस्ति), तेषां कृते मे निःश्वासः दौर्मनस्यं च जायते?

(etat kim,) yat cittaṃ viguṇeṣu api bandhuṣu premapravaṇam (asti), teṣāṃ kṛte me niḥśvāsaḥ daurmanasyaṃ ca jāyate?

A यत् clause (‘that …’) spelling out the एतत् of 1.32: two statements, the first nominal (verb ‘is’ understood), the second with जायते.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The merchant names what he cannot understand: love that persists toward the unworthy, and the sighing and gloom it brings. The symptoms are bodily (निःश्वास) and mental (दौर्मनस्य).

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the verse does not call the love wrong. It reports, without judgement, that love does not wait for its object to deserve it — which is both the merchant’s pain and, later in the text, the shape of the Goddess’s own compassion.

Verse 1.34

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

करोमि किं यन्न मनस्तेष्वप्रीतिषु निष्ठुरम्॥⁠३४⁠॥

karomi kiṃ yanna manasteṣvaprītiṣu niṣṭhuram ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

करोमि · किम् · यत् · न · मनः · तेषु · अप्रीतिषु · निष्ठुरम्

karomi · kim · yat · na · manaḥ · teṣu · aprītiṣu · niṣṭhuram

Word by word

  1. करोमिkaromiam I to do√कृ (tanādi, 8U), laṭ (present), uttama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  2. किम्kimwhatinterrogative pronoun किम्, n. acc. sg.; object of करोमि
  3. यत्yatsince, seeing thatindeclinable use of यद् (n.), a causal conjunction
  4. नnanotindeclinable (negative particle)
  5. मनःmanaḥthe mind, the heartn. nom. sg. of मनस्; subject
  6. तेषुteṣutoward thempronoun तद्, m. loc. pl.
  7. अप्रीतिषुaprītiṣuwho are without lovem. loc. pl. of अप्रीति (as an adjective); compound (see Samāsa); qualifies तेषु
  8. निष्ठुरम्niṣṭhuramhardn. nom. sg. of निष्ठुर; predicate of मनः

Translation

What am I to do, since the mind is not hard toward those loveless ones?

In readable EnglishWhat am I to do? My heart will not harden against those who have no love for me.

‘for me’ makes explicit whom the kin do not love; the compound says only ‘without love’.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • यन्न yanna → यत् + न

    consonant sandhi (nasalisation) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45)

    Final t before the nasal n becomes n.

  • मनस्तेष्वप्रीतिषु manasteṣvaprītiṣu → मनः + तेषु + अप्रीतिषु

    visarga sandhi; vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34); इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Visarga before t becomes s; final u before a becomes v.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अप्रीतिषु aprītiṣu

    bahuvrīhi (nañ-bahuvrīhi)

    Members
    अ + प्रीति
    Vigraha
    न विद्यते प्रीतिः येषां ते, तेषु na vidyate prītiḥ yeṣāṃ te, teṣu
    Literally
    “those for whom there is no love”
    In the verse
    the unloving kin
    Alternative
    Also possible as a nañ tatpuruṣa noun, न प्रीतिः ‘absence of love’, in the locative plural: ‘amid (their) unkindnesses’. The bahuvrīhi fits better, since the word stands beside तेषु as its qualifier.
Morphology & anvaya

  • करोमि karomi

    Deliberative present, as in 1.31: करोमि किम् here answers किं करोमि there, so the merchant’s reply begins and ends with the same helpless question.

  • निष्ठुरम् niṣṭhuram

    The adjective whose abstract noun (निष्ठुरता) appeared in 1.31; here neuter, agreeing with मनः.

Anvaya · prose order

किं करोमि, यत् मनः तेषु अप्रीतिषु निष्ठुरं न (भवति)?

kiṃ karomi, yat manaḥ teṣu aprītiṣu niṣṭhuraṃ na (bhavati)?

A question with a causal यत् clause; the verb ‘is’ (भवति) is understood.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The merchant closes his reply where he began (1.31): ‘What can I do?’ The repetition marks the end of his speech and of his own resources; the next step is to go to the sage.

Speaker

mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ||

  1. मार्कण्डेयःmārkaṇḍeyaḥMārkaṇḍeya, the sagem. nom. sg. of मार्कण्डेय (taddhita: ‘descendant of Mṛkaṇḍu’); subject of उवाच

  • मार्कण्डेय उवाच mārkaṇḍeya uvāca → मार्कण्डेयः + उवाच

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17), लोपः शाकल्यस्य (8.3.19)

    As in 1.1: the y that replaces the visarga before a vowel is dropped, and the vowels stand apart.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

Anvaya · prose order

मार्कण्डेयः उवाच।

mārkaṇḍeyaḥ uvāca |

Subject and verb: a speaker label.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The frame narrator, Mārkaṇḍeya, speaking to his pupil Krauṣṭuki, takes up the story again: the conversation of the king and the merchant is over, and he tells how the two went together to the sage Medhas.

Verse 1.36

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

tatastau sahitau vipra taṃ muniṃ samupasthitau ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

ततः · तौ · सहितौ · विप्र · तम् · मुनिम् · समुपस्थितौ

tataḥ · tau · sahitau · vipra · tam · munim · samupasthitau

Word by word

  1. ततःtataḥthenindeclinable (adverb of time, the ablative of तद् fixed as a particle)
  2. तौtauthose twopronoun तद्, m. nom. du.; subject
  3. सहितौsahitautogetheradjective सहित ‘accompanied, joined’, m. nom. du.; qualifies तौ
  4. विप्रvipraO brahminm. voc. sg. of विप्र; Mārkaṇḍeya addresses his listener
  5. तम्tamthatpronoun तद्, m. acc. sg.; qualifies मुनिम्
  6. मुनिम्munimsagem. acc. sg. of मुनि (i-stem); object of समुपस्थितौ
  7. समुपस्थितौsamupasthitauapproachedसम् + उप + √स्था (bhvādi, 1P ‘to stand’) + क्त (past participle in active sense), m. nom. du.; predicate of तौ

Translation

Then, O brahmin, those two together approached that sage —

In readable EnglishThen, O brahmin, the two went together to the sage:

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • ततस्तौ tatastau → ततः + तौ

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

  • तं मुनिं समुपस्थितौ taṃ muniṃ samupasthitau → तम् + मुनिम् + समुपस्थितौ

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra, twice.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • समुपस्थितौ samupasthitau

    Past participle of √स्था with सम् + उप. With verbs of motion and standing the क्त participle is active and may take an object: तं मुनिं समुपस्थितौ ‘(they) approached the sage’. It serves as the finite verb.

Anvaya · prose order

(हे) विप्र, ततः सहितौ तौ तं मुनिं समुपस्थितौ।

(he) vipra, tataḥ sahitau tau taṃ muniṃ samupasthitau |

Subject (तौ, with सहितौ), object (तं मुनिम्), and the participle समुपस्थितौ as the verb; विप्र is a vocative aside. The two are named in 1.37.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king and the merchant go together to Medhas. The vocative विप्र is Mārkaṇḍeya’s address to his listener in the frame, the brahmin Krauṣṭuki — a reminder that the whole story is being told to him.

Verse 1.37

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

समाधिर्नाम वैश्योऽसौ स च पार्थिवसत्तमः।कृत्वा तु तौ यथान्यायं यथार्हं तेन संविदम्॥⁠३७⁠॥

samādhirnāma vaiśyo'sau sa ca pārthivasattamaḥ |kṛtvā tu tau yathānyāyaṃ yathārhaṃ tena saṃvidam ||

Word by word

Translation

— that merchant named Samādhi and that best of kings. And the two, having made with him, as was proper and as was fitting, an exchange of greetings,

In readable Englishthe merchant Samādhi and the noble king. When they had greeted him with due courtesy, as was fitting,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • समाधिर्नाम samādhirnāma → समाधिः + नाम

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    After i the visarga (as रु) is sounded r before the voiced n.

  • वैश्योऽसौ vaiśyo'sau → वैश्यः + असौ

    visarga sandhi with pūrvarūpa · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a becomes -o, and the following a is absorbed (avagraha).

  • स च sa ca → सः + च

    visarga sandhi (special rule for सः) · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132)

    The visarga of सः is dropped before a consonant.

  • यथान्यायं यथार्हं yathānyāyaṃ yathārhaṃ → यथा + न्यायम्; यथा + अर्हम्

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha); anusvāra · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101); मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    ā + a → ā in यथार्हम्; each final m becomes anusvāra before the next consonant.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • पार्थिवसत्तमः pārthivasattamaḥ

    saptamī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    पार्थिव + सत्तम
    Vigraha
    पार्थिवेषु सत्तमः pārthiveṣu sattamaḥ
    Literally
    “the best among kings”
    In the verse
    the noble king Suratha
    Alternative
    Superlatives of selection are not compounded as genitives (‘best of kings’); the grammarians resolve them with the locative of the group.

  • यथान्यायम् yathānyāyam

    avyayībhāva

    Members
    यथा + न्याय
    Vigraha
    न्यायम् अनतिक्रम्य nyāyam anatikramya
    Literally
    “not going beyond what is proper”
    In the verse
    in due form

  • यथार्हम् yathārham

    avyayībhāva

    Members
    यथा + अर्ह
    Vigraha
    अर्हम् अनतिक्रम्य arham anatikramya
    Literally
    “not going beyond what is fitting”
    In the verse
    as befitted the sage
Morphology & anvaya

  • असौ asau

    Nominative singular masculine (and feminine) of अदस् ‘that (yonder)’, the pronoun of distance.

  • कृत्वा kṛtvā

    Absolutive of √कृ (unprefixed, so -त्वा): ‘having made’. Its subject तौ is the subject of the main verb चक्रतुः in 1.38.

  • संविदम् saṃvidam

    Accusative of संविद्, from सम् + √विद् ‘to know together’: agreement, mutual understanding; with कृ ‘to come to terms, exchange courtesies’.

Anvaya · prose order

समाधिः नाम असौ वैश्यः सः पार्थिवसत्तमः च। तौ तु तेन यथान्यायं यथार्हं संविदं कृत्वा, (उपविष्टौ …)

samādhiḥ nāma asau vaiśyaḥ saḥ pārthivasattamaḥ ca | tau tu tena yathānyāyaṃ yathārhaṃ saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā, (upaviṣṭau …)

The first line names the two (in apposition to तौ of 1.36). The second line opens a new sentence with an absolutive clause; its main verb (चक्रतुः) is in 1.38.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The two exiles are named side by side and come before the sage in due form. The courtesies are not skipped: the teaching that follows begins with the proper approach of the pupil.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the merchant’s name, Samādhi, is the word for meditative absorption. The text does not comment on it, but at its end (13.15ff) it is he who asks for knowledge rather than a kingdom.

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh

उपविष्टौ कथाः काश्चिच्चक्रतुर्वैश्यपार्थिवौ॥⁠३८⁠॥

upaviṣṭau kathāḥ kāściccakraturvaiśyapārthivau ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

उपविष्टौ · कथाः · काश्चित् · चक्रतुः · वैश्यपार्थिवौ

upaviṣṭau · kathāḥ · kāścit · cakratuḥ · vaiśyapārthivau

Word by word

  1. उपविष्टौupaviṣṭauseated, having sat downउप + √विश् (tudādi, 6P ‘to enter’) + क्त (past participle in active sense), m. nom. du.
  2. कथाःkathāḥtalks, conversationf. acc. pl. of कथा; object of चक्रतुः
  3. काश्चित्kāścitsomeindefinite pronoun किम् + चित्, f. acc. pl.; qualifies कथाः
  4. चक्रतुःcakratuḥ(they two) made, held√कृ (tanādi, 8U), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa dvivacana, parasmaipada
  5. वैश्यपार्थिवौvaiśyapārthivauthe merchant and the kingm. nom. du.; compound (see Samāsa); subject

Translation

— seated, the merchant and the king held some talks.

In readable Englishthe merchant and the king sat down and spoke with him a while.

‘with him’ is carried over from तेन in 1.37.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • काश्चिच्चक्रतुर् kāściccakratur → काश्चित् + चक्रतुः

    consonant sandhi (palatalisation); visarga sandhi · स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40); ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    Final t before c becomes c. The visarga of चक्रतुः after u is sounded r before the voiced v of वैश्य-.

  • काश्चिच् kāścic → काः + चित् (before च-)

    visarga sandhi inside the indefinite pronoun · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    The visarga of काः becomes s before c, and the s becomes ś next to the palatal: काः + चित् → काश्चित्, whose t then becomes c before चक्रतुः.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • वैश्यपार्थिवौ vaiśyapārthivau

    itaretara dvandva

    Members
    वैश्य + पार्थिव
    Vigraha
    वैश्यश्च पार्थिवश्च vaiśyaśca pārthivaśca
    Literally
    “the merchant and the king”
    In the verse
    Samādhi and Suratha, named as a pair
Morphology & anvaya

  • चक्रतुः cakratuḥ

    Perfect of √कृ, third person dual: reduplication च (k → c) + क्र + the dual ending -अतुः.

  • उपविष्टौ upaviṣṭau

    Past participle of उप + √विश् ‘to sit down’ (श् + त → ष्ट), active in sense: ‘having seated themselves’.

  • काश्चित् kāścit

    The indefinite pronoun: a form of किम् with the particle चित् (‘some’). It is one word and declines in its first part (कश्चित्, काश्चित्, केचित्).

Anvaya · prose order

(तौ) वैश्यपार्थिवौ उपविष्टौ (सन्तौ) काश्चित् कथाः चक्रतुः।

(tau) vaiśyapārthivau upaviṣṭau (santau) kāścit kathāḥ cakratuḥ |

The main clause of the sentence begun in 1.37: subject वैश्यपार्थिवौ, participle उपविष्टौ, object कथाः with काश्चित्, verb चक्रतुः.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The scene is set for the teaching: the two are seated before the sage and the conversation begins. The king’s question follows.

राजोवाच॥⁠३९⁠॥

rājovāca ||

    ā + u → o, as in 1.26.

राजा उवाच।

rājā uvāca |

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Verse 1.40

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

भगवंस्त्वामहं प्रष्टुमिच्छाम्येकं वदस्व तत्॥⁠४०⁠॥

bhagavaṃstvāmahaṃ praṣṭumicchāmyekaṃ vadasva tat ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

भगवन् · त्वाम् · अहम् · प्रष्टुम् · इच्छामि · एकम् · वदस्व · तत्

bhagavan · tvām · aham · praṣṭum · icchāmi · ekam · vadasva · tat

Word by word

  1. भगवन्bhagavanO revered onem. voc. sg. of भगवत्; addressed to the sage
  2. त्वाम्tvāmyousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, acc. sg.; object of प्रष्टुम्
  3. अहम्ahamIfirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, nom. sg.; subject of इच्छामि
  4. प्रष्टुम्praṣṭumto ask√प्रच्छ् (tudādi, 6P ‘to ask’) + तुमुन् (infinitive)
  5. इच्छामिicchāmiI wish√इष् (tudādi, 6P ‘to wish’), laṭ (present), uttama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  6. एकम्ekamone thingn. acc. sg. of एक; second object of प्रष्टुम् (verbs of asking take two accusatives)
  7. वदस्वvadasvatell√वद् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to speak’), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada
  8. तत्tatthatpronoun तद्, n. acc. sg.; object of वदस्व

Translation

Revered one, I wish to ask you one thing; tell (me) that.

In readable EnglishRevered sir, there is one thing I wish to ask you. Please explain it to me.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • भगवंस्त्वामहं bhagavaṃstvāmahaṃ → भगवन् + त्वाम् + अहम्

    consonant sandhi (n before t) · नश्छव्यप्रशान् (8.3.7)

    Final n before t becomes ṃs (anusvāra + s): भगवन् त्वाम् → भगवंस्त्वाम्. The m of त्वाम् joins the vowel of अहम्.

  • प्रष्टुमिच्छाम्येकं praṣṭumicchāmyekaṃ → प्रष्टुम् + इच्छामि + एकम्

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Final i before e becomes y; the m of प्रष्टुम् joins the following vowel.

  • एकं वदस्व ekaṃ vadasva → एकम् + वदस्व

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • प्रष्टुम् praṣṭum

    Infinitive of √प्रच्छ्: the root-final छ् becomes ष् before त्, which becomes ट् (प्रच्छ् + तुम् → प्रष्टुम्).

  • वदस्व vadasva

    Imperative ātmanepada of √वद्, a root normally parasmaipada. Pāṇini allows the ātmanepada of वद् in certain senses, among them speaking with knowledge or expertise; here it suits a request for instruction. It is also common in epic usage.

  • भगवन् bhagavan

    Vocative of भगवत् (‘possessed of fortune, revered’), the -vat stem: nominative भगवान्, vocative भगवन्.

Anvaya · prose order

भगवन्, अहं त्वाम् एकं प्रष्टुम् इच्छामि; तत् वदस्व।

bhagavan, ahaṃ tvām ekaṃ praṣṭum icchāmi; tat vadasva |

Two clauses: the wish to ask (इच्छामि with the infinitive प्रष्टुम् and its two objects त्वाम्, एकम्), and the imperative वदस्व with तत्.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king formally asks to put a question. After the approach (1.36–38) comes the request, and then the question itself (1.41–45).

Traditional interpretation

The shape is that of a classical teaching dialogue: a pupil who has come with due courtesy asks one question, and the teacher’s answer becomes the text. The rest of the Devī Māhātmya unfolds as Medhas’s answer.

Verse 1.41

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

दुःखाय यन्मे मनसः स्वचित्तायत्ततां विना।ममत्वं गतराज्यस्य राज्याङ्गेष्वखिलेष्वपि॥⁠४१⁠॥

duḥkhāya yanme manasaḥ svacittāyattatāṃ vinā |mamatvaṃ gatarājyasya rājyāṅgeṣvakhileṣvapi ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

दुःखाय · यत् · मे · मनसः · स्वचित्तायत्तताम् · विनाममत्वम् · गतराज्यस्य · राज्याङ्गेषु · अखिलेषु · अपि

duḥkhāya · yat · me · manasaḥ · svacittāyattatām · vināmamatvam · gatarājyasya · rājyāṅgeṣu · akhileṣu · api

Word by word

  1. दुःखायduḥkhāyato the grief (of), so as to painn. dat. sg. of दुःख; dative of result
  2. यत्yatthatindeclinable use of यद् (n.), a conjunction; the clause it opens is taken up by एतत् in 1.42
  3. मेmeof me, in meenclitic form of अस्मद्, gen. sg.; possessor of ममत्वम्, and qualified by गतराज्यस्य
  4. मनसःmanasaḥof the mindn. gen. sg. of मनस्; with दुःखाय
  5. स्वचित्तायत्तताम्svacittāyattatāmdependence on one’s own mind, being under one’s own controlf. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); governed by विना
  6. विनाvināwithout, apart fromindeclinable (postposition, with the accusative)
  7. ममत्वम्mamatvamthe sense of ‘mine’, possessivenessn. nom. sg. of ममत्व (abstract noun from मम ‘mine’); subject, with ‘is’ understood
  8. गतराज्यस्यgatarājyasyawhose kingdom is gonem. gen. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); agrees with मे
  9. राज्याङ्गेषुrājyāṅgeṣutoward the limbs of the kingdomn. loc. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); locative of the object of ममत्व
  10. अखिलेषुakhileṣualladjective अखिल, n. loc. pl.; qualifies राज्याङ्गेषु
  11. अपिapievenindeclinable (particle)

Translation

That — to the grief of my mind, without (its) being under the control of my own mind — there is in me, whose kingdom is gone, a sense of ‘mine’ even toward all the limbs of the kingdom,

In readable EnglishMy kingdom is gone, yet I still feel that every part of it is mine — against my own will, and to my mind’s distress,

The Sanskrit is a ‘that …’ clause completed by ‘what is this?’ in 1.42; the translation makes it a statement. ‘Against my own will’ renders स्वचित्तायत्ततां विना.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • यन्मे yanme → यत् + मे

    consonant sandhi (nasalisation) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45)

    Final t before the nasal m becomes n.

  • राज्याङ्गेष्वखिलेष्वपि rājyāṅgeṣvakhileṣvapi → राज्याङ्गेषु + अखिलेषु + अपि

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Final u before a becomes v, twice.

  • स्वचित्तायत्ततां svacittāyattatāṃ → स्वचित्त + आयत्तताम्

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + ā → ā. The same joining inside राज्याङ्गेषु (राज्य + अङ्ग).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • स्वचित्तायत्तताम् svacittāyattatām

    saptamī tatpuruṣa (स्वचित्तायत्त) containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (स्वचित्त), made abstract with -ता

    Members
    स्व + चित्त + आयत्त + ता
    Vigraha
    स्वस्य चित्तं स्वचित्तम्; स्वचित्ते आयत्तः स्वचित्तायत्तः; तस्य भावः स्वचित्तायत्तता, ताम् svasya cittaṃ svacittam; svacitte āyattaḥ svacittāyattaḥ; tasya bhāvaḥ svacittāyattatā, tām
    Literally
    “the state of being dependent on one’s own mind”
    In the verse
    self-control; विना ‘without’ it means ‘beyond my control, against my will’

  • गतराज्यस्य gatarājyasya

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    गत + राज्य
    Vigraha
    गतं राज्यं यस्य सः, तस्य gataṃ rājyaṃ yasya saḥ, tasya
    Literally
    “of one whose kingdom has gone”
    In the verse
    of me, the dispossessed king

  • राज्याङ्गेषु rājyāṅgeṣu

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    राज्य + अङ्ग
    Vigraha
    राज्यस्य अङ्गानि, तेषु rājyasya aṅgāni, teṣu
    Literally
    “in the limbs of the kingdom”
    In the verse
    every part of the realm he once ruled
Morphology & anvaya

  • ममत्वम् mamatvam

    A noun built on an inflected form: the genitive मम ‘of me, mine’ + the abstract suffix -त्व. ‘Mine-ness’: the feeling that something belongs to me. The same idea returns as ममता in 1.53.

  • दुःखाय duḥkhāya

    Dative of result: ‘for the grief of (my) mind’, i.e. so that it pains me.

  • स्वचित्तायत्तताम् svacittāyattatām

    Abstract noun in -ता on a compound: the whole phrase ‘dependent on one’s own mind’ is turned into a state, then governed by विना.

Anvaya · prose order

यत् गतराज्यस्य मे अखिलेषु अपि राज्याङ्गेषु ममत्वं (अस्ति), (मम) मनसः दुःखाय, स्वचित्तायत्ततां विना, …

yat gatarājyasya me akhileṣu api rājyāṅgeṣu mamatvaṃ (asti), (mama) manasaḥ duḥkhāya, svacittāyattatāṃ vinā, …

A यत् clause (‘that …’), nominal, with ‘is’ understood; its subject is ममत्वम्. It is taken up by किम् एतत् in 1.42.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Now the king speaks of himself. He asked the merchant why he still loved those who had wronged him (1.27–28); here he admits the same bondage: he has lost his kingdom and cannot stop feeling it is his.

Traditional interpretation

‘Limbs of the kingdom’ is a term of Indian political thought, where a state has seven limbs: the king, ministers, territory, fort, treasury, army and ally. The king’s earlier worries (1.12–14) touch several of them: his city, his servants, his elephant, his treasury.

Verse 1.42

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

जानतोऽपि यथाज्ञस्य किमेतन्मुनिसत्तम।अयं च निकृतः पुत्रैर्दारैर्भृत्यैस्तथोज्झितः॥⁠४२⁠॥

jānato'pi yathājñasya kimetanmunisattama |ayaṃ ca nikṛtaḥ putrairdārairbhṛtyaistathojjhitaḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

जानतः · अपि · यथा · अज्ञस्य · किम् · एतत् · मुनिसत्तमअयम् · च · निकृतः · पुत्रैः · दारैः · भृत्यैः · तथा · उज्झितः

jānataḥ · api · yathā · ajñasya · kim · etat · munisattamaayam · ca · nikṛtaḥ · putraiḥ · dāraiḥ · bhṛtyaiḥ · tathā · ujjhitaḥ

Word by word

  1. जानतःjānataḥknowing√ज्ञा (kryādi, 9U) + शतृ (present participle), m. gen. sg.; agrees with मे in 1.41
  2. अपिapieven thoughindeclinable (concessive particle)
  3. यथाyathāas, just likeindeclinable (adverb of comparison)
  4. अज्ञस्यajñasyaof one who does not knowm. gen. sg. of अज्ञ; compound (see Samāsa)
  5. किम्kimwhatinterrogative pronoun किम्, n. nom. sg.; predicate
  6. एतत्etatthisdemonstrative pronoun एतद्, n. nom. sg.; subject; refers back to the यत् clause of 1.41
  7. मुनिसत्तमmunisattamaO best of sagesm. voc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)
  8. अयम्ayamthis man (the merchant)demonstrative pronoun इदम्, m. nom. sg.; subject
  9. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  10. निकृतःnikṛtaḥwronged, humiliatedनि + √कृ (tanādi, 8U) + क्त (past passive participle), m. nom. sg.
  11. पुत्रैःputraiḥby sonsm. instr. pl. of पुत्र; agent
  12. दारैःdāraiḥby his wifem. instr. pl. of दार (always masculine plural, ‘wife’); agent
  13. भृत्यैःbhṛtyaiḥby servantsm. instr. pl. of भृत्य; agent
  14. तथाtathālikewise, and alsoindeclinable (adverb)

Translation

— (in me,) though knowing, as in one who does not know: what is this, O best of sages? And this man has been wronged by sons, wife and servants, and likewise abandoned,

In readable Englishthough I know better, as if I did not. What is this, best of sages? And this man too has been wronged and cast off by his sons, his wife and his servants,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • जानतोऽपि jānato'pi → जानतः + अपि

    visarga sandhi with pūrvarūpa · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a becomes -o and the a is absorbed (avagraha).

  • यथाज्ञस्य yathājñasya → यथा + अज्ञस्य

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    ā + a → ā. Read as two words: ‘as of one who does not know’.

  • किमेतन्मुनिसत्तम kimetanmunisattama → किम् + एतत् + मुनिसत्तम

    consonant sandhi (nasalisation) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45)

    Final t before m becomes n.

  • पुत्रैर्दारैर्भृत्यैस्तथोज्झितः putrairdārairbhṛtyaistathojjhitaḥ → पुत्रैः + दारैः + भृत्यैः + तथा + उज्झितः

    visarga sandhi; vowel sandhi (guṇa) · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66); विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34); आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aiḥ is sounded -air before the voiced d and bh, and becomes -ais before t; तथा + उज्झितः gives तथोज्झितः.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अज्ञस्य ajñasya

    nañ tatpuruṣa

    Members
    अ + ज्ञ
    Vigraha
    न ज्ञः अज्ञः, तस्य na jñaḥ ajñaḥ, tasya
    Literally
    “not a knower”
    In the verse
    an ignorant man; ज्ञ ‘knowing’ is itself a kṛt noun from √ज्ञा

  • मुनिसत्तम munisattama

    saptamī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    मुनि + सत्तम
    Vigraha
    मुनिषु सत्तमः, तत्सम्बोधने muniṣu sattamaḥ, tatsambodhane
    Literally
    “best among sages”
    In the verse
    a respectful address to Medhas (compare पार्थिवसत्तमः, 1.37)
Morphology & anvaya

  • जानतः jānataḥ

    Genitive of the present participle जानत्, agreeing with मे in 1.41: ‘of me, though knowing’. It echoes the merchant’s जानन्नपि (1.32).

  • दारैः dāraiḥ

    दार ‘wife’ is masculine and used only in the plural; one wife is meant.

  • निकृतः nikṛtaḥ

    Past participle of नि + √कृ ‘to bring down, to wrong’; with उज्झितः the two participles describe the merchant, the verb ‘is’ understood.

Anvaya · prose order

(हे) मुनिसत्तम, जानतः अपि (मे) अज्ञस्य यथा (ममत्वम्) — एतत् किम्? अयं च पुत्रैः दारैः भृत्यैः निकृतः तथा उज्झितः, …

(he) munisattama, jānataḥ api (me) ajñasya yathā (mamatvam) — etat kim? ayaṃ ca putraiḥ dāraiḥ bhṛtyaiḥ nikṛtaḥ tathā ujjhitaḥ, …

The first line closes the king’s own case (‘though knowing, as if not knowing’) and asks ‘what is this?’. The second opens the merchant’s case, continued in 1.43.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king states his own paradox in the words of the merchant: knowing, yet behaving like one who does not know (compare जानन्नपि, 1.32). Then he presents the merchant’s case beside his own.

Verse 1.43

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

स्वजनेन च संत्यक्तस्तेषु हार्दी तथाप्यति।एवमेष तथाहं च द्वावप्यत्यन्तदुःखितौ॥⁠४३⁠॥

svajanena ca saṃtyaktasteṣu hārdī tathāpyati |evameṣa tathāhaṃ ca dvāvapyatyantaduḥkhitau ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

स्वजनेन · च · संत्यक्तः · तेषु · हार्दी · तथा · अपि · अतिएवम् · एषः · तथा · अहम् · च · द्वौ · अपि · अत्यन्तदुःखितौ

svajanena · ca · saṃtyaktaḥ · teṣu · hārdī · tathā · api · atievam · eṣaḥ · tathā · aham · ca · dvau · api · atyantaduḥkhitau

Word by word

  1. स्वजनेनsvajanenaby his own people, his kinm. instr. sg. of स्वजन (used collectively); agent
  2. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  3. संत्यक्तःsaṃtyaktaḥdesertedसम् + √त्यज् (bhvādi, 1P) + क्त (past passive participle), m. nom. sg.
  4. तेषुteṣutoward thempronoun तद्, m. loc. pl.
  5. हार्दीhārdīaffectionate, lovingm. nom. sg. of the adjective हार्दिन्; predicate of the merchant
  6. तथाtathāso (with अपि: even so)indeclinable (adverb)
  7. अपिapieven (with तथा: nevertheless)indeclinable (particle)
  8. अतिatiexceedinglyindeclinable, here used as a free adverb
  9. एवम्evamthusindeclinable (adverb of manner)
  10. एषःeṣaḥthis mandemonstrative pronoun एतद्, m. nom. sg.
  11. तथाtathālikewiseindeclinable (adverb)
  12. अहम्ahamIfirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, nom. sg.
  13. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  14. द्वौdvautwonumeral द्वि, m. nom. du.
  15. अपिapiboth (with द्वौ)indeclinable (particle of inclusion)

Translation

and deserted by his kin; even so he is exceedingly affectionate toward them. Thus this man and likewise I — both of us are deeply afflicted,

In readable Englishand deserted by his kin; yet he loves them dearly. So he and I alike are both in deep distress,

Textual verification / uncertain: तथाप्यति is split तथा अपि अति, with अति as a free adverb qualifying हार्दी. This is a point of interpretation, not of reading: the uncommon free adverb अति could also be taken loosely with the whole clause (‘even so, too much’); either way he loves them excessively.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • संत्यक्तस्तेषु saṃtyaktasteṣu → संत्यक्तः + तेषु

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

  • तथाप्यति tathāpyati → तथा + अपि + अति

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha; yaṇ) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101); इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    ā + a → ā (तथापि); then i before a becomes y (अप्यति).

  • एवमेष तथाहं evameṣa tathāhaṃ → एवम् + एषः + तथा + अहम्

    visarga sandhi (special rule for एषः); vowel sandhi · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    The visarga of एषः is dropped before the consonant t; तथा + अहम् → तथाहम्.

  • द्वावप्यत्यन्तदुःखितौ dvāvapyatyantaduḥkhitau → द्वौ + अपि + अत्यन्तदुःखितौ

    vowel sandhi (ayādi; yaṇ) · एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78); इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    au before a becomes āv (द्वावपि); i before a becomes y (अप्यत्यन्त-).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अत्यन्तदुःखितौ atyantaduḥkhitau

    karmadhāraya (with an adverbial first member)

    Members
    अत्यन्त + दुःखित
    Vigraha
    अत्यन्तं दुःखितौ atyantaṃ duḥkhitau
    Literally
    “endlessly pained”
    In the verse
    in the deepest distress
    Alternative
    अत्यन्त is itself a prādi compound, अन्तम् अतिक्रान्तम् ‘going beyond the end’, used as an adverb.

  • स्वजनेन svajanena

    karmadhāraya

    Members
    स्व + जन
    Vigraha
    स्वः जनः, तेन svaḥ janaḥ, tena
    Literally
    “one’s own people”
    In the verse
    the merchant’s kinsfolk
Morphology & anvaya

  • हार्दी hārdī

    Masculine nominative of हार्दिन् (in-stem: the n drops and the i lengthens), the word used in the neuter (हार्दि) in 1.32 of the merchant’s mind.

  • अति ati

    Normally a prefix (अति-), here a free adverb ‘exceedingly’, a usage found in epic and Purāṇic verse; it goes with हार्दी.

  • अत्यन्तदुःखितौ atyantaduḥkhitau

    दुःखित ‘pained’ is दुःख + the taddhita -इत (‘in whom grief has arisen’), dual to match द्वौ.

Anvaya · prose order

(अयं) स्वजनेन च संत्यक्तः, तथा अपि तेषु अति हार्दी। एवम् एषः तथा अहं च द्वौ अपि अत्यन्तदुःखितौ, …

(ayaṃ) svajanena ca saṃtyaktaḥ, tathā api teṣu ati hārdī | evam eṣaḥ tathā ahaṃ ca dvau api atyantaduḥkhitau, …

The first line finishes the merchant’s case: participle संत्यक्तः, then a concessive clause with हार्दी. The second sums up both men; the nominal predicate अत्यन्तदुःखितौ continues into 1.44.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king sets the two cases side by side and draws the sum: both men are in great pain, and for the same reason. The next verse names it.

Word by word

  4. ममत्वाकृष्टमानसौmamatvākṛṣṭamānasauwhose minds are dragged by the sense of ‘mine’m. nom. du.; compound (see Samāsa); agrees with द्वौ in 1.43

Translation

— our minds dragged by possessiveness toward an object even though its fault has been seen. So what is this, O blessed one, that there is delusion even in (us) two who know?

In readable Englishour minds dragged by the sense of ‘mine’ toward things whose faults we have plainly seen. Then what is this, blessed one — that even we, who know, are deluded?

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • दृष्टदोषे dṛṣṭadoṣe

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    दृष्ट + दोष
    Vigraha
    दृष्टः दोषः यस्मिन् सः, तस्मिन् dṛṣṭaḥ doṣaḥ yasmin saḥ, tasmin
    Literally
