    a thing whose flaw is already plain

  • ममत्वाकृष्टमानसौ mamatvākṛṣṭamānasau

    bahuvrīhi containing a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (ममत्वाकृष्ट)

    Members
    ममत्व + आकृष्ट + मानस
    Vigraha
    ममत्वेन आकृष्टं ममत्वाकृष्टम्; ममत्वाकृष्टं मानसं ययोः तौ mamatvena ākṛṣṭaṃ mamatvākṛṣṭam; mamatvākṛṣṭaṃ mānasaṃ yayoḥ tau
    Literally
    “the two whose minds are drawn by mine-ness”
    In the verse
    pulled by possessiveness against their judgement

  • महाभाग mahābhāga

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    महत् + भाग
    Vigraha
    महान् भागः यस्य सः, तत्सम्बोधने mahān bhāgaḥ yasya saḥ, tatsambodhane
    Literally
    “one whose portion is great”
    In the verse
    a respectful address (as in 1.3)
Morphology & anvaya

  • ज्ञानिनोः jñāninoḥ

    Genitive dual of ज्ञानिन् ‘one who has knowledge’ (the same form serves as locative dual). ‘Of us two who know’: the king includes himself and the merchant.

  • ममत्वाकृष्टमानसौ mamatvākṛṣṭamānasau

    आकृष्ट is the past participle of आ + √कृष् ‘to drag’. Compare 1.12, where the king alone was ममत्वाकृष्टचेतनः; now both men are.

Anvaya · prose order

(आवां) दृष्टदोषे अपि विषये ममत्वाकृष्टमानसौ (स्वः)। तत्, महाभाग, एतत् किम्, यत् ज्ञानिनोः अपि (आवयोः) मोहः (भवति)?

(āvāṃ) dṛṣṭadoṣe api viṣaye mamatvākṛṣṭamānasau (svaḥ) | tat, mahābhāga, etat kim, yat jñāninoḥ api (āvayoḥ) mohaḥ (bhavati)?

The first line completes the description of the two (from 1.43); the second asks the question proper, with a यत् clause explaining एतत्.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The question of the first carita, in its full form: why does delusion (मोह) persist in those who know? The king and the merchant both see the fault in what they cling to, and cling still.

Traditional interpretation

The sage’s answer turns on two words of this verse. He takes up विषय at once (1.47–48), and he names the source of the मोह of ‘even those who know’ as Mahāmāyā (1.55, ज्ञानिनामपि चेतांसि).

Verse 1.45

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

ममास्य च भवत्येषा विवेकान्धस्य मूढता॥⁠४५⁠॥

mamāsya ca bhavatyeṣā vivekāndhasya mūḍhatā ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

मम · अस्य · च · भवति · एषा · विवेकान्धस्य · मूढता

mama · asya · ca · bhavati · eṣā · vivekāndhasya · mūḍhatā

Word by word

  1. ममmamaof me, in mefirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg.
  2. अस्यasyaof him (this man)demonstrative pronoun इदम्, m. gen. sg.
  3. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  4. भवतिbhavatiis, comes about√भू (bhvādi, 1P ‘to be, become’), laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  5. एषाeṣāthisdemonstrative pronoun एतद्, f. nom. sg.; qualifies मूढता
  6. विवेकान्धस्यvivekāndhasyablind in discernmentm. gen. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); agrees with अस्य and is meant of both
  7. मूढताmūḍhatābewilderment, follyf. nom. sg. of मूढता (abstract noun from मूढ ‘bewildered’); subject of भवति

Translation

— this bewilderment comes to me and to him, blind in discernment.

In readable English— this bewilderment, in him and in me, blind as we are to discernment.

‘as we are’ renders the singular विवेकान्धस्य applied to both.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • ममास्य mamāsya → मम + अस्य

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + a → ā.

  • भवत्येषा bhavatyeṣā → भवति + एषा

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Final i before e becomes y.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • विवेकान्धस्य vivekāndhasya

    saptamī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    विवेक + अन्ध
    Vigraha
    विवेके अन्धः, तस्य viveke andhaḥ, tasya
    Literally
    “blind in (the matter of) discernment”
    In the verse
    unable to judge rightly, though not unknowing
Morphology & anvaya

  • विवेकान्धस्य vivekāndhasya

    Singular, agreeing with the nearer genitive अस्य, but the sense applies to both speakers: ‘of me and of him, (each) blind in discernment’.

  • मूढता mūḍhatā

    Abstract noun in -ता from मूढ, the past participle of √मुह् ‘to be bewildered’ — the same root as मोह (1.44).

Anvaya · prose order

मम अस्य च विवेकान्धस्य एषा मूढता भवति।

mama asya ca vivekāndhasya eṣā mūḍhatā bhavati |

A simple sentence completing the question of 1.44: subject मूढता with एषा, possessors मम अस्य च, verb भवति.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king’s question ends. He distinguishes two things: they have knowledge (ज्ञान, 1.44) but lack discernment (विवेक), and so they are bewildered. The sage begins his answer in 1.47.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the king’s diagnosis is precise. Information is not the problem; the faculty that weighs it and lets go is. The rest of the chapter traces that failure to a power larger than the two men.

Verse 1.46

Speaker
‹›

ऋषिरुवाच॥⁠४६⁠॥

ṛṣiruvāca ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

ऋषिः · उवाच

ṛṣiḥ · uvāca

Word by word

  1. ऋषिःṛṣiḥthe sage (Medhas)m. nom. sg. of ऋषि (i-stem); subject of उवाच
  2. उवाचuvācasaid√वच् (adādi, 2P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, kartari prayoga

Translation

The sage said:

In readable EnglishThe sage said:

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • ऋषिरुवाच ṛṣiruvāca → ऋषिः + उवाच

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    After i the visarga (as रु) is sounded r before a vowel and joins it: ऋषिः उवाच → ऋषिरुवाच.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

Anvaya · prose order

ऋषिः उवाच।

ṛṣiḥ uvāca |

Subject and verb: a speaker label.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Medhas, the sage whose hermitage Suratha found (1.10), begins his answer to the question of 1.40–45. From here the ṛṣi is the narrator of the Goddess’s deeds; his answer runs to the end of the text.

Verse 1.47

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

ज्ञानमस्ति समस्तस्य जन्तोर्विषयगोचरे॥⁠४७⁠॥

jñānamasti samastasya jantorviṣayagocare ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

ज्ञानम् · अस्ति · समस्तस्य · जन्तोः · विषयगोचरे

jñānam · asti · samastasya · jantoḥ · viṣayagocare

Word by word

  1. ज्ञानम्jñānamknowledgen. nom. sg. of ज्ञान; subject of अस्ति
  2. अस्तिastithere is, (every creature) has√अस् (adādi, 2P ‘to be’), laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  3. समस्तस्यsamastasyaevery, alladjective समस्त, m. gen. sg.; qualifies जन्तोः
  4. जन्तोःjantoḥof a creature, of a living beingm. gen. sg. of जन्तु (u-stem); genitive of possession with अस्ति
  5. विषयगोचरेviṣayagocarein the range of sense-objectsm. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)

Translation

There is knowledge of every creature in the range of sense-objects.

In readable EnglishEvery living creature has knowledge in the realm of the senses.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • ज्ञानमस्ति jñānamasti → ज्ञानम् + अस्ति

    no change (m before a vowel) · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23) does not apply before a vowel

    Final m stays m before a vowel and is written joined.

  • जन्तोर्विषयगोचरे jantorviṣayagocare → जन्तोः + विषयगोचरे

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    After o (not a/ā) the visarga is sounded r before the voiced v.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • विषयगोचरे viṣayagocare

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    विषय + गोचर
    Vigraha
    विषयाणां गोचरः, तस्मिन् viṣayāṇāṃ gocaraḥ, tasmin
    Literally
    “in the pasture of sense-objects”
    In the verse
    in the sphere of what the senses grasp
    Alternative
    Also read as a karmadhāraya, विषयः एव गोचरः ‘the field that is the object’; the sense is the same. गोचर is literally ‘where cattle graze’, then any range or province.
Morphology & anvaya

  • अस्ति asti

    With a genitive, ‘to be’ means ‘to have’: समस्तस्य जन्तोः ज्ञानम् अस्ति ‘every creature has knowledge’.

  • जन्तोः jantoḥ

    Genitive singular of an u-stem: guṇa of the stem vowel + -ः (जन्तु → जन्तोः).

Anvaya · prose order

समस्तस्य जन्तोः विषयगोचरे ज्ञानम् अस्ति।

samastasya jantoḥ viṣayagocare jñānam asti |

A simple existential sentence: possessor in the genitive, sphere in the locative, subject ज्ञानम्, verb अस्ति.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Medhas begins by granting the king’s premise in a limited way: yes, there is knowledge — but the knowledge every creature has, knowledge of sense-objects.

Traditional interpretation

The word picks up the king’s विषय (1.44). The text will distinguish this ordinary knowing from the knowledge that frees, which it calls the supreme विद्या and identifies with the Goddess herself (1.57).

Verse 1.48

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

विषयश्च महाभाग याति चैवं पृथक् पृथक्।दिवान्धाः प्राणिनः केचिद्रात्रावन्धास्तथापरे॥⁠४८⁠॥

viṣayaśca mahābhāga yāti caivaṃ pṛthak pṛthak |divāndhāḥ prāṇinaḥ kecidrātrāvandhāstathāpare ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

विषयः · च · महाभाग · याति · च · एवम् · पृथक् · पृथक्दिवा · अन्धाः · प्राणिनः · केचित् · रात्रौ · अन्धाः · तथा · अपरे

viṣayaḥ · ca · mahābhāga · yāti · ca · evam · pṛthak · pṛthakdivā · andhāḥ · prāṇinaḥ · kecit · rātrau · andhāḥ · tathā · apare

Word by word

  1. विषयःviṣayaḥthe sense-object, the world of objectsm. nom. sg. of विषय; subject of याति
  2. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction, linking to 1.47)
  3. महाभागmahābhāgaO blessed onem. voc. sg.; compound (bahuvrīhi, as in 1.44); addressed to the king

  5. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  6. एवम्evamthus, in this wayindeclinable (adverb of manner)
  7. पृथक्pṛthakseparatelyindeclinable (adverb)
  8. पृथक्pṛthak(repeated:) each in its own wayindeclinable; repetition (āmreḍita) for distribution
  9. दिवाdivāby dayindeclinable (adverb of time)
  10. अन्धाःandhāḥblindadjective अन्ध, m. nom. pl.; predicate of प्राणिनः
  11. प्राणिनःprāṇinaḥcreatures, living beingsm. nom. pl. of प्राणिन् (‘having breath’); subject
  12. केचित्kecitsomeindefinite pronoun किम् + चित्, m. nom. pl.; qualifies प्राणिनः
  13. रात्रौrātrauat nightf. loc. sg. of रात्रि (i-stem); locative of time
  14. अन्धाःandhāḥblindadjective अन्ध, m. nom. pl.; predicate of अपरे

Translation

And the sense-object, O blessed one, reaches (creatures) thus, severally. Some creatures are blind by day; likewise others are blind at night.

In readable EnglishAnd the world of objects, blessed one, reaches each creature in its own way. Some creatures are blind by day, others blind by night,

‘creatures’ in the first sentence is supplied; the Sanskrit says only that the object ‘goes’ severally.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • विषयश्च viṣayaśca → विषयः + च

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    Visarga before c becomes s, and s next to the palatal c becomes ś.

  • चैवं caivaṃ → च + एवम्

    vowel sandhi (vṛddhi) · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88)

    a + e → ai. The final m becomes anusvāra before p (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

  • दिवान्धाः divāndhāḥ → दिवा + अन्धाः

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    ā + a → ā. Taken here as two words, to match रात्रौ अन्धाः in the same line; दिवान्ध can also be read as one word (it is a name of the owl).

  • केचिद्रात्रावन्धास्तथापरे kecidrātrāvandhāstathāpare → केचित् + रात्रौ + अन्धाः + तथा + अपरे

    consonant, vowel and visarga sandhi · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39); एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78); विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    t → d before the voiced r; au → āv before a; āḥ → ās before t; ā + a → ā.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • पृथक् pṛthak

    Repeated (पृथक् पृथक्) to express distribution: ‘severally, each in its own way’.

  • अपरे apare

    Nominative plural masculine in -e: अपर follows the pronominal declension (like सर्वे).

  • प्राणिनः prāṇinaḥ

    Nominative plural of the in-stem प्राणिन् ‘one who has breath (प्राण)’, a general word for living beings.

Anvaya · prose order

(हे) महाभाग, विषयः च एवं पृथक् पृथक् याति च। केचित् प्राणिनः दिवा अन्धाः, तथा अपरे रात्रौ अन्धाः।

(he) mahābhāga, viṣayaḥ ca evaṃ pṛthak pṛthak yāti ca | kecit prāṇinaḥ divā andhāḥ, tathā apare rātrau andhāḥ |

A general statement (the object reaches each being differently), then two examples in nominal sentences (the verb ‘are’ understood).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Medhas illustrates: knowledge of objects is not uniform. What a creature can know depends on its nature — some see only by night, some only by day. The text names no species.

Traditional interpretation

The point prepares the next step: if knowing objects were what made a being wise, the animals would be wise too (1.49–50). The knowledge the king has is real but of this ordinary kind.

  • केचिद्दिवा keciddivā → केचित् + दिवा

  • तुल्यदृष्टयः tulyadṛṣṭayaḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    तुल्य + दृष्टि
    Vigraha
    तुल्या दृष्टिः येषां ते tulyā dṛṣṭiḥ yeṣāṃ te

    In the verse
    who see alike by day and night

    upapada tatpuruṣa (ज from √जन् ‘to be born’)

    Members

    Literally
    “born of Manu”
    In the verse
    human beings
Morphology & anvaya

  • सत्यम् satyam

    Accusative neuter of सत्य used as an adverb of concession: ‘true, (men) are knowers’ — answered by किं तु ‘but’.

  • केवलम् kevalam

    Adverbial accusative of केवल ‘alone’: न हि केवलम् ‘not (they) alone, indeed’.

Anvaya · prose order

केचित् प्राणिनः दिवा तथा रात्रौ तुल्यदृष्टयः। मनुजाः सत्यं ज्ञानिनः, किं तु ते केवलं न हि (ज्ञानिनः)।

kecit prāṇinaḥ divā tathā rātrau tulyadṛṣṭayaḥ | manujāḥ satyaṃ jñāninaḥ, kiṃ tu te kevalaṃ na hi (jñāninaḥ) |

Three nominal clauses with ‘are’ understood: the third example of creatures, a concession about men, and its correction.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Medhas completes the list (blind by day, blind by night, seeing in both) and turns it on the king’s claim to be a ‘knower’: humans do know, but knowledge of this kind is shared with all creatures.

Verse 1.50

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

यतो हि ज्ञानिनः सर्वे पशुपक्षिमृगादयः।ज्ञानं च तन्मनुष्याणां यत्तेषां मृगपक्षिणाम्॥⁠५०⁠॥

yato hi jñāninaḥ sarve paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ |jñānaṃ ca tanmanuṣyāṇāṃ yatteṣāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

यतः · हि · ज्ञानिनः · सर्वे · पशुपक्षिमृगादयःज्ञानम् · च · तत् · मनुष्याणाम् · यत् · तेषाम् · मृगपक्षिणाम्

yataḥ · hi · jñāninaḥ · sarve · paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥjñānam · ca · tat · manuṣyāṇām · yat · teṣām · mṛgapakṣiṇām

Word by word

  1. यतःyataḥbecause, forindeclinable (causal conjunction, the ablative of यद् fixed as a particle)
  2. हिhiindeedindeclinable (emphatic particle)
  3. ज्ञानिनःjñāninaḥpossessed of knowledgem. nom. pl. of ज्ञानिन्; predicate
  4. सर्वेsarveallpronominal adjective सर्व, m. nom. pl.
  5. पशुपक्षिमृगादयःpaśupakṣimṛgādayaḥcattle, birds, wild beasts and the restm. nom. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); subject
  6. ज्ञानम्jñānamknowledgen. nom. sg. of ज्ञान; subject
  7. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  8. तत्tatthat (same)pronoun तद्, n. nom. sg.; correlative of यत्
  9. मनुष्याणाम्manuṣyāṇāmof human beingsm. gen. pl. of मनुष्य; genitive of possession
  10. यत्yatwhichrelative pronoun यद्, n. nom. sg.
  11. तेषाम्teṣāmof thosepronoun तद्, m. gen. pl.; qualifies मृगपक्षिणाम्

Translation

For all — cattle, birds, wild beasts and the rest — are possessed of knowledge. And men have that knowledge which those beasts and birds (have);

In readable Englishfor every creature — cattle, birds, wild beasts and the rest — has knowledge. And the knowledge men have is the same as that of beasts and birds,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • यतो हि yato hi → यतः + हि

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced h becomes -o.

  • तन्मनुष्याणां tanmanuṣyāṇāṃ → तत् + मनुष्याणाम्

    consonant sandhi (nasalisation) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45)

    Final t before m becomes n.

  • यत्तेषां yatteṣāṃ → यत् + तेषाम्

    no change (t before t) · खरि च (8.4.55)

    The final t stays t before the unvoiced t; the words are written together.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • पशुपक्षिमृगादयः paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ

    bahuvrīhi containing an itaretara dvandva (पशुपक्षिमृग)

    Members
    पशु + पक्षिन् + मृग + आदि
    Vigraha
    पशवश्च पक्षिणश्च मृगाश्च पशुपक्षिमृगाः; पशुपक्षिमृगाः आदयः येषां ते paśavaśca pakṣiṇaśca mṛgāśca paśupakṣimṛgāḥ; paśupakṣimṛgāḥ ādayaḥ yeṣāṃ te
    Literally
    “those of whom cattle, birds and wild beasts are the first”
    In the verse
    all the animals

  • मृगपक्षिणाम् mṛgapakṣiṇām

    itaretara dvandva

    Members
    मृग + पक्षिन्
    Vigraha
    मृगाश्च पक्षिणश्च, तेषाम् mṛgāśca pakṣiṇaśca, teṣām
    Literally
    “of beasts and birds”
    In the verse
    of the animals just named
Morphology & anvaya

  • पशुपक्षिमृगादयः paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ

    पक्षिन् ‘bird’ drops its final n inside the compound (पक्षि-). पशु is the domestic animal, मृग the wild one.

  • सर्वे sarve

    Pronominal nominative plural in -e (सर्व, like अपरे in 1.48).

Anvaya · prose order

यतः हि पशुपक्षिमृगादयः सर्वे ज्ञानिनः (सन्ति)। मनुष्याणां च तत् ज्ञानम् (अस्ति), यत् तेषां मृगपक्षिणाम् (अस्ति)।

yataḥ hi paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ sarve jñāninaḥ (santi) | manuṣyāṇāṃ ca tat jñānam (asti), yat teṣāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām (asti) |

A causal clause (यतः …) and a relative pair (तत् … यत्): men’s knowledge is the same as that which belongs to beasts and birds.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The argument reaches its point: as far as knowledge of objects goes, humans and animals are on a level. The king’s ‘knowing’ (1.42, 1.44) is of this kind, and so it cannot by itself free him.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the sage is not belittling the king. He is moving the question from how much one knows to what one is bound by — the subject of the next three verses.

Verse 1.51

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

मनुष्याणां च यत्तेषां तुल्यमन्यत्तथोभयोः।ज्ञानेऽपि सति पश्यैतान् पतङ्गाञ्छावचञ्चुषु॥⁠५१⁠॥

manuṣyāṇāṃ ca yatteṣāṃ tulyamanyattathobhayoḥ |jñāne'pi sati paśyaitān pataṅgāñchāvacañcuṣu ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

मनुष्याणाम् · च · यत् · तेषाम् · तुल्यम् · अन्यत् · तथा · उभयोःज्ञाने · अपि · सति · पश्य · एतान् · पतङ्गान् · शावचञ्चुषु

manuṣyāṇām · ca · yat · teṣām · tulyam · anyat · tathā · ubhayoḥjñāne · api · sati · paśya · etān · pataṅgān · śāvacañcuṣu

Word by word

  1. मनुष्याणाम्manuṣyāṇāmof human beingsm. gen. pl. of मनुष्य; genitive of possession
  2. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  3. यत्yatwhat, that whichrelative pronoun यद्, n. nom. sg. (‘knowledge’ understood from 1.50)
  4. तेषाम्teṣāmof them (the animals)pronoun तद्, m. gen. pl.
  5. तुल्यम्tulyamequal, alikeadjective तुल्य, n. nom. sg.; predicate of अन्यत्
  6. अन्यत्anyatthe rest, everything elsepronominal adjective अन्य, n. nom. sg. (pronominal ending -त्); subject
  7. तथाtathālikewiseindeclinable (adverb)
  8. उभयोःubhayoḥfor bothpronominal adjective उभ, m. gen. du.; with तुल्यम्
  9. ज्ञानेjñāneknowledgen. loc. sg. of ज्ञान; in the locative absolute with सति
  10. अपिapieven thoughindeclinable (concessive particle)
  11. सतिsatibeing (there)√अस् (adādi, 2P) + शतृ (present participle सत्), n. loc. sg.; locative absolute with ज्ञाने
  12. पश्यpaśyalook at, see√दृश् (bhvādi, 1P; present stem पश्य-), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  13. एतान्etānthesedemonstrative pronoun एतद्, m. acc. pl.; qualifies पतङ्गान्
  14. पतङ्गान्pataṅgānbirdsm. acc. pl. of पतङ्ग (‘flying one’: a bird, also a winged insect); object of पश्य
  15. शावचञ्चुषुśāvacañcuṣuinto the beaks of their youngf. loc. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); locative of the goal, with कणमोक्ष- in 1.52

Translation

And what is men’s is theirs; and the rest is likewise equal for both. Even though there is knowledge, look at these birds — into the beaks of their young

In readable Englishand what men have, they have; in all else, too, the two are alike. Yet, for all their knowledge, look at these birds — into the beaks of their young

The sentence runs on into 1.52: the birds are intent on dropping grain into those beaks.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तुल्यमन्यत्तथोभयोः tulyamanyattathobhayoḥ → तुल्यम् + अन्यत् + तथा + उभयोः

    consonant and vowel sandhi · खरि च (8.4.55); आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    The m of तुल्यम् joins the vowel; t stays t before t; ā + u → o (तथोभयोः).

  • ज्ञानेऽपि jñāne'pi → ज्ञाने + अपि

    vowel sandhi (pūrvarūpa) · एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    Final e before a: the a is absorbed (avagraha).

  • पश्यैतान् paśyaitān → पश्य + एतान्

    vowel sandhi (vṛddhi) · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88)

    a + e → ai.

  • पतङ्गाञ्छावचञ्चुषु pataṅgāñchāvacañcuṣu → पतङ्गान् + शावचञ्चुषु

    consonant sandhi (n before ś) · स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40), शश्छोऽटि (8.4.63)

    Final n before ś becomes the palatal ñ, and the ś becomes ch. In the full derivation a t is optionally inserted after the n, made palatal, and then lost; the Gita Press writes the result ञ्छ (compare the variant note on 3.22). Without the change the words would be written पतङ्गान् शाव-.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • शावचञ्चुषु śāvacañcuṣu

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    शाव + चञ्चु
    Vigraha
    शावानां चञ्चवः, तासु śāvānāṃ cañcavaḥ, tāsu
    Literally
    “in the beaks of the young”
    In the verse
    into their nestlings’ open beaks
Morphology & anvaya

  • सति sati

    Locative of the present participle of √अस् ‘to be’: ज्ञाने सति ‘knowledge being (present)’, a locative absolute; with अपि it is concessive: ‘even though they have knowledge’.

  • पश्य paśya

    √दृश् has no present of its own; the stem पश्य- serves for the present system. Imperative 2nd sg.: ‘look!’

  • अन्यत् anyat

    Neuter nominative of the pronominal adjective अन्य, with -त् as in तत्, यत्: ‘the other (things)’.

Anvaya · prose order

मनुष्याणां च यत् (ज्ञानम्), (तत्) तेषाम् (अपि अस्ति); अन्यत् (च) तथा उभयोः तुल्यम्। ज्ञाने सति अपि, एतान् पतङ्गान् पश्य, शावचञ्चुषु (कणमोक्षादृतान् …)

manuṣyāṇāṃ ca yat (jñānam), (tat) teṣām (api asti); anyat (ca) tathā ubhayoḥ tulyam | jñāne sati api, etān pataṅgān paśya, śāvacañcuṣu (kaṇamokṣādṛtān …)

The first line: a relative clause with its correlative understood, then a nominal clause. The second line: a concessive locative absolute and the imperative पश्य with its object पतङ्गान्, described further in 1.52.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Medhas closes the comparison (humans and animals are alike in knowledge and in the rest) and points to an example. The demonstrative एतान् with the imperative पश्य suggests birds within sight at the hermitage.

Traditional interpretation

The text does not say what ‘the rest’ (अन्यत्) is; the point is only that, in the ordinary life of the senses, humans and animals are on one level.

Verse 1.52

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

कणमोक्षादृतान्मोहात् पीड्यमानानपि क्षुधा।मानुषा मनुजव्याघ्र साभिलाषाः सुतान् प्रति॥⁠५२⁠॥

kaṇamokṣādṛtānmohāt pīḍyamānānapi kṣudhā |mānuṣā manujavyāghra sābhilāṣāḥ sutān prati ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

kaṇamokṣādṛtān · mohāt · pīḍyamānān · api · kṣudhāmānuṣāḥ · manujavyāghra · sābhilāṣāḥ · sutān · prati

Word by word

  1. कणमोक्षादृतान्kaṇamokṣādṛtānintent on letting fall grains (of food)m. acc. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies पतङ्गान् in 1.51
  2. मोहात्mohātout of delusionm. abl. sg. of मोह; ablative of cause
  3. पीड्यमानान्pīḍyamānānbeing tormented√पीड् (curādi, 10 ‘to press, pain’) + यक् + शानच् (passive present participle), m. acc. pl.; qualifies पतङ्गान्
  4. अपिapieven thoughindeclinable (concessive particle)
  5. क्षुधाkṣudhāby hungerf. instr. sg. of क्षुध् (consonant stem); agent of पीड्यमानान्
  6. मानुषाःmānuṣāḥhuman beingsm. nom. pl. of मानुष; subject
  7. मनुजव्याघ्रmanujavyāghraO tiger among menm. voc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); addressed to the king
  8. साभिलाषाःsābhilāṣāḥfull of longingm. nom. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate of मानुषाः
  9. सुतान्sutānsons, childrenm. acc. pl. of सुत; governed by प्रति
  10. प्रतिpratitowardindeclinable (postposition with the accusative)

Translation

— intent, out of delusion, on letting fall grains, though tormented by hunger. Human beings, O tiger among men, are full of longing toward their sons

In readable Englishthey drop grain into them out of sheer delusion, though racked by hunger themselves. Men, tiger among men, long for sons

‘themselves’ makes plain that the hunger is the parent birds’ own. The second line runs on into 1.53.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • कणमोक्षादृतान् kaṇamokṣādṛtān → कणमोक्ष + आदृतान्

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + ā → ā.

  • पीड्यमानानपि pīḍyamānānapi → पीड्यमानान् + अपि

    no change (n before a vowel) · ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम् (8.3.32) does not apply

    After the long ā the final n is not doubled; it simply joins the vowel.

  • मानुषा मनुजव्याघ्र mānuṣā manujavyāghra → मानुषाः + मनुजव्याघ्र

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17)

    -āḥ before a voiced sound: the visarga becomes y, and the y is dropped before a consonant, leaving -ā.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • कणमोक्षादृतान् kaṇamokṣādṛtān

    saptamī tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (कणमोक्ष)

    Members
    कण + मोक्ष + आदृत
    Vigraha
    कणानां मोक्षः कणमोक्षः; कणमोक्षे आदृताः, तान् kaṇānāṃ mokṣaḥ kaṇamokṣaḥ; kaṇamokṣe ādṛtāḥ, tān
    Literally
    “devoted to the release of grains”
    In the verse
    intent on dropping food into their young’s beaks

  • मनुजव्याघ्र manujavyāghra

    karmadhāraya (upamita: the standard of comparison stands second)

    Members
    मनुज + व्याघ्र
    Vigraha
    मनुजः व्याघ्रः इव, तत्सम्बोधने manujaḥ vyāghraḥ iva, tatsambodhane
    Literally
    “a man (who is) a tiger”
    In the verse
    a heroic address to the king
    Alternative
    Also resolved as a saptamī tatpuruṣa, मनुजेषु व्याघ्रः ‘a tiger among men’; the sense is the same.

  • साभिलाषाः sābhilāṣāḥ

    bahuvrīhi (with सह, shortened to स)

    Members
    स (सह) + अभिलाष
    Vigraha
    अभिलाषेण सह वर्तन्ते ये ते abhilāṣeṇa saha vartante ye te
    Literally
    “those who are with longing”
    In the verse
    full of desire, yearning
Morphology & anvaya

  • पीड्यमानान् pīḍyamānān

    Passive present participle: passive stem पीड्य- (yak) + -मान. ‘Being tormented’, with the agent क्षुधा in the instrumental.

  • मोहात् mohāt

    Ablative of cause: the birds act ‘from delusion’, not from calculation — the contrast with लोभात् (‘from greed’) in 1.53.

  • प्रति prati

    As a postposition (karmapravacanīya) प्रति takes the accusative: सुतान् प्रति ‘toward (their) sons’.

Anvaya · prose order

(पतङ्गान्) मोहात् कणमोक्षादृतान्, क्षुधा पीड्यमानान् अपि (पश्य)। (हे) मनुजव्याघ्र, मानुषाः सुतान् प्रति साभिलाषाः (भवन्ति), …

(pataṅgān) mohāt kaṇamokṣādṛtān, kṣudhā pīḍyamānān api (paśya) | (he) manujavyāghra, mānuṣāḥ sutān prati sābhilāṣāḥ (bhavanti), …

The first line completes the description of the birds (objects of पश्य in 1.51). The second begins a new statement about humans; its cause comes in 1.53.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The birds feed their young while starving themselves, and the sage calls the motive मोह, delusion. Then he turns to humans, who also long for their children.

Traditional interpretation

The two cases are not the same: the birds act from blind delusion, humans (1.53) from greed for a return. Both are forms of the attachment the king asked about, and both, Medhas says next, are the work of Mahāmāyā (1.54).

  2. प्रत्युपकारायpratyupakārāyafor a return of the favourm. dat. sg. of प्रत्युपकार; dative of purpose
  3. ननुnanusurelyindeclinable (particle introducing a question that expects assent)
  4. एतान्etānthese (people)demonstrative pronoun एतद्, m. acc. pl.; object of पश्यसि
  5. किम्kim(do you) …?indeclinable (interrogative particle)
  6. नnanotindeclinable (negative particle)
  7. पश्यसिpaśyasiyou see√दृश् (bhvādi, 1P; present stem पश्य-), laṭ (present), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  8. तथाtathāso (with अपि: even so)indeclinable (adverb)
  9. अपिapieven (with तथा: nevertheless)indeclinable (particle)
  10. ममतावर्त्तेmamatāvartteinto the whirlpool of ‘mine’m. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); locative of the goal
  11. मोहगर्तेmohagarteinto the pit of delusionm. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to ममतावर्त्ते
  12. निपातिताःnipātitāḥcast down, made to fallनि + √पत् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to fall’), causative (णिच्) + क्त (past passive participle), m. nom. pl.; ‘they’ (all these beings) understood

Translation

— out of greed, for a return of the favour. Surely you see these? Even so, (they are) cast down into the whirlpool of mine-ness, into the pit of delusion,

In readable Englishout of greed, hoping to be repaid. Do you not see them? And still they are thrown into the whirlpool of ‘mine’, into the pit of delusion —

The sentence is completed in 1.54: ‘by the power of Mahāmāyā, who keeps the world of saṃsāra in being’.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • लोभात्प्रत्युपकाराय lobhātpratyupakārāya → लोभात् + प्रत्युपकाराय

    no change (t before an unvoiced stop) · खरि च (8.4.55)

    The final t stays unvoiced before p; the words are only written together. Inside प्रत्युपकार, प्रति + उप- gives प्रत्युप- (इको यणचि, 6.1.77).

  • नन्वेतान् nanvetān → ननु + एतान्

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Final u before e becomes v.

  • तथापि tathāpi → तथा + अपि

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    ā + a → ā. The same joining inside ममतावर्त्ते (ममता + आवर्त्त).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • ममतावर्त्ते mamatāvartte

    karmadhāraya (a metaphor, rūpaka: the first member is identified with the second)

    Members
    ममता + आवर्त्त
    Vigraha
    ममता एव आवर्त्तः, तस्मिन् mamatā eva āvarttaḥ, tasmin
    Literally
    “in the whirlpool that is mine-ness”
    In the verse
    caught in the circling pull of possessiveness
    Alternative
    Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, ममतायाः आवर्त्तः ‘the whirlpool of mine-ness’; the metaphorical reading fits the paired image मोहगर्ते.

  • मोहगर्ते mohagarte

    karmadhāraya (rūpaka)

    Members
    मोह + गर्त
    Vigraha
    मोहः एव गर्तः, तस्मिन् mohaḥ eva gartaḥ, tasmin
    Literally
    “in the pit that is delusion”
    In the verse
    fallen into bewilderment as into a pit
    Alternative
    Also ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, मोहस्य गर्तः; as above.
Morphology & anvaya

  • निपातिताः nipātitāḥ

    Past passive participle of the causative of नि + √पत्: ‘made to fall, thrown down’. The causer is named in the next verse: by the power of Mahāmāyā (1.54).

  • ममतावर्त्ते mamatāvartte

    ममता (मम + -ता) is the same idea as ममत्व in 1.41 and 1.44. आवर्त्त ‘whirlpool’ (आ + √वृत् ‘to turn’) is printed with a doubled t after r, a spelling the grammarians permit; it is the same word as आवर्त.

  • प्रत्युपकाराय pratyupakārāya

    प्रत्युपकार ‘a service in return’ (प्रति + उपकार); the dative gives the purpose: parents cherish children ‘for the sake of a return’.

Anvaya · prose order

(मानुषाः) लोभात् प्रत्युपकाराय (सुतान् प्रति साभिलाषाः)। ननु एतान् किं न पश्यसि? तथा अपि (एते) ममतावर्त्ते मोहगर्ते निपातिताः (महामायाप्रभावेण, 1.54)।

(mānuṣāḥ) lobhāt pratyupakārāya (sutān prati sābhilāṣāḥ) | nanu etān kiṃ na paśyasi? tathā api (ete) mamatāvartte mohagarte nipātitāḥ (mahāmāyāprabhāveṇa, 1.54) |

The first half finishes 1.52 (why men long for sons) and asks a rhetorical question. The second begins the sentence completed in 1.54: the beings are thrown into mamatā and moha by the power of Mahāmāyā.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Human love for children is mixed with self-interest: greed for a return. Yet humans and birds alike, knowing as they are, are thrown into the same whirlpool of possessiveness and pit of delusion. The next verse names who throws them.

Traditional interpretation

The two images answer the king’s words: his ममत्व (1.41, 1.44) and मोह (1.44) return as the whirlpool and the pit. The sage’s answer is that this is not a private failure of the king and the merchant but the working of Mahāmāyā (1.54–56), who is also the cause of release (1.57).

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

The Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names the Goddess from the other side of the same pair: ममताहन्त्री (165), ‘destroyer of mine-ness’, and मोहनाशिनी (163), ‘remover of delusion’. Here in the Devī Māhātmya the same power that casts beings into mamatā and moha is the one that frees them when she is gracious (1.57).

Verse 1.54

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

महामायाप्रभावेण संसारस्थितिकारिणा।तन्नात्र विस्मयः कार्यो योगनिद्रा जगत्पतेः॥⁠५४⁠॥

mahāmāyāprabhāveṇa saṃsārasthitikāriṇā |tannātra vismayaḥ kāryo yoganidrā jagatpateḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

महामायाप्रभावेण · संसारस्थितिकारिणातत् · न · अत्र · विस्मयः · कार्यः · योगनिद्रा · जगत्पतेः

mahāmāyāprabhāveṇa · saṃsārasthitikāriṇātat · na · atra · vismayaḥ · kāryaḥ · yoganidrā · jagatpateḥ

Word by word

  1. महामायाप्रभावेणmahāmāyāprabhāveṇaby the power of Mahāmāyām. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); agent of निपातिताः in 1.53
  2. संसारस्थितिकारिणाsaṃsārasthitikāriṇāwhich brings about the continuance of saṃsāram. instr. sg. of the in-stem संसारस्थितिकारिन्; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies महामायाप्रभावेण
  3. तत्tatthereforepronoun तद्, n. acc. sg. used as an indeclinable of consequence (‘so, hence’)
  4. नnanotindeclinable (negation)
  5. अत्रatrahere, in this matterindeclinable (adverb of place, from इदम् + tral)
  6. विस्मयःvismayaḥwonder, astonishmentm. nom. sg. of विस्मय (वि + √स्मि); subject of the gerundive
  7. कार्यःkāryaḥto be felt; lit. ‘to be made’gerundive (kṛtya, ṇyat) of √कृ (tanādi 8U ‘to do’), m. nom. sg.; agrees with विस्मयः
  8. योगनिद्राyoganidrāthe Yoganidrā, the yogic sleepf. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate of एषा in 1.55
  9. जगत्पतेःjagatpateḥof the lord of the world (Viṣṇu)m. gen. sg. of the i-stem जगत्पति; compound (see Samāsa)

Translation

(They are thrown down) by the power of Mahāmāyā, which makes the continuance of saṃsāra. Therefore no wonder is to be felt in this: the yogic sleep of the lord of the world —

In readable EnglishIt is the power of Mahāmāyā, who keeps the round of worldly existence turning, that casts them down. So there is nothing to wonder at here. She who is the yogic sleep of the Lord of the world —

The first line ends the sentence of 1.53; the last words begin the sentence completed in 1.55.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तन्नात्र tannātra → तत् + न + अत्र

    consonant sandhi (nasal assimilation) and vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    The final t of तत् becomes the nasal n before the nasal n of न (optional, but usual); then the a of न and the a of अत्र merge into ā.

  • विस्मयः कार्यो vismayaḥ kāryo → विस्मयः + कार्यः

    visarga sandhi (no change) · खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः (8.3.15)

    Before an unvoiced k the visarga simply stays. Contrast the next junction.

  • कार्यो योगनिद्रा kāryo yoganidrā → कार्यः + योगनिद्रा

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced y becomes -o.

  • महामायाप्रभावेण mahāmāyāprabhāveṇa → महामाया + प्रभावेन

    internal retroflexion (ṇatva) inside a compound · the n of an ending becomes ṇ after r in the same word when no dental or palatal intervenes (ṇatva)

    The r of प्र- turns the instrumental ending -ena into -eṇa; the same happens in संसारस्थितिकारिणा (r of कारिन्).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • महामायाप्रभावेण mahāmāyāprabhāveṇa

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (महामाया is itself a karmadhāraya: महती चासौ माया च)

    Members
    महामाया + प्रभाव
    Vigraha
    महामायायाः प्रभावः, तेन mahāmāyāyāḥ prabhāvaḥ, tena
    Literally
    “by the might of the Great Māyā”
    In the verse
    by the Goddess’s own power — the answer to the question of 1.44–45

  • संसारस्थितिकारिणा saṃsārasthitikāriṇā

    upapada tatpuruṣa (the agent noun कारिन्, kṛt -in, after its object) containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (संसारस्थिति)

    Members
    संसार + स्थिति + कारिन्
    Vigraha
    संसारस्य स्थितिः संसारस्थितिः; तां करोति इति संसारस्थितिकारी, तेन saṃsārasya sthitiḥ saṃsārasthitiḥ; tāṃ karoti iti saṃsārasthitikārī, tena
    Literally
    “making the standing of saṃsāra”
    In the verse
    which keeps the round of birth and death going

  • योगनिद्रा yoganidrā

    karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa: the first member identified with the second)

    Members
    योग + निद्रा
    Vigraha
    योगः एव निद्रा yogaḥ eva nidrā
    Literally
    “the sleep that is yoga”
    In the verse
    Viṣṇu’s sleep between ages, which is not ignorance but withdrawn absorption
    Alternative
    Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, योगस्य निद्रा, ‘the sleep of yoga’; the sense is the same.

  • जगत्पतेः jagatpateḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    जगत् + पति
    Vigraha
    जगतः पतिः, तस्य jagataḥ patiḥ, tasya
    Literally
    “of the lord of the world”
    In the verse
    of Viṣṇu (named as Hari in 1.55)
Morphology & anvaya

  • कार्यः kāryaḥ

    Gerundive of √कृ with ṇyat: कृ + य → कार्य (vṛddhi of the root vowel). With न it expresses what ought not to be: विस्मयः न कार्यः ‘wonder is not to be made’ = ‘do not wonder’.

  • संसारस्थितिकारिणा saṃsārasthitikāriṇā

    Instrumental singular of an -in stem: कारिन् + आ → कारिणा (n → ṇ after r). It agrees with प्रभावेण, not with महामाया: it is the power that keeps saṃsāra in place.

Anvaya · prose order

(ते) संसारस्थितिकारिणा महामायाप्रभावेण (ममतावर्ते मोहगर्ते निपातिताः)। तत् अत्र विस्मयः न कार्यः। (एषा) जगत्पतेः योगनिद्रा …

(te) saṃsārasthitikāriṇā mahāmāyāprabhāveṇa (mamatāvarte mohagarte nipātitāḥ) | tat atra vismayaḥ na kāryaḥ | (eṣā) jagatpateḥ yoganidrā …

The first line completes the sentence of 1.53 (‘they are thrown into the whirlpool of mine-ness … by the power of Mahāmāyā’). Then a short main clause with a gerundive (विस्मयः न कार्यः), and the opening of a new sentence that 1.55 completes (योगनिद्रा जगत्पतेः … एषा).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The sage Medhas answers the king’s question (1.44–45: why are we attached when we see the fault?). Creatures who know better are still bound to their own, as the birds feeding their young show (1.51–53); the cause is the power of Mahāmāyā, so it is no cause for surprise. In the digital text a footnote asterisk of the printed book followed संसारस्थितिकारिणा; it has been removed (corrections.json, encoding).

Traditional interpretation

The answer turns a psychological question into a theological one: attachment is not merely a private failure but the working of the power that keeps the world in being. The same Goddess is introduced in the same breath as Viṣṇu’s Yoganidrā, the name under which Brahmā will praise her (1.69–71).

Verse 1.55

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

महामाया हरेश्चैषा तया सम्मोह्यते जगत्।ज्ञानिनामपि चेतांसि देवी भगवती हि सा॥⁠५५⁠॥

mahāmāyā hareścaiṣā tayā sammohyate jagat |jñānināmapi cetāṃsi devī bhagavatī hi sā ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

महामाया · हरेः · च · एषा · तया · सम्मोह्यते · जगत्ज्ञानिनाम् · अपि · चेतांसि · देवी · भगवती · हि · सा

mahāmāyā · hareḥ · ca · eṣā · tayā · sammohyate · jagatjñāninām · api · cetāṃsi · devī · bhagavatī · hi · sā

Word by word

  1. महामायाmahāmāyāthe Great Māyāf. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate of एषा
  2. हरेःhareḥof Hari (Viṣṇu)m. gen. sg. of हरि (i-stem)
  3. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction); joins हरेः महामाया to जगत्पतेः योगनिद्रा (1.54)
  4. एषाeṣāshe, this onepronoun एतद्, f. nom. sg.; subject
  5. तयाtayāby herpronoun तद्, f. instr. sg.; agent of the passive सम्मोह्यते
  6. सम्मोह्यतेsammohyateis deluded, is made to be bewilderedसम् + √मुह् (divādi 4P ‘to be bewildered’), causative stem मोहय-, karmaṇi prayoga, laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  7. जगत्jagatthe worldn. nom. sg. of जगत्; subject of the passive
  8. ज्ञानिनाम्jñānināmof the wise, of those who knowm. gen. pl. of ज्ञानिन् (ज्ञान + ini, ‘possessing knowledge’); depends on चेतांसि
  9. अपिapievenindeclinable (emphatic particle)
  10. चेतांसिcetāṃsithe mindsn. acc. pl. of चेतस् (s-stem); object of आकृष्य and प्रयच्छति in 1.56
  11. देवीdevīthe Goddessf. nom. sg. of देवी; predicate of सा
  12. भगवतीbhagavatīthe Blessed One, the Ladyf. nom. sg. of भगवती (भगवत् + ṅīp); qualifies देवी

Translation

— and this one is the Mahāmāyā of Hari; by her the world is deluded. The minds even of the wise — for she is the Goddess, the Blessed One —

In readable English— she is Hari’s Great Māyā, and by her the whole world is held in delusion. Even the minds of the wise — for she is the Goddess, the Blessed Lady —

The sentence is carried over from 1.54 and into 1.56, where the verbs governing चेतांसि stand.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • हरेश्चैषा hareścaiṣā → हरेः + च + एषा

    visarga sandhi and vowel sandhi (vṛddhi) · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40); वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88)

    Visarga before c becomes s, and s next to c becomes ś (हरेश्च). Then a + e → ai (चैषा).

  • ज्ञानिनामपि jñānināmapi → ज्ञानिनाम् + अपि

    no change (final m before a vowel) · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23) does not apply before a vowel

    Final m becomes anusvāra only before a consonant; before the vowel of अपि it is simply written together with it.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • महामाया mahāmāyā

    karmadhāraya

    Members
    महत् + माया
    Vigraha
    महती चासौ माया च mahatī cāsau māyā ca
    Literally
    “the great illusion-power”
    In the verse
    the Goddess as the power that veils and binds
    Alternative
    As a name it can also be taken as a bahuvrīhi, महती माया यस्याः सा ‘she whose māyā is great’; the karmadhāraya fits the identification with Yoganidrā better.
Morphology & anvaya

  • सम्मोह्यते sammohyate

    Passive of a causative: मोहय- loses its causative -ay- before the passive -ya- (मोह् + य + ते). The world is the subject; तया names the agent: ‘the world is deluded by her’.

  • चेतांसि cetāṃsi

    Neuter plural of चेतस्: the s-stems insert a nasal and lengthen the vowel in the nominative and accusative plural (चेतांसि, like मनांसि). Here accusative, looking forward to the verbs of 1.56.

Anvaya · prose order

(या) जगत्पतेः योगनिद्रा, एषा हरेः महामाया च; तया जगत् सम्मोह्यते। सा हि भगवती देवी ज्ञानिनाम् अपि चेतांसि (बलात् आकृष्य मोहाय प्रयच्छति)।

(yā) jagatpateḥ yoganidrā, eṣā hareḥ mahāmāyā ca; tayā jagat sammohyate | sā hi bhagavatī devī jñāninām api cetāṃsi (balāt ākṛṣya mohāya prayacchati) |

The first line identifies the Yoganidrā of 1.54 with Hari’s Mahāmāyā and states her work with a passive (तया सम्मोह्यते जगत्). The second line begins a sentence completed in 1.56: चेतांसि is the object of आकृष्य … प्रयच्छति there, and देवी भगवती हि सा is a parenthesis giving the reason.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Medhas names the power: Viṣṇu’s Yoganidrā is the same as Hari’s Mahāmāyā, and the whole world is deluded by her. Even the wise are not exempt — the very point the king and the merchant found puzzling about themselves (1.44).

Traditional interpretation

The verse joins two roles that the chapter keeps together: the sleep that holds Viṣṇu (the story of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, 1.66 onward) and the delusion that holds all beings. In the Śākta reading the god who sustains the world is himself subject to her, which is why his waking depends on her withdrawal (1.86–89).

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has both names: 215, महामाया, and 339, विष्णुमाया. The Devī Māhātmya itself will later praise her as Viṣṇumāyā in the hymn of chapter 5; the two works remain distinct.

Verse 1.56

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

बलादाकृष्य मोहाय महामाया प्रयच्छति।तया विसृज्यते विश्वं जगदेतच्चराचरम्॥⁠५६⁠॥

balādākṛṣya mohāya mahāmāyā prayacchati |tayā visṛjyate viśvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

  3. मोहायmohāyato delusionm. dat. sg. of मोह; dative of the end to which (with प्रयच्छति ‘hands over to’)

  8. विश्वम्viśvamentire, the wholepronominal adjective विश्व, n. nom. sg.; qualifies जगत्
  9. जगत्jagatworldn. nom. sg. of जगत्; subject of विसृज्यते
  10. एतत्etatthispronoun एतद्, n. nom. sg.; qualifies जगत्

Translation

having dragged (them) by force, Mahāmāyā hands (them) over to delusion. By her is emitted this entire world, moving and unmoving.

In readable English— Mahāmāyā seizes them by force and gives them over to delusion. It is she who brings forth this whole world of the moving and the still.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • बलादाकृष्य balādākṛṣya → बलात् + आकृष्य

    consonant sandhi (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    Final t becomes d before a vowel.

  • जगदेतच्चराचरम् jagadetaccarācaram → जगत् + एतत् + चराचरम्

    consonant sandhi (voicing; palatal assimilation) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39); स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    The t of जगत् is voiced to d before the vowel of एतत्; the t of एतत् becomes c next to the c of चराचरम्.

  • विश्वं जगद् viśvaṃ jagad → विश्वम् + जगत्

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • चराचरम् carācaram

    dvandva (samāhāra, neuter singular), used here as an attribute of जगत्

    Members
    चर + अचर
    Vigraha
    चरं च अचरं च caraṃ ca acaraṃ ca
    Literally
    “the moving and the unmoving”
    In the verse
    all beings, animate and inanimate
    Alternative
    Inside the dvandva, अचर is a nañ tatpuruṣa (न चरम्). Some take चराचर as an itaretara dvandva (चराः च अचराः च); as an adjective of the neuter singular जगत् the samāhāra form fits.
Morphology & anvaya

  • प्रयच्छति prayacchati

    √दा in the sense ‘give’ (दाण्) takes the stem यच्छ- in the present system: प्र-यच्छ-ति. With the dative मोहाय: ‘hands (them) over to delusion’.

  • आकृष्य ākṛṣya

    Absolutive with a prefix takes -य (lyap) instead of -त्वा: आ-कृष्-य ‘having dragged’. Its subject is the subject of the main verb, Mahāmāyā.

  • विसृज्यते visṛjyate

    Passive present of वि + √सृज्: ‘is emitted’, the Purāṇic word for creation as outflow (visarga).

Anvaya · prose order

(सा) महामाया ज्ञानिनाम् अपि चेतांसि बलात् आकृष्य मोहाय प्रयच्छति। तया एतत् विश्वं चराचरं जगत् विसृज्यते।

(sā) mahāmāyā jñāninām api cetāṃsi balāt ākṛṣya mohāya prayacchati | tayā etat viśvaṃ carācaraṃ jagat visṛjyate |

The first line completes the sentence begun in 1.55 (object चेतांसि); the second is a passive sentence with तया as agent.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Two works of the one Goddess are named: she forcibly binds even the wise in delusion, and she emits the entire world. Delusion and creation are put side by side as acts of the same power.

Traditional interpretation

The force (बलात्) is stressed: knowledge alone does not free a person from attachment, which is why the next verse turns to her grace (प्रसन्ना). The tradition reads the sequence 1.55–58 as the theological core of Medhas’s teaching, to which the three caritas are the illustration.

Translation

She, this one, when pleased, becomes boon-giving to men for liberation. She is the supreme knowledge, the eternal cause of liberation,

In readable EnglishAnd when she is pleased, this same Goddess grants human beings the boon of liberation. She is the supreme knowledge, the eternal cause of freedom —

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सैषा saiṣā → सा + एषा

    vowel sandhi (vṛddhi) · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88)

    ā + e → ai.

  • नृणां भवति nṛṇāṃ bhavati → नृणाम् + भवति

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

  • मुक्तेर्हेतुभूता mukterhetubhūtā → मुक्तेः + हेतुभूता

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    Visarga after a vowel other than a/ā, before a voiced sound, appears as r.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • वरदा varadā

    upapada tatpuruṣa (√दा with the kṛt affix -a after its object)

    Members
    वर + दा
    Vigraha
    वरं ददाति इति varaṃ dadāti iti
    Literally
    “giving a boon”
    In the verse
    gracious, granting what is sought

  • हेतुभूता hetubhūtā

    karmadhāraya-type compound with भूत ‘being’ as final member

    Members
    हेतु + भूत
    Vigraha
    हेतुः भूता hetuḥ bhūtā
    Literally
    “become the cause”
    In the verse
    who is the cause (of liberation)
    Alternative
    Grammarians also class such -भूत compounds as supsupā (‘nominal with nominal’) compounds; the sense ‘serving as the cause’ is unaffected.
Morphology & anvaya

  • प्रसन्ना prasannā

    Past participle of प्र + √सद् with the -na variant of the kta affix (सद् + न → सन्न): ‘settled, clear’, hence ‘pleased, gracious’.

  • नृणाम् nṛṇām

    Genitive plural of the ṛ-stem नृ: नृ + नाम् → नृणाम् (n → ṇ after ṛ). The long form नॄणाम् is equally correct.

  • सनातनी sanātanī

    Feminine of सनातन ‘eternal’ formed with ṅīp (-ī) rather than -ā.

Anvaya · prose order

सा एषा प्रसन्ना (सती) नृणां मुक्तये वरदा भवति। सा परमा विद्या, सनातनी, मुक्तेः हेतुभूता (च)।

sā eṣā prasannā (satī) nṛṇāṃ muktaye varadā bhavati | sā paramā vidyā, sanātanī, mukteḥ hetubhūtā (ca) |

Two clauses: a verbal one (सा … वरदा भवति) with a dative of purpose, and a nominal one (सा विद्या परमा … हेतुभूता सनातनी) that 1.58 continues.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The power that binds (1.55–56) is the same power that frees. When she is gracious she grants liberation; as supreme knowledge she is its eternal cause.

Traditional interpretation

The Śākta tradition reads this verse with 1.58 as the key to the text: bondage and release both come from her, so release is sought by turning to her, not by escaping her. The rest of the Devī Māhātmya — and Suratha’s and Samādhi’s boons in chapter 13 — is the working out of प्रसन्ना वरदा.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names her 402, विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपिणी, ‘whose form is both knowledge and ignorance’, and 331, वरदा. The pairing of binding and freeing in one Goddess is common Śākta ground; the texts are separate.

Verse 1.58

Translation

and the cause of the bondage of saṃsāra; she alone is the sovereign of the sovereigns of all.

In readable Englishand the cause of bondage to worldly existence. She alone is sovereign over all who rule.

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    Visarga before c → s → ś.

  • सैव saiva → सा + एव

    vowel sandhi (vṛddhi) · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88)

    ā + e → ai.

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa, twice) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + ī → e at both seams.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • संसारबन्धहेतुः saṃsārabandhahetuḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa containing a karmadhāraya (संसारबन्ध, avadhāraṇa: ‘the bondage that is saṃsāra’)

    Members
    संसारबन्ध + हेतु
    Vigraha
    संसार एव बन्धः संसारबन्धः; तस्य हेतुः saṃsāra eva bandhaḥ saṃsārabandhaḥ; tasya hetuḥ
    Literally
    “cause of the saṃsāra-bondage”
    In the verse
    she is the reason beings are bound to the round of births
    Alternative
    संसारबन्ध can also be a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, संसारस्य बन्धः ‘the bondage of (belonging to) saṃsāra’; the meaning hardly differs.

  • सर्वेश्वरेश्वरी sarveśvareśvarī

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    सर्वेश्वर + ईश्वरी
    Vigraha
    सर्वेषाम् ईश्वराः सर्वेश्वराः; तेषाम् ईश्वरी sarveṣām īśvarāḥ sarveśvarāḥ; teṣām īśvarī
    Literally
    “ruler of the rulers of all”
    In the verse
    sovereign even over the gods who rule the world
    Alternative
    Or सर्वस्य ईश्वरः सर्वेश्वरः (the Lord of all, i.e. Viṣṇu or Śiva), तस्य ईश्वरी ‘ruler of the Lord of all’. Either way she stands above the highest god — which fits a verse spoken of Viṣṇu’s Yoganidrā.
Morphology & anvaya

  • संसारबन्धहेतुः saṃsārabandhahetuḥ

    A feminine subject with a masculine predicate noun: हेतु is a masculine noun and does not change gender to agree, as in English ‘she is the cause’.

Anvaya · prose order

सा एव संसारबन्धहेतुः च, सर्वेश्वरेश्वरी (च)।

sā eva saṃsārabandhahetuḥ ca, sarveśvareśvarī (ca) |

A nominal sentence continuing 1.57: सा (subject) with two predicates.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The teaching closes on its paradox: the cause of liberation (1.57) is also the cause of bondage, and she alone (सैव) is both. She is therefore above every ruling power, including the gods.

Traditional interpretation

With this half-verse Medhas’s answer to the king is complete, and the king’s next question (1.60–62) follows from it: who is this Goddess? The three caritas are told as the answer.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: what holds us and what frees us may not be two different things. The same capacity for attachment that binds a parent to a child (the birds of 1.51–52) is, turned rightly, the capacity for devotion.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • महामायेति mahāmāyeti → महामाया + इति

    vowel sandhi (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    ā + i → e.

  • यां भवान् yāṃ bhavān → याम् + भवान्

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • भवान् bhavān

    The polite pronoun भवत् takes a third-person verb: भवान् … ब्रवीति (1.61) ‘your honour says’, not ‘you say’ in the second person.

  • भगवन् bhagavan

    Vocative of the -vat stem भगवत्: भगवन् (nominative भगवान्).

Anvaya · prose order

भगवन्, यां भवान् महामाया इति (ब्रवीति), सा देवी का हि?

bhagavan, yāṃ bhavān mahāmāyā iti (bravīti), sā devī kā hi?

A direct question (का हि सा देवी) with a relative clause (यां भवान् … ब्रवीति) whose verb stands at the start of 1.61.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king takes up the name the sage used (1.55–56) and asks who she is. The question is the hinge of the whole text: everything that follows, through chapter 13, is Medhas’s answer.

Traditional interpretation

Suratha’s questions in 1.60–62 — who she is, how she arose, what she does, her power, her nature, her origin — are traditionally read as the plan of the Devī Māhātmya: the three caritas show her arising and her deeds, and the hymns show her nature.

bravīti kathamutpannā sā karmāsyāśca kiṃ dvija |yatprabhāvā ca sā devī yatsvarūpā yadudbhavā ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

ब्रवीति · कथम् · उत्पन्ना · सा · कर्म · अस्याः · च · किम् · द्विजयत्प्रभावा · च · सा · देवी · यत्स्वरूपा · यदुद्भवा

bravīti · katham · utpannā · sā · karma · asyāḥ · ca · kim · dvijayatprabhāvā · ca · sā · devī · yatsvarūpā · yadudbhavā

Word by word

  1. ब्रवीतिbravīti(you) call, speak of√ब्रू (adādi 2U ‘to speak’), laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada; its subject is भवान् (1.60)
  2. कथम्kathamhowindeclinable (interrogative adverb)
  3. उत्पन्नाutpannāarisen, bornpast participle (kta) of उद् + √पद् (divādi 4Ā ‘to go’; with उद् ‘to arise’), f. nom. sg.; predicate of सा
  4. साsāshepronoun तद्, f. nom. sg.
  5. कर्मkarmadeed, workn. nom. sg. of कर्मन्
  6. अस्याःasyāḥherpronoun इदम्, f. gen. sg.
  7. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  8. किम्kimwhatinterrogative pronoun किम्, n. nom. sg.; predicate of कर्म
  9. द्विजdvijaO twice-born (brāhmaṇa)m. voc. sg. of द्विज
  10. यत्प्रभावाyatprabhāvāof what powerf. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate of सा देवी (indirect question)
  11. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  12. साsāthatpronoun तद्, f. nom. sg.; qualifies देवी
  13. देवीdevīGoddessf. nom. sg. of देवी; subject
  14. यत्स्वरूपाyatsvarūpāof what naturef. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)
  15. यदुद्भवाyadudbhavāof what origin, arising from whatf. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)

Translation

— calls (Mahāmāyā): how did she arise, and what is her deed, O twice-born? And of what power that Goddess is, of what nature, of what origin —

In readable EnglishHow did she come to be, O brāhmaṇa, and what are her deeds? What is her power, what her true nature, and from where does she arise?

कर्म is singular (‘deed’); the readable version renders it as the collective ‘deeds’.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • कथमुत्पन्ना kathamutpannā → कथम् + उत्पन्ना

    no change (final m before a vowel) · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23) applies only before a consonant

    The m stays m and is written together with the following vowel.

  • कर्मास्याश्च karmāsyāśca → कर्म + अस्याः + च

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) and visarga sandhi · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101); विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    a + a → ā; then the visarga of अस्याः before c becomes ś.

  • यदुद्भवा yadudbhavā → यत् + उद्भवा

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    The t of the pronoun stem becomes d before a vowel.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • यत्प्रभावा yatprabhāvā

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    यद् + प्रभाव
    Vigraha
    यः प्रभावः यस्याः सा yaḥ prabhāvaḥ yasyāḥ sā
    Literally
    “she whose power is which”
    In the verse
    what her power is
    Alternative
    The relative pronoun here does the work of an indirect interrogative (‘of what power’); all three compounds are resumed by तत्सर्वम् in 1.62.

  • यत्स्वरूपा yatsvarūpā

    bahuvrīhi (स्वरूप is itself a karmadhāraya: स्वम् रूपम्)

    Members
    यद् + स्वरूप
    Vigraha
    यत् स्वरूपं यस्याः सा yat svarūpaṃ yasyāḥ sā
    Literally
    “she whose own form is which”
    In the verse
    what her true nature is

  • यदुद्भवा yadudbhavā

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    यद् + उद्भव
    Vigraha
    यतः उद्भवः यस्याः सा yataḥ udbhavaḥ yasyāḥ sā
    Literally
    “she whose arising is from which”
    In the verse
    where she comes from
    Alternative
    Or यः उद्भवः यस्याः ‘she whose origin is which’; the sense is the same.
Morphology & anvaya

  • ब्रवीति bravīti

    √ब्रू inserts ī before consonant-initial strong endings: ब्रव् + ई + ति. Third person because the subject is the honorific भवान् (1.60).

  • उत्पन्ना utpannā

    Past participle of उद् + √पद् with the -na affix (पद् + न → पन्न; d + t → tt, ud-panna → utpanna). Used as a finite past: ‘how did she arise?’

Anvaya · prose order

(यां भवान् महामाया इति) ब्रवीति। द्विज, सा कथम् उत्पन्ना? अस्याः कर्म च किम्? सा देवी यत्प्रभावा, यत्स्वरूपा, यदुद्भवा च, …

(yāṃ bhavān mahāmāyā iti) bravīti | dvija, sā katham utpannā? asyāḥ karma ca kim? sā devī yatprabhāvā, yatsvarūpā, yadudbhavā ca, …

The first word completes the relative clause of 1.60. Two direct questions follow (कथम् … किम्), then three indirect questions in compound form, resumed by तत्सर्वम् in 1.62.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king asks six things: how she arose, what she does, her power, her nature, her origin — and, in 1.62, he asks to hear it all. He addresses Medhas as द्विज, a brāhmaṇa.

Traditional interpretation

The sage’s answer (1.64–66) qualifies the first question at once: she is eternal, and is said to ‘arise’ only when she becomes manifest for the gods’ work. The questions about power and nature are answered less by definition than by the stories and the hymns.

Verse 1.62

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh

तत्सर्वं श्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तो ब्रह्मविदां वर॥⁠६२⁠॥

tatsarvaṃ śrotumicchāmi tvatto brahmavidāṃ vara ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

तत् · सर्वम् · श्रोतुम् · इच्छामि · त्वत्तः · ब्रह्मविदाम् · वर

tat · sarvam · śrotum · icchāmi · tvattaḥ · brahmavidām · vara

Word by word

  1. तत्tatthatpronoun तद्, n. acc. sg.; qualifies सर्वम्
  2. सर्वम्sarvamallpronominal adjective सर्व, n. acc. sg.; object of श्रोतुम्
  3. श्रोतुम्śrotumto hearinfinitive (tumun) of √श्रु (bhvādi 1P ‘to hear’ in the Dhātupāṭha, with the class-5 present शृणोति)
  4. इच्छामिicchāmiI wish√इष् (tudādi 6P ‘to wish’, present stem इच्छ-), laṭ (present), uttama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  5. त्वत्तःtvattaḥfrom youpronoun युष्मद् with the ablative suffix -tas (त्वत् + तसिल्); indeclinable ablative
  6. ब्रह्मविदाम्brahmavidāmamong the knowers of Brahmanm. gen. pl. of ब्रह्मविद्; compound (see Samāsa); genitive of the group (nirdhāraṇa) with वर
  7. वरvaraO bestm. voc. sg. of वर

Translation

All that I wish to hear from you, O best of the knowers of Brahman.

In readable EnglishAll this I long to hear from you, O best of those who know Brahman.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तत्सर्वं tatsarvaṃ → तत् + सर्वम्

    no change (unvoiced before unvoiced); anusvāra · खरि च (8.4.55); मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    The t stays unvoiced before s; the final m of सर्वम् becomes anusvāra before the consonant of श्रोतुम्.

  • श्रोतुमिच्छामि śrotumicchāmi → श्रोतुम् + इच्छामि

    no change (final m before a vowel) · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23) applies only before a consonant

    The m is written together with the following vowel.

  • त्वत्तो ब्रह्मविदां tvatto brahmavidāṃ → त्वत्तः + ब्रह्मविदाम्

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced b becomes -o.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • ब्रह्मविदाम् brahmavidām

    upapada tatpuruṣa (√विद् with the zero kṛt affix kvip after its object)

    Members
    ब्रह्मन् + विद्
    Vigraha
    ब्रह्म विदन्ति इति ब्रह्मविदः, तेषाम् brahma vidanti iti brahmavidaḥ, teṣām
    Literally
    “of the Brahman-knowers”
    In the verse
    among those who know the ultimate reality
Morphology & anvaya

  • श्रोतुम् śrotum

    Infinitive in -tum with guṇa of the root vowel (श्रु → श्रो-तुम्), complement of इच्छामि: ‘I wish to hear’.

  • त्वत्तः tvattaḥ

    The -tas ablative of the pronoun: त्वत्तः ‘from you’ (equivalent to त्वत्), regular with verbs of hearing and learning.

Anvaya · prose order

ब्रह्मविदां वर, तत् सर्वं त्वत्तः श्रोतुम् इच्छामि।

brahmavidāṃ vara, tat sarvaṃ tvattaḥ śrotum icchāmi |

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The king’s request closes: he wants to hear all of it from the sage, whom he honours as the best of Brahman-knowers. Medhas begins his answer at once (1.63).

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the king who has lost his kingdom does not ask for it back here; he asks to understand. The text lets the desire to know come before the desire to regain.

ṛṣiḥ uvāca |

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Medhas answers King Suratha (with the merchant Samādhi listening) in his hermitage. His answer runs from the Goddess’s eternity (1.64) into the first story, the slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha.

Verse 1.64

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

नित्यैव सा जगन्मूर्तिस्तया सर्वमिदं ततम्॥⁠६४⁠॥

nityaiva sā jaganmūrtistayā sarvamidaṃ tatam ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

नित्या · एव · सा · जगन्मूर्तिः · तया · सर्वम् · इदम् · ततम्

nityā · eva · sā · jaganmūrtiḥ · tayā · sarvam · idam · tatam

Word by word

  1. नित्याnityāeternalf. nom. sg. of नित्य; predicate of सा
  2. एवevatruly, in fact (she is eternal — not born)indeclinable (restrictive particle)
  3. साsāshepronoun तद्, f. nom. sg.; subject
  4. जगन्मूर्तिःjaganmūrtiḥshe whose form is the worldf. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); second predicate
  5. तयाtayāby herpronoun तद्, f. instr. sg.; agent with ततम्
  6. सर्वम्sarvamallpronominal adjective सर्व, n. nom. sg.; qualifies इदम्
  7. इदम्idamthispronoun इदम्, n. nom. sg.; subject
  8. ततम्tatampervaded, spread throughpast participle (kta) of √तन् (tanādi 8U ‘to stretch, extend’), n. nom. sg.; predicate

Translation

She is eternal indeed, having the world as her form; by her all this is pervaded.

In readable EnglishShe is eternal; the world is her very form, and by her all this is pervaded.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • नित्यैव nityaiva → नित्या + एव

    vowel sandhi (vṛddhi) · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88)

    ā + e → ai.

  • जगन्मूर्तिस्तया jaganmūrtistayā → जगन्मूर्तिः + तया

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

  • जगन्मूर्ति jaganmūrti → जगत् + मूर्ति

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (nasal assimilation) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45)

    t before the nasal m becomes the nasal n.

  • सर्वमिदं ततम् sarvamidaṃ tatam → सर्वम् + इदम् + ततम्

    final m before vowel and before consonant · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    सर्वम् keeps its m before the vowel of इदम्; इदम् shows anusvāra before the t of ततम्.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • जगन्मूर्तिः jaganmūrtiḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    जगत् + मूर्ति
    Vigraha
    जगत् मूर्तिः यस्याः सा jagat mūrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā
    Literally
    “she whose embodied form is the world”
    In the verse
    the world is her body
    Alternative
    Also possible as a karmadhāraya, जगत् एव मूर्तिः ‘the world-form’, predicated of her; the bahuvrīhi suits a feminine subject described by a compound.
Morphology & anvaya

  • ततम् tatam

    Past participle of √तन्: the root-final nasal is dropped before -ta (तन् + त → तत). ‘Stretched out, pervaded’.

Anvaya · prose order

सा नित्या एव, जगन्मूर्तिः; तया इदं सर्वं ततम्।

sā nityā eva, jaganmūrtiḥ; tayā idaṃ sarvaṃ tatam |

Two nominal sentences: a description of her (नित्या एव … जगन्मूर्तिः) and a passive statement with a participle as predicate (तया … ततम्).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The sage’s first answer corrects the king’s first question (‘how did she arise?’, 1.61): she is eternal and has no birth. The world is her form, and all of it is filled by her.

Traditional interpretation

The phrase तया सर्वमिदं ततम् echoes the Bhagavad Gītā’s language for the pervading Absolute (येन सर्वमिदं ततम्, 2.17; मया ततमिदं सर्वम्, 9.4). The Devī Māhātmya applies to the Goddess what the Gītā says of the imperishable and of Kṛṣṇa.

Word by word

In readable EnglishEven so, hear from me how she comes forth, again and again. When she becomes manifest to accomplish the purpose of the gods,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तथापि tathāpi → तथा + अपि

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    ā + a → ā.

  • तत्समुत्पत्तिर्बहुधा tatsamutpattirbahudhā → तत्समुत्पत्तिः + बहुधा

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    Visarga after i, before the voiced b, appears as r.

  • कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थमाविर्भवति kāryasiddhyarthamāvirbhavati → कार्यसिद्धि + अर्थम् + आविर्भवति

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (yaṇ); final m before a vowel · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    The i of सिद्धि becomes y before अर्थ (सिद्ध्यर्थ); the final m of the compound is written together with the vowel of आविर्भवति.

  • आविर्भवति āvirbhavati → आविस् + भवति

    visarga (s) sandhi before a voiced consonant · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    The s of the gati आविस् becomes r before the voiced bh.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • तत्समुत्पत्तिः tatsamutpattiḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    तद् + समुत्पत्ति
    Vigraha
    तस्याः समुत्पत्तिः tasyāḥ samutpattiḥ
    Literally
    “the arising of her”
    In the verse
    the occasions of her appearing
    Alternative
    The pronoun stem तद् serves for every gender inside a compound; here it stands for the feminine तस्याः.

  • कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थम् kāryasiddhyartham

    caturthī tatpuruṣa (with अर्थ, always compounded; used adverbially in the accusative)

    Members
    कार्यसिद्धि + अर्थ
    Vigraha
    कार्यसिद्धये इदम् kāryasiddhaye idam
    Literally
    “for the sake of task-accomplishment”
    In the verse
    to bring about what the gods need done
    Alternative
    The first member कार्यसिद्धि is a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, कार्यस्य सिद्धिः; देवानाम् outside the compound depends on कार्य inside it.
Morphology & anvaya

  • श्रूयताम् śrūyatām

    Passive imperative: श्रू-य-ताम् (the root vowel lengthened before the passive -ya). The courteous Sanskrit way of saying ‘listen’: ‘let (it) be heard (from me)’.

  • आविर्भवति āvirbhavati

    आविस् ‘openly, visibly’ is a gati that combines with √भू and √कृ: आविर्भवति ‘becomes visible, appears’. It describes manifestation, not birth — the key to the sage’s answer.

Anvaya · prose order

तथा अपि मम (मत्तः) तत्समुत्पत्तिः बहुधा श्रूयताम्। यदा सा देवानां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थम् आविर्भवति, (तदा …)

tathā api mama (mattaḥ) tatsamutpattiḥ bahudhā śrūyatām | yadā sā devānāṃ kāryasiddhyartham āvirbhavati, (tadā …)

A passive imperative sentence, then a यदा clause whose main clause (तदा …) is in 1.66.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Although she is eternal, she has many ‘arisings’, and the sage will tell them. Each is a manifestation (आविर्भाव) for the gods’ need — the pattern of all three caritas.

Traditional interpretation

The three caritas — the slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, of Mahiṣa, and of Śumbha and Niśumbha — are traditionally read as three such manifestations. The Gita Press pāṭha assigns them the presiding forms Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī and Mahāsarasvatī; that assignment is liturgical tradition, not stated in this verse.

Verse 1.66

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

उत्पन्नेति तदा लोके सा नित्याप्यभिधीयते।योगनिद्रां यदा विष्णुर्जगत्येकार्णवीकृते॥⁠६६⁠॥

utpanneti tadā loke sā nityāpyabhidhīyate |yoganidrāṃ yadā viṣṇurjagatyekārṇavīkṛte ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

उत्पन्ना · इति · तदा · लोके · सा · नित्या · अपि · अभिधीयतेयोगनिद्राम् · यदा · विष्णुः · जगति · एकार्णवीकृते

utpannā · iti · tadā · loke · sā · nityā · api · abhidhīyateyoganidrām · yadā · viṣṇuḥ · jagati · ekārṇavīkṛte

Word by word

  1. उत्पन्नाutpannāborn, arisenpast participle (kta) of उद् + √पद्, f. nom. sg.; the word quoted by इति
  2. इतिiti(as) ‘…’indeclinable (quotation marker)
  3. तदाtadāthenindeclinable (correlative adverb of time, answering यदा in 1.65)
  4. लोकेlokein the world, among peoplem. loc. sg. of लोक
  5. साsāshepronoun तद्, f. nom. sg.; subject
  6. नित्याnityāeternalf. nom. sg. of नित्य; concessive with अपि
  7. अपिapithoughindeclinable (concessive particle)
  8. अभिधीयतेabhidhīyateis called, is spoken ofअभि + √धा (juhotyādi 3U ‘to place’; with अभि ‘to name’), karmaṇi prayoga, laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  9. योगनिद्राम्yoganidrāmthe Yoganidrā, yogic sleepf. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa, 1.54); object of अभजत् (1.67)
  10. यदाyadāwhenindeclinable (relative adverb of time); correlative of तदा in 1.67
  11. विष्णुःviṣṇuḥViṣṇum. nom. sg. of विष्णु (u-stem); subject of अभजत् (1.67)
  12. जगतिjagatithe worldn. loc. sg. of जगत्; locative absolute with एकार्णवीकृते
  13. एकार्णवीकृतेekārṇavīkṛtehaving been made a single oceanpast participle (kta) of √कृ with the cvi formation एकार्णवी-, n. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); locative absolute

Translation

— then in the world she, though eternal, is called ‘born’. When Viṣṇu, the world having been made one ocean, (resorted to) Yoganidrā —

In readable Englishthen, though eternal, she is said in the world to be ‘born’. At the end of an age, when the world had become a single ocean and Viṣṇu entered his yogic sleep,

‘At the end of an age’ is drawn from कल्पान्ते in 1.67, and ‘entered’ renders अभजत् there.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • उत्पन्नेति utpanneti → उत्पन्ना + इति

    vowel sandhi (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    ā + i → e.

  • नित्याप्यभिधीयते nityāpyabhidhīyate → नित्या + अपि + अभिधीयते

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha; yaṇ) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101); इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    ā + a → ā; then the i of अपि becomes y before the a of अभिधीयते.

  • विष्णुर्जगत्येकार्णवीकृते viṣṇurjagatyekārṇavīkṛte → विष्णुः + जगति + एकार्णवीकृते

    visarga sandhi; vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66); इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Visarga after u before the voiced j appears as r; the i of जगति becomes y before e.

  • योगनिद्रां यदा yoganidrāṃ yadā → योगनिद्राम् + यदा

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • एकार्णवीकृते ekārṇavīkṛte

    gati tatpuruṣa with a cvi formation (a thing made into what it was not: the final a of एकार्णव becomes ī)

    Members
    एकार्णव + (cvi) + कृत
    Vigraha
    अनेकार्णवम् एकार्णवं कृतम् इति एकार्णवीकृतम्, तस्मिन् anekārṇavam ekārṇavaṃ kṛtam iti ekārṇavīkṛtam, tasmin
    Literally
    “made into one ocean”
    In the verse
    when the whole world was flooded into a single sea at the dissolution
    Alternative
    The inner member एकार्णव is a karmadhāraya, एकः च असौ अर्णवः च ‘one ocean’, with savarṇa-dīrgha (एक + अर्णव).
Morphology & anvaya

  • एकार्णवीकृते ekārṇavīkṛte

    cvi construction: a noun + ī + a form of √कृ/√भू means ‘make (become) what was not before’ — एकार्णवी-कृत ‘made one ocean’. In the locative with जगति it is a locative absolute: ‘when the world had been made one ocean’.

  • अभिधीयते abhidhīyate

    Passive of अभि + √धा: the root vowel becomes ī before the passive -ya (धी-य-ते). ‘Is named’.

Anvaya · prose order

(यदा सा … आविर्भवति,) तदा सा नित्या अपि लोके उत्पन्ना इति अभिधीयते। (कल्पान्ते) जगति एकार्णवीकृते यदा विष्णुः योगनिद्राम् (अभजत्), …

(yadā sā … āvirbhavati,) tadā sā nityā api loke utpannā iti abhidhīyate | (kalpānte) jagati ekārṇavīkṛte yadā viṣṇuḥ yoganidrām (abhajat), …

The first line is the main clause answering यदा in 1.65 (तदा … अभिधीयते). The second line opens a new यदा clause whose verb अभजत् and main clause (तदा …) are in 1.67.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The answer to ‘how did she arise?’ is completed: her ‘birth’ is a way of speaking about her appearing. The second line begins the first story, set at the dissolution, when the world is one ocean and Viṣṇu lies in yogic sleep.

Traditional interpretation

The distinction between eternal being and occasional manifestation governs the whole text: the Goddess of the three caritas is not three goddesses but one, appearing as the need arises. The idea runs parallel to Bhagavad Gītā 4.6–8 (अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा …), where the Lord, though unborn, comes into being from age to age for the protection of the good.

Verse 1.67

āstīrya śeṣamabhajatkalpānte bhagavān prabhuḥ |tadā dvāvasurau ghorau vikhyātau madhukaiṭabhau ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

āstīrya · śeṣam · abhajat · kalpānte · bhagavān · prabhuḥtadā · dvau · asurau · ghorau · vikhyātau · madhukaiṭabhau

Word by word

  3. अभजत्abhajatresorted to, entered√भज् (bhvādi 1U ‘to share, resort to’), laṅ (imperfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada; object योगनिद्राम् (1.66)
  4. कल्पान्तेkalpānteat the end of the kalpa (world-age)m. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)
  5. भगवान्bhagavānthe Blessed Onem. nom. sg. of भगवत्; qualifies विष्णुः (1.66)
  6. प्रभुःprabhuḥthe Lordm. nom. sg. of प्रभु (u-stem); qualifies विष्णुः
  7. तदाtadāthenindeclinable (correlative adverb of time, answering यदा in 1.66)
  8. द्वौdvautwonumeral द्वि, m. nom. du.
  9. असुरौasurauasuras, demonsm. nom. du. of असुर; subject (verb उद्यतौ in 1.68)
  10. घोरौghorauterriblem. nom. du. of घोर; qualifies असुरौ
  11. विख्यातौvikhyātaurenownedpast participle (kta) of वि + √ख्या (adādi 2P ‘to be known’), m. nom. du.
  12. मधुकैटभौmadhukaiṭabhauMadhu and Kaiṭabham. nom. du.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to असुरौ

Translation

— having spread out Śeṣa, the Blessed Lord resorted (to it) at the end of the kalpa; then two terrible asuras, the renowned Madhu and Kaiṭabha,

In readable Englishspreading out the serpent Śeṣa as his couch — then two dreadful asuras, the notorious Madhu and Kaiṭabha,

The readable version keeps the verse’s order across 1.66–68; ‘the Blessed Lord’ and ‘at the end of the kalpa’ are rendered in 1.66’s readable line.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • शेषमभजत्कल्पान्ते śeṣamabhajatkalpānte → शेषम् + अभजत् + कल्पान्ते

    final m before a vowel; t before an unvoiced stop · खरि च (8.4.55)

    शेषम् keeps its m before the vowel of अभजत्; the t of अभजत् stays unvoiced before k and is written together.

  • कल्पान्ते kalpānte → कल्प + अन्ते

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + a → ā.

  • द्वावसुरौ dvāvasurau → द्वौ + असुरौ

    vowel sandhi (āv) · एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78)

    Final au before a vowel becomes āv: dvāv-asurau.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • कल्पान्ते kalpānte

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    कल्प + अन्त
    Vigraha
    कल्पस्य अन्तः, तस्मिन् kalpasya antaḥ, tasmin
    Literally
    “at the end of the kalpa”
    In the verse
    at the dissolution, when one day of Brahmā closes

  • मधुकैटभौ madhukaiṭabhau

    itaretara dvandva (dual)

    Members
    मधु + कैटभ
    Vigraha
    मधुः च कैटभः च madhuḥ ca kaiṭabhaḥ ca
    Literally
    “Madhu and Kaiṭabha”
    In the verse
    the two asuras of the first carita
Morphology & anvaya

  • आस्तीर्य āstīrya

    Absolutive of आ + √स्तॄ: the root ṝ becomes īr before -ya (स्तॄ → स्तीर्). ‘Having spread out Śeṣa’ — the serpent as Viṣṇu’s couch.

  • अभजत् abhajat

    Imperfect of √भज्: augment a- + bhaja- + t. Its object योगनिद्राम् stands in the previous verse: ‘he took to yogic sleep’.

  • द्वौ dvau

    The numeral द्वि is declined only in the dual: m. nom. द्वौ.

Anvaya · prose order

(यदा) भगवान् प्रभुः विष्णुः कल्पान्ते (जगति एकार्णवीकृते) शेषम् आस्तीर्य योगनिद्राम् अभजत्, तदा घोरौ विख्यातौ मधुकैटभौ द्वौ असुरौ (विष्णुकर्णमलोद्भूतौ ब्रह्माणं हन्तुम् उद्यतौ)।

(yadā) bhagavān prabhuḥ viṣṇuḥ kalpānte (jagati ekārṇavīkṛte) śeṣam āstīrya yoganidrām abhajat, tadā ghorau vikhyātau madhukaiṭabhau dvau asurau (viṣṇukarṇamalodbhūtau brahmāṇaṃ hantum udyatau) |

The first line ends the यदा clause begun in 1.66; the second begins the main clause (तदा …), whose predicate उद्यतौ is in 1.68.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The scene is set: at the dissolution, Viṣṇu lies on the serpent Śeṣa in yogic sleep on the single ocean. Two asuras, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, appear.

Traditional interpretation

Śeṣa (‘the remainder’) is the serpent who remains when all else is dissolved. The first carita is traditionally presided over by Mahākālī in the Gita Press pāṭha; that is liturgical tradition, not stated in the text.

— sprung from the wax of Viṣṇu’s ears, were intent on killing Brahmā. He, Brahmā, the lord of creatures, stationed on the navel-lotus of Viṣṇu,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • हन्तुं ब्रह्माणमुद्यतौ hantuṃ brahmāṇamudyatau → हन्तुम् + ब्रह्माणम् + उद्यतौ

    हन्तुम् shows anusvāra before b; ब्रह्माणम् keeps its m before the vowel of उद्यतौ.

  • स नाभिकमले sa nābhikamale → सः + नाभिकमले

    visarga sandhi (special rule for सः) · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132)

    The visarga of सः is dropped before a consonant.

  • स्थितो ब्रह्मा sthito brahmā → स्थितः + ब्रह्मा

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced b becomes -o.

  • विष्णुकर्णमलोद्भूतौ viṣṇukarṇamalodbhūtau → विष्णुकर्णमल + उद्भूतौ

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + u → o.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • विष्णुकर्णमलोद्भूतौ viṣṇukarṇamalodbhūtau

    pañcamī tatpuruṣa containing two ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣas (विष्णुकर्ण, विष्णुकर्णमल)

    Members
    विष्णुकर्णमल + उद्भूत
    Vigraha
    विष्णोः कर्णौ विष्णुकर्णौ; तयोः मलम् विष्णुकर्णमलम्; तस्मात् उद्भूतौ viṣṇoḥ karṇau viṣṇukarṇau; tayoḥ malam viṣṇukarṇamalam; tasmāt udbhūtau
    Literally
    “arisen from the dirt of Viṣṇu’s ears”
    In the verse

  • नाभिकमले nābhikamale

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    नाभि + कमल
    Vigraha
    नाभेः कमलम्, तस्मिन् nābheḥ kamalam, tasmin
    Literally
    “on the lotus of the navel”
    In the verse

    Alternative
    Or saptamī tatpuruṣa, नाभौ कमलम् ‘the lotus at the navel’; the sense is the same. विष्णोः outside the compound depends on its first member.

  • प्रजापतिः prajāpatiḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    प्रजा + पति
    Vigraha

    Literally
    “lord of offspring”
    In the verse
