Morphology & anvaya

  • उद्यतौ udyatau

    Past participle of उद् + √यम्: the nasal is dropped before -ta (यम् + त → यत). Used as a finite verb: ‘the two were ready (to kill)’, with the infinitive हन्तुम्.

  • ब्रह्माणम् brahmāṇam

    Accusative of the masculine n-stem ब्रह्मन् (the god Brahmā): strong stem ब्रह्माण्-. The neuter ब्रह्मन् (Brahman) is a different word.

Anvaya · prose order

(तौ असुरौ) विष्णुकर्णमलोद्भूतौ ब्रह्माणं हन्तुम् उद्यतौ। विष्णोः नाभिकमले स्थितः सः प्रजापतिः ब्रह्मा (तौ असुरौ … दृष्ट्वा … तुष्टाव)।

(tau asurau) viṣṇukarṇamalodbhūtau brahmāṇaṃ hantum udyatau | viṣṇoḥ nābhikamale sthitaḥ saḥ prajāpatiḥ brahmā (tau asurau … dṛṣṭvā … tuṣṭāva) |

The first line completes the main clause of 1.67. The second introduces the subject (सः … ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः) of a sentence whose verb, तुष्टाव, is in 1.69.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The asuras are born from the sleeping Viṣṇu’s own ear-wax and set out to kill Brahmā, who sits on the lotus from Viṣṇu’s navel. The creator is threatened by what comes from the sustainer while the sustainer sleeps.

Traditional interpretation

The tradition reads the image closely: danger arises from Viṣṇu himself while he is held by Yoganidrā, and Brahmā cannot wake him directly. He must turn to the power that holds Viṣṇu — the Goddess.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: what threatens creation is born of the sleeper’s own neglect. The remedy the story offers is not force but praise — attention turned to the power at work.

Verse 1.69

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

दृष्ट्वा तावसुरौ चोग्रौ प्रसुप्तं च जनार्दनम्।तुष्टाव योगनिद्रां तामेकाग्रहृदयस्थितः॥⁠६९⁠॥

dṛṣṭvā tāvasurau cograu prasuptaṃ ca janārdanam |tuṣṭāva yoganidrāṃ tāmekāgrahṛdayasthitaḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

दृष्ट्वा · तौ · असुरौ · च · उग्रौ · प्रसुप्तम् · च · जनार्दनम्तुष्टाव · योगनिद्राम् · ताम् · एकाग्रहृदयस्थितः

dṛṣṭvā · tau · asurau · ca · ugrau · prasuptam · ca · janārdanamtuṣṭāva · yoganidrām · tām · ekāgrahṛdayasthitaḥ

Word by word

  1. दृष्ट्वाdṛṣṭvāhaving seenabsolutive (ktvā) of √दृश् (bhvādi 1P ‘to see’)
  2. तौtauthose twopronoun तद्, m. acc. du.; qualifies असुरौ
  3. असुरौasurauasurasm. acc. du. of असुर; object of दृष्ट्वा
  4. चcaboth … (and)indeclinable (conjunction; the first of a च … च pair)
  5. उग्रौugraufiercem. acc. du. of उग्र; qualifies असुरौ
  6. प्रसुप्तम्prasuptamfast asleeppast participle (kta) of प्र + √स्वप् (adādi 2P ‘to sleep’), m. acc. sg.; qualifies जनार्दनम्
  7. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction; the second of the pair)
  8. जनार्दनम्janārdanamJanārdana (Viṣṇu)m. acc. sg. of जनार्दन; compound (see Samāsa); object of दृष्ट्वा
  9. तुष्टावtuṣṭāvapraised√स्तु (adādi 2U ‘to praise’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  10. योगनिद्राम्yoganidrāmYoganidrāf. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa, 1.54); object of तुष्टाव
  11. ताम्tāmher, that (Goddess)pronoun तद्, f. acc. sg.; qualifies योगनिद्राम्
  12. एकाग्रहृदयस्थितःekāgrahṛdayasthitaḥsteadied in a one-pointed heartm. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies ब्रह्मा (1.68)

Translation

having seen both those two fierce asuras and Janārdana fast asleep, praised that Yoganidrā, steadied in a one-pointed heart —

In readable Englishseeing the two fierce asuras and Janārdana deep in sleep, with his heart wholly gathered, began to praise Yoganidrā —

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तावसुरौ tāvasurau → तौ + असुरौ

    vowel sandhi (āv) · एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78)

    Final au before a vowel becomes āv.

  • चोग्रौ cograu → च + उग्रौ

    vowel sandhi (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + u → o.

  • प्रसुप्तं च prasuptaṃ ca → प्रसुप्तम् + च

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra (pronounced as the palatal nasal before c: अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः, 8.4.58, वा पदान्तस्य, 8.4.59).

  • तामेकाग्रहृदयस्थितः tāmekāgrahṛdayasthitaḥ → ताम् + एकाग्रहृदयस्थितः

    no change (final m before a vowel) · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23) applies only before a consonant

    The m is written together with the following vowel. Inside the compound, एक + अग्र → एकाग्र (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, 6.1.101).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • एकाग्रहृदयस्थितः ekāgrahṛdayasthitaḥ

    saptamī tatpuruṣa containing a karmadhāraya (एकाग्रहृदय) whose first member एकाग्र is a bahuvrīhi

    Members
    एकाग्रहृदय + स्थित
    Vigraha
    एकम् अग्रं यस्य तत् एकाग्रम्; एकाग्रं हृदयम् एकाग्रहृदयम्; तस्मिन् स्थितः ekam agraṃ yasya tat ekāgram; ekāgraṃ hṛdayam ekāgrahṛdayam; tasmin sthitaḥ
    Literally
    “standing in a heart that has one point”
    In the verse
    with his whole mind gathered on her
    Alternative
    Or tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa, एकाग्रहृदयेन स्थितः ‘standing (there) with a concentrated heart’; the sense — Brahmā’s focused devotion — is the same.

  • जनार्दनम् janārdanam

    upapada tatpuruṣa (traditional etymology; अर्दन from √अर्द् ‘to afflict, stir’)

    Members
    जन + अर्दन
    Vigraha
    जनान् अर्दयति इति janān ardayati iti
    Literally
    “he who afflicts (wicked) people”
    In the verse
    a standard name of Viṣṇu
    Alternative
    Traditional etymologies differ (also ‘he whom people entreat’, from √अर्द् ‘to ask’); the name is used here simply for Viṣṇu.
Morphology & anvaya

  • तुष्टाव tuṣṭāva

    Perfect of √स्तु: the reduplicated syllable keeps the stop (tu-), and the s of the root becomes ṣ, drawing t into ṭ (tu-ṣṭāva); the root vowel takes vṛddhi in the 3rd singular. The verb that frames the whole hymn (1.73–87).

  • दृष्ट्वा dṛṣṭvā

    Absolutive of √दृश्: दृश् + त्वा → दृष्ट्वा (ś → ṣ, t → ṭ). Its subject is Brahmā, the subject of तुष्टाव.

  • प्रसुप्तम् prasuptam

    Past participle of प्र + √स्वप् with samprasāraṇa (स्वप् → सुप्): ‘deeply asleep’.

Anvaya · prose order

(सः ब्रह्मा) तौ उग्रौ असुरौ च प्रसुप्तं जनार्दनं च दृष्ट्वा एकाग्रहृदयस्थितः तां योगनिद्रां तुष्टाव।

(saḥ brahmā) tau ugrau asurau ca prasuptaṃ janārdanaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā ekāgrahṛdayasthitaḥ tāṃ yoganidrāṃ tuṣṭāva |

The subject (ब्रह्मा) comes from 1.68; an absolutive phrase with two objects joined by च … च, then the main verb with its object.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Brahmā sees the danger and sees that Viṣṇu cannot help while asleep. With a one-pointed heart he praises Yoganidrā, the power holding Viṣṇu — the hymn of 1.73–87.

Traditional interpretation

The narrative logic is precise: to wake Viṣṇu, Brahmā addresses not Viṣṇu but the sleep that holds him. In the Śākta reading even the highest god’s activity depends on her release.

Word by word

  1. विबोधनार्थायvibodhanārthāyafor the sake of awakeningcompound (see Samāsa), m. dat. sg.; dative of purpose
  2. हरेःhareḥof Harim. gen. sg. of हरि; objective genitive with विबोधन (‘the waking of Hari’)
  3. हरिनेत्रकृतालयाम्harinetrakṛtālayāmwho had made her dwelling in Hari’s eyesf. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies योगनिद्राम् (1.69)

for the sake of the awakening of Hari — (her) who had made her abode in Hari’s eyes, the sovereign of the universe, the supporter of the world, the maker of maintenance and dissolution,

In readable Englishto wake Hari: she who dwelt in Hari’s eyes, sovereign of the universe, sustainer of the world, who preserves it and dissolves it —

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • हरेर्हरिनेत्रकृतालयाम् harerharinetrakṛtālayām → हरेः + हरिनेत्रकृतालयाम्

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    Visarga after e, before the voiced h, appears as r.

  • विबोधनार्थाय vibodhanārthāya → विबोधन + अर्थाय

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + a → ā; likewise कृत + आलय → कृतालय.

  • विश्वेश्वरीं viśveśvarīṃ → विश्व + ईश्वरीम्

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa); anusvāra · आद्गुणः (6.1.87); मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    a + ī → e; the final m becomes anusvāra before the j of जगद्धात्रीम्.

  • जगद्धात्रीं jagaddhātrīṃ → जगत् + धात्रीम्

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    The t of जगत् is voiced to d before the voiced dh.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • विबोधनार्थाय vibodhanārthāya

    caturthī tatpuruṣa (with अर्थ, always compounded)

    Members
    विबोधन + अर्थ
    Vigraha
    विबोधनाय इदम् vibodhanāya idam
    Literally

  • हरिनेत्रकृतालयाम् harinetrakṛtālayām

    Literally

    Members

    Vigraha

  • जगद्धात्रीम् jagaddhātrīm

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    जगत् + धात्री
    Vigraha
    जगतः धात्री, ताम् jagataḥ dhātrī, tām
    Literally

    In the verse

  • स्थितिसंहारकारिणीम् sthitisaṃhārakāriṇīm

    ṣaṣṭhī (upapada-type) tatpuruṣa containing an itaretara dvandva (स्थितिसंहार)

    Members
    स्थिति + संहार + कारिणी
    Vigraha
    स्थितिः च संहारः च स्थितिसंहारौ; तयोः कारिणी, ताम् sthitiḥ ca saṃhāraḥ ca sthitisaṃhārau; tayoḥ kāriṇī, tām
    Literally
    “maker of maintenance and destruction”
    In the verse
    who keeps the world in being and withdraws it
Morphology & anvaya

  • जगद्धात्रीम् jagaddhātrīm

    धात्री is the feminine of the agent noun धातृ (√धा + tṛc), formed with ṅīp: ‘she who places, supports’.

  • स्थितिसंहारकारिणीम् sthitisaṃhārakāriṇīm

    Feminine of the -in agent noun कारिन् (+ ī): कारिणी, accusative कारिणीम्. Compare the masculine instrumental कारिणा in 1.54.

Anvaya · prose order

(ब्रह्मा) हरेः विबोधनार्थाय हरिनेत्रकृतालयां विश्वेश्वरीं जगद्धात्रीं स्थितिसंहारकारिणीं (तां योगनिद्रां तुष्टाव)।

(brahmā) hareḥ vibodhanārthāya harinetrakṛtālayāṃ viśveśvarīṃ jagaddhātrīṃ sthitisaṃhārakāriṇīṃ (tāṃ yoganidrāṃ tuṣṭāva) |

A string of accusative epithets in apposition to योगनिद्राम् (1.69), with a dative of purpose; the verb is तुष्टाव (1.69).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The purpose of Brahmā’s praise is stated — to wake Hari — and the Goddess is described by her place (resting in Viṣṇu’s eyes, as sleep) and her cosmic functions: sovereign, supporter, preserver and dissolver of the world.

Traditional interpretation

The epithets already give her the works usually divided among the gods: preservation (Viṣṇu’s) and dissolution (Rudra’s). The hymn will add creation (1.75–77), so that all three belong to her.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the same epithet, name 935, जगद्धात्री, and lists the three functions as separate names: 264, सृष्टिकर्त्री; 266, गोप्त्री; 268, संहारिणी.

Verse 1.71

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

निद्रां भगवतीं विष्णोरतुलां तेजसः प्रभुः॥⁠७१⁠॥

nidrāṃ bhagavatīṃ viṣṇoratulāṃ tejasaḥ prabhuḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

निद्राम् · भगवतीम् · विष्णोः · अतुलाम् · तेजसः · प्रभुः

nidrām · bhagavatīm · viṣṇoḥ · atulām · tejasaḥ · prabhuḥ

Word by word

  1. निद्राम्nidrāmSleepf. acc. sg. of निद्रा; in apposition to योगनिद्राम् (1.69)
  2. भगवतीम्bhagavatīmthe Blessed Onef. acc. sg. of भगवती; qualifies निद्राम्
  3. विष्णोःviṣṇoḥof Viṣṇum. gen. sg. of विष्णु; depends on निद्राम्
  4. अतुलाम्atulāmincomparablef. acc. sg. of अतुल (nañ compound: न तुला यस्य); qualifies निद्राम्
  5. तेजसःtejasaḥof radiance, of splendourn. gen. sg. of तेजस् (s-stem); depends on प्रभुः
  6. प्रभुःprabhuḥthe lord (Brahmā)m. nom. sg. of प्रभु; subject (= ब्रह्मा of 1.68)

Translation

— the Blessed Sleep of Viṣṇu, the incomparable — (so) the lord of radiance (praised her).

In readable Englishthe incomparable Lady, the Sleep of Viṣṇu. So Brahmā, lord of splendour, praised her.

‘Brahmā’ and ‘praised her’ are supplied from 1.68–69 to close the sentence.

Textual verification / uncertain: The construction of तेजसः is open. Taken here with प्रभुः, ‘the lord of radiance’, an epithet of Brahmā (the subject); it can also be read with अतुलाम्, ‘(her) unequalled in radiance’, with प्रभुः simply ‘the Lord’. Both are grammatical; the sense of the verse is not affected.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • विष्णोरतुलां viṣṇoratulāṃ → विष्णोः + अतुलाम्

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    Visarga after o (not a/ā), before a vowel, appears as r.

  • निद्रां भगवतीं nidrāṃ bhagavatīṃ → निद्राम् + भगवतीम्

    anusvāra sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra (also in भगवतीं विष्णोः and अतुलां तेजसः).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अतुलाम् atulām

    bahuvrīhi (nañ-bahuvrīhi)

    Members
    न + तुला
    Vigraha
    न विद्यते तुला यस्याः सा, ताम् na vidyate tulā yasyāḥ sā, tām
    Literally
    “she who has no equal measure”
    In the verse
    beyond compare
Morphology & anvaya

  • तेजसः tejasaḥ

    Genitive singular of the s-stem तेजस्; its construction is open (see flags): with प्रभुः ‘lord of radiance’, or with अतुलाम् ‘unequalled in radiance’.

Anvaya · prose order

तेजसः प्रभुः (ब्रह्मा) विष्णोः अतुलां भगवतीं निद्रां (तुष्टाव)।

tejasaḥ prabhuḥ (brahmā) viṣṇoḥ atulāṃ bhagavatīṃ nidrāṃ (tuṣṭāva) |

The half-verse closes the sentence begun in 1.68: more accusatives in apposition to योगनिद्राम्, and the nominative प्रभुः restating the subject.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The last epithets: she is Viṣṇu’s Sleep, the Blessed One, beyond compare. The nominative प्रभुः restates the subject, Brahmā, before the hymn begins.

Traditional interpretation

The Goddess is named here by her plainest name, निद्रा ‘sleep’, with the honorific भगवती: what holds the highest god is not a lesser power but the Blessed One herself.

Anvaya · prose order

ब्रह्मा उवाच।

brahmā uvāca |

Subject and verb: a speaker label.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Within the sage Medhas’s narration, Brahmā on the navel-lotus speaks to Yoganidrā. His hymn (1.73–87) is the first of the four great hymns of the Devī Māhātmya.

Translation

You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā, you indeed are the vaṣaṭ-call, you whose self is sound.

In readable EnglishYou are Svāhā, you are Svadhā; you are the sacred cry Vaṣaṭ — your very self is the sound of the Veda.

‘Of the Veda’ interprets स्वर (see Samāsa).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • वषट्कारः vaṣaṭkāraḥ

    tatpuruṣa with कार ‘making, utterance’ after a quoted sound (as in ओंकार)

    Members

    Vigraha

    “the making of ‘vaṣaṭ’”
    In the verse
    the cry vaṣaṭ with which the hotṛ priest signals the pouring of the oblation

  • स्वरात्मिका svarātmikā

    bahuvrīhi (with the suffix -ka; feminine -ikā)

    Members
    स्वर + आत्मन् (+ ka)
    Vigraha

Morphology & anvaya

  • स्वरात्मिका svarātmikā

    Bahuvrīhis ending in आत्मन् add -ka; in the feminine the a before -kā becomes i: आत्मक → आत्मिका. The same formation recurs as मात्रात्मिका in 1.74.

  • वषट्कारः vaṣaṭkāraḥ

    A masculine noun predicated of the Goddess: in identity statements (‘you are X’) the predicate noun keeps its own gender.

Anvaya · prose order

त्वं स्वाहा, त्वं स्वधा, त्वं हि स्वरात्मिका वषट्कारः।

tvaṃ svāhā, tvaṃ svadhā, tvaṃ hi svarātmikā vaṣaṭkāraḥ |

Three identity statements with त्वम् repeated; स्वरात्मिका qualifies the subject.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Brahmā opens by identifying the Goddess with the three ritual calls of Vedic sacrifice: svāhā (offering to the gods), svadhā (offering to the ancestors) and vaṣaṭ (the hotṛ’s call at the oblation). She is the very sound through which offering reaches its recipient.

Traditional interpretation

The hymn begins with sacrificial speech because in the Vedic view the sacrifice sustains the world. To call her svāhā and svadhā is to make her the power by which gods and ancestors are fed — the support of both worlds. In Purāṇic myth Svāhā and Svadhā are also personified as goddesses, consorts of Agni and of the ancestors.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the same pair as consecutive names: 535, स्वाहा, and 536, स्वधा.

Translation

You are nectar; in the eternal imperishable (syllable) you abide threefold, having the morae as your self; you abide in the half-mora, eternal, (you) who cannot be uttered distinctly.

In readable EnglishYou are the nectar of immortality. In the eternal, imperishable syllable you dwell as its three sounds; and you dwell in the half-measure beyond them, eternal, which no voice can utter as a separate sound.

‘Syllable’ and ‘its three sounds’ interpret अक्षर and मात्रा as the syllable Om and its parts a, u, m, the standard sense in this context.

Textual verification / uncertain: अक्षरे नित्ये may be locative (‘in the eternal imperishable [syllable]’, chosen here) or two feminine vocatives (‘O Imperishable, O Eternal One’); both are grammatical and both are found in translations. अर्धमात्रास्थिता is printed as one word; a division into अर्धमात्रा स्थिता is equally possible.

Morphology & anvaya

  • अनुच्चार्या anuccāryā

    Gerundive of the causative of उद् + √चर् (उच्चारयति ‘pronounces’): उच्चार्य ‘to be pronounced’; with the negative अन्- ‘not pronounceable’.

  • अक्षरे akṣare

    Ambiguous form: n. loc. sg. of अक्षर (‘in the imperishable syllable’) or f. voc. sg. of अक्षरा (‘O Imperishable!’). The locative is chosen because it gives स्थिता its place and matches the half-mora of the next line.

  • त्रिधा tridhā

    The suffix -धा makes adverbs of manner from numerals: त्रिधा ‘in three ways’, बहुधा ‘in many ways’ (1.65).

Anvaya · prose order

त्वं सुधा। त्वं नित्ये अक्षरे त्रिधा मात्रात्मिका स्थिता। (त्वं) या विशेषतः अनुच्चार्या, नित्या, अर्धमात्रास्थिता (असि)।

tvaṃ sudhā | tvaṃ nitye akṣare tridhā mātrātmikā sthitā | (tvaṃ) yā viśeṣataḥ anuccāryā, nityā, ardhamātrāsthitā (asi) |

A short identity (सुधा त्वम्), a participial predicate with a locative of place, and a second predicate expanded by a relative clause (या … विशेषतः).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The Goddess is identified with the sacred syllable: she abides in its three morae (a, u, m) and in the half-mora — the fading resonance after m — which cannot be pronounced as a distinct sound. She is also सुधा, the nectar of immortality.

Traditional interpretation

The analysis of Om into three measures and a fourth beyond utterance is Upaniṣadic: the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad treats a, u and m as the three states of waking, dream and deep sleep and the ‘measureless fourth’ (अमात्रः चतुर्थः) as the self beyond them. Brahmā places the Goddess both in the three and in what lies beyond them.

Modern reflection

A modern reading: the hymn begins with words that can be spoken — svāhā, svadhā, vaṣaṭ — and moves at once to the part of the sacred sound that cannot be spoken. Praise here is a way of approaching what speech cannot hold.

    ā + e → ai; the t of एतत् is voiced to d before the voiced dh.

    Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • धार्यते dhāryate

    Passive of the causative of √धृ (धारयति ‘holds up, sustains’): the causative -ay- drops before the passive -ya (धार्-य-ते). ‘Is sustained’.

  • सावित्री sāvitrī

    Taddhita in -ī from सवितृ: ‘belonging to Savitṛ’, the name of the Gāyatrī verse addressed to the Sun-god Savitṛ.

  • जननी jananī

    Feminine agent noun from √जन् with -ana and -ī: ‘she who gives birth’.

Anvaya · prose order

त्वम् एव संध्या, सावित्री। देवि, त्वं परा जननी। त्वया एतत् विश्वं धार्यते, त्वया एतत् जगत् सृज्यते।

tvam eva saṃdhyā, sāvitrī | devi, tvaṃ parā jananī | tvayā etat viśvaṃ dhāryate, tvayā etat jagat sṛjyate |

Identity statements (त्वम् … संध्या सावित्री; त्वम् … जननी परा), then two parallel passive sentences with त्वया as agent.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Brahmā continues identifying her with the forms of sacred worship — the twilight rite (Sandhyā) and the Sāvitrī verse recited in it — and then names her the supreme Mother, by whom the world is created and sustained.

Traditional interpretation

Sandhyā and Sāvitrī belong together: the Sāvitrī (Gāyatrī) verse addressed to Savitṛ is recited at the twilight worship. To call the Goddess both is to make the daily Vedic observance itself her form. The verse then passes from ritual to cosmology: the one invoked at dawn and dusk is the mother of the world.

  7. अन्तेanteat the endm. loc. sg. of अन्त; locative of time
  8. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  9. सर्वदाsarvadāalways, at every (end)indeclinable (adverb of time, सर्व + -dā)
  10. विसृष्टौvisṛṣṭauin creation, at the emission (of the world)f. loc. sg. of विसृष्टि (वि + √सृज् + ktin)
  11. सृष्टिरूपाsṛṣṭirūpāhaving the form of creationf. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate of त्वम्

Translation

By you this is protected, O Goddess, and you devour (it) at the end, always. In creation you have the form of creation, and the form of preservation in protecting,

In readable EnglishBy you, O Goddess, it is protected, and at the end of every age you consume it. When the world is brought forth, you are its creation; while it is sustained, you are its preservation;

सर्वदा ‘always’ with अन्ते is rendered ‘at the end of every age’: each dissolution, not one alone.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • त्वयैतत्पाल्यते tvayaitatpālyate → त्वया + एतत् + पाल्यते

    vowel sandhi (vṛddhi); no change before an unvoiced stop · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88); खरि च (8.4.55)

    ā + e → ai; the t stays unvoiced before p.

  • त्वमत्स्यन्ते tvamatsyante → त्वम् + अत्सि + अन्ते

    final m before a vowel; vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    त्वम् keeps its m before the a of अत्सि; the i of अत्सि becomes y before the a of अन्ते.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • सृष्टिरूपा sṛṣṭirūpā

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    सृष्टि + रूप
    Vigraha
    सृष्टिः रूपं यस्याः सा sṛṣṭiḥ rūpaṃ yasyāḥ sā
    Literally
    “she whose form is creation”
    In the verse
    you take the form of creation when the world is made

  • स्थितिरूपा sthitirūpā

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    स्थिति + रूप
    Vigraha
    स्थितिः रूपं यस्याः सा sthitiḥ rūpaṃ yasyāḥ sā
    Literally
    “she whose form is continuance”
    In the verse
    you take the form of preservation while the world endures
Morphology & anvaya

  • अत्सि atsi

    Present 2nd singular of √अद्, a root-class (adādi) verb: अद् + सि, the d unvoiced to t before s (खरि च, 8.4.55). ‘You eat’ — the image of dissolution as the world swallowed back.

  • पाल्यते pālyate

    Passive of the curādi root √पाल् (पालयति): the -aya- of the present drops before the passive -ya (पाल्-य-ते).

Anvaya · prose order

देवि, त्वया एतत् पाल्यते; अन्ते च सर्वदा त्वम् (एतत्) अत्सि। विसृष्टौ त्वं सृष्टिरूपा, पालने च स्थितिरूपा, …

devi, tvayā etat pālyate; ante ca sarvadā tvam (etat) atsi | visṛṣṭau tvaṃ sṛṣṭirūpā, pālane ca sthitirūpā, …

A passive sentence, an active one with an understood object (एतत्), and a series of nominal predicates with locatives of occasion, continued in 1.77 (संहृतिरूपा).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The three cosmic works are given to her one after another: she protects the world, consumes it at every end, and in each phase takes the form of that phase — creation in creating, preservation in protecting. Dissolution follows in 1.77.

Traditional interpretation

The three works ordinarily assigned to Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra are all hers; the speaker is Brahmā himself, the creator, who here says that creation is her form. The tradition reads this as the Devī Māhātmya’s central claim: the gods act through her power.

so too, at the end of this world, the form of dissolution, O you who consist of the world. (You are) the great knowledge, the great illusion, the great intelligence, the great memory,

In readable Englishand at the end of this world, O you whose being is the world, you are its dissolution. You are the Great Knowledge and the Great Illusion, the Great Intelligence and the Great Memory,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • संहृतिरूपान्ते saṃhṛtirūpānte → संहृतिरूपा + अन्ते

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    ā + a → ā.

  • जगतोऽस्य jagato'sya → जगतः + अस्य

    visarga sandhi with pūrvarūpa · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a becomes -o, and the following a is elided (avagraha).

  • जगन्मये jaganmaye → जगत् + मये

    consonant sandhi before a suffix (nasal assimilation) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45)

    The t of जगत् becomes n before the m of the suffix -maya.

  • महाविद्या mahāvidyā → महत् + विद्या

    stem form in a compound · महत् becomes महा- as the first member of a karmadhāraya (described in words; no sūtra from the list applies)

    The same replacement gives महामाया, महामेधा, महास्मृतिः.

Morphology & anvaya

  • जगन्मये jaganmaye

    The suffix -मय (mayaṭ) means ‘consisting of’; feminine जगन्मयी, vocative जगन्मये (ī shortened to e in the vocative of feminines in -ī).

  • संहृतिरूपा saṃhṛtirūpā

    संहृति ‘drawing together, withdrawal’ is सम् + √हृ + ktin: the dissolution pictured as the world gathered back in.

Anvaya · prose order

जगन्मये, तथा अस्य जगतः अन्ते (त्वं) संहृतिरूपा। (त्वं) महाविद्या, महामाया, महामेधा, महास्मृतिः, …

jaganmaye, tathā asya jagataḥ ante (tvaṃ) saṃhṛtirūpā | (tvaṃ) mahāvidyā, mahāmāyā, mahāmedhā, mahāsmṛtiḥ, …

The first line completes the series of 1.76 (सृष्टिरूपा … स्थितिरूपा … संहृतिरूपा); the second begins a list of nominatives predicated of the Goddess, continued in 1.78.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The triad of 1.76 is completed: at the world’s end she takes the form of its dissolution. Then begins a litany of ‘great’ names — knowledge, illusion, intelligence, memory. Two printing errors of the digital text are corrected in this verse (सिंहृति → संहृति, महास्मृतः → महास्मृतिः), both with the independent witnesses; see corrections.json.

Traditional interpretation

Mahāvidyā and Mahāmāyā stand side by side, as liberation and bondage did in 1.57–58: the Goddess is both the knowledge that frees and the illusion that binds. ‘Great’ marks each as her cosmic form, not a human faculty.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has 584, महाविद्या, and 215, महामाया, and the simple forms 538, मेधा, and 540, स्मृतिः.

Morphology & anvaya

  • भवती bhavatī

    The feminine of the honorific भवत् (‘Your Ladyship’); in Brahmā’s hymn it alternates with the familiar त्वम्, which follows in the next line.

  • गुणत्रयविभाविनी guṇatrayavibhāvinī

    विभाविन् is an agent noun from the causative of वि + √भू (‘cause to appear distinctly’) with the kṛt affix -in; feminine -ī.

Anvaya · prose order

भवती च महामोहा, महादेवी, महासुरी। त्वं च सर्वस्य गुणत्रयविभाविनी प्रकृतिः।

bhavatī ca mahāmohā, mahādevī, mahāsurī | tvaṃ ca sarvasya guṇatrayavibhāvinī prakṛtiḥ |

The list of 1.77 continues with भवती as its expressed subject; a second clause names her as Prakṛti, with सर्वस्य and an epithet.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The litany continues: she is the great delusion as well as the great knowledge of 1.77, the great Goddess, and — in the Gita Press reading — the great Asurī. She is also Prakṛti, the material source of everything, from which the three guṇas unfold.

Traditional interpretation

The Sāṃkhya term prakṛti is taken over: matter and its three qualities (sattva, rajas, tamas) are not an inert principle opposed to spirit but the Goddess herself. The Gita Press pāṭha’s liturgical scheme, in which the three caritas are presided over by Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī and Mahāsarasvatī, is often explained through these guṇas; that scheme is tradition, not stated in this verse.

Translation

(You are) the Night of Time, the Great Night, and the dreadful Night of Delusion. You are Śrī, you are the Sovereign, you are Modesty, you are Understanding, whose mark is awareness.

In readable EnglishYou are the Night of Time, the Great Night, the terrible Night of Delusion. You are Fortune, you are the Sovereign, you are Modesty, you are Understanding, whose very mark is awakening.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • कालरात्रिर्महारात्रिर्मोहरात्रिश्च kālarātrirmahārātrirmoharātriśca → कालरात्रिः + महारात्रिः + मोहरात्रिः + च

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66); विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    Visarga after i before the voiced m appears as r (twice); before c it becomes s and then ś.

  • श्रीस्त्वमीश्वरी śrīstvamīśvarī → श्रीः + त्वम् + ईश्वरी

    visarga sandhi; final m before a vowel · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s; त्वम् keeps its m before the vowel of ईश्वरी.

  • ह्रीस्त्वं hrīstvaṃ → ह्रीः + त्वम्

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

  • बुद्धिर्बोधलक्षणा buddhirbodhalakṣaṇā → बुद्धिः + बोधलक्षणा

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    Visarga after i before the voiced b appears as r.

Morphology & anvaya

  • श्रीः śrīḥ

    Root-nouns in ī keep the visarga in the nominative singular (श्रीः, ह्रीः, धीः), unlike the derived feminines in ī (देवी, ईश्वरी) which have no ending.

  • दारुणा dāruṇā

    Feminine of the adjective दारुण ‘harsh, dreadful’, agreeing with the feminine रात्रि compounds.

Anvaya · prose order

(त्वं) कालरात्रिः, महारात्रिः, दारुणा मोहरात्रिः च। त्वं श्रीः, त्वम् ईश्वरी, त्वं ह्रीः, त्वं बोधलक्षणा बुद्धिः।

(tvaṃ) kālarātriḥ, mahārātriḥ, dāruṇā moharātriḥ ca | tvaṃ śrīḥ, tvam īśvarī, tvaṃ hrīḥ, tvaṃ bodhalakṣaṇā buddhiḥ |

Three ‘night’ names with one adjective, then four identity statements each with त्वम्.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Brahmā names her as three nights — of Time, the Great Night, and the dreadful night of delusion — and then as Fortune, Sovereignty, Modesty and Understanding. The dark and the auspicious are named in one breath. बोध ‘awakening’ in the last word echoes the purpose of the hymn, the awakening (विबोधन) of Viṣṇu (1.70).

Traditional interpretation

The three nights are commonly explained as nights of dissolution and of delusion, though explanations of each differ and the text does not define them. Kālarātri is also one of the nine Durgās: the Devī Kavaca recited before the Gita Press pāṭha names her seventh (सप्तमं कालरात्रीति). Here ह्री is the virtue of modesty, paired with लज्जा in 1.80, not a seed-syllable.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has 271, ईश्वरी, and describes her as 491, कालरात्र्यादिशक्त्यौघवृता, ‘surrounded by hosts of powers beginning with Kālarātri’ — there Kālarātri is one of her attendant powers, here one of her own names.

lajjā puṣṭistathā tuṣṭistvaṃ śāntiḥ kṣāntireva ca |khaḍginī śūlinī ghorā gadinī cakriṇī tathā ||

lajjā · puṣṭiḥ · tathā · tuṣṭiḥ · tvam · śāntiḥ · kṣāntiḥ · eva · cakhaḍginī · śūlinī · ghorā · gadinī · cakriṇī · tathā

Word by word

  1. लज्जाlajjāmodesty, the sense of shame that restrainsf. nom. sg. of लज्जा (ā-stem); predicate of an understood असि with त्वम्

  3. तथाtathālikewise, andindeclinable (adverb of manner, here connective)
  4. तुष्टिःtuṣṭiḥcontentmentf. nom. sg. of तुष्टि (i-stem; √तुष् + ktin)
  5. त्वम्tvamyousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, nom. sg.; subject (the verb असि is understood throughout the hymn)

  9. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  10. खड्गिनीkhaḍginībearing the swordf. nom. sg. of खड्गिन् (possessive taddhita -इन् on खड्ग ‘sword’; feminine in -ई)
  11. शूलिनीśūlinībearing the trident (or spear)f. nom. sg. of शूलिन् (possessive -इन् on शूल)
  12. घोराghorāterrible, dreadfulf. nom. sg. of the adjective घोर

Translation

(You are) modesty, nourishment and likewise contentment; you (are) peace and forbearance too. (You are) sword-bearing, trident-bearing, terrible, mace-bearing and likewise discus-bearing;

In readable EnglishYou are modesty, nourishment and contentment; you are peace, and patience too. You bear the sword and the trident; you are terrible; you carry the mace and the discus;

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • पुष्टिस्तथा puṣṭistathā → पुष्टिः + तथा

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s. The same change gives तुष्टिस्त्वं.

  • त्वं शान्तिः tvaṃ śāntiḥ → त्वम् + शान्तिः

    anusvāra · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra.

  • क्षान्तिरेव kṣāntireva → क्षान्तिः + एव

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    Visarga after i, before a vowel, appears as r.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • खड्गिनी khaḍginī

    Possessive taddhita -इन् (‘having’) on खड्ग gives खड्गिन् ‘sword-bearer’; the feminine adds -ई. The verse builds five such forms in a row (खड्गिनी, शूलिनी, गदिनी, चक्रिणी, and in 1.81 शङ्खिनी, चापिनी).

  • चक्रिणी cakriṇī

    The n of the suffix turns retroflex (ṇ) because r stands earlier in the same word with nothing to block it; compare गदिनी and शूलिनी, where there is no r.

  • क्षान्तिः kṣāntiḥ

    Action noun in -ति (ktin) from √क्षम् ‘to endure’; the nasal of the root appears as न् before त. शान्तिः from √शम् is formed the same way.

Anvaya · prose order

त्वं लज्जा पुष्टिः तथा तुष्टिः, त्वं शान्तिः क्षान्तिः एव च (असि)। (त्वं) खड्गिनी शूलिनी घोरा गदिनी तथा चक्रिणी (असि)।

tvaṃ lajjā puṣṭiḥ tathā tuṣṭiḥ, tvaṃ śāntiḥ kṣāntiḥ eva ca (asi) | (tvaṃ) khaḍginī śūlinī ghorā gadinī tathā cakriṇī (asi) |

A list of predicate nominatives with त्वम् and an understood असि, continuing the list of 1.77–79: first five virtues, then a run of feminine possessive adjectives naming her weapons.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Brahmā’s list turns in mid-verse from inner qualities to weapons. Modesty, nourishment, contentment, peace and forbearance are the gentlest powers of a person; the next line arms the same Goddess and calls her घोरा, ‘terrible’. The hymn makes no division between the two.

Traditional interpretation

Several of these qualities return in the yā devī hymn of chapter 5 as forms in which the Devī abides in all beings: क्षान्ति (5.38-40), लज्जा (5.44-46), शान्ति (5.47-49) and तुष्टि (5.68-70). The weapons named in 1.80–81 match the dhyāna of Mahākālī that the Gita Press pāṭha sets before the first carita (sword, discus, mace, arrows, bow, iron club, trident, bhuśuṇḍī, a head, conch); the hymn names all of them except the head. The dhyāna is liturgical tradition, not part of the Purāṇa.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the same names as single epithets: 443 तुष्टिः, 444 पुष्टिः, 447 शान्तिः and 740 लज्जा. The overlap is in vocabulary for the Goddess’s powers; the two texts are separate works.

Padaccheda · the words separated

śaṅkhinī · cāpinī · bāṇabhuśuṇḍīparighāyudhāsaumyā · saumyatarā · aśeṣasaumyebhyaḥ · tu · atisundarī

Word by word

  1. शङ्खिनीśaṅkhinībearing the conchf. nom. sg. of शङ्खिन् (possessive -इन् on शङ्ख)
  2. चापिनीcāpinībearing the bowf. nom. sg. of चापिन् (possessive -इन् on चाप)
  3. बाणभुशुण्डीपरिघायुधाbāṇabhuśuṇḍīparighāyudhāwhose weapons are arrows, the bhuśuṇḍī and the iron clubf. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)
  4. सौम्याsaumyāgentle, benign (lit. ‘moon-like’, from सोम)f. nom. sg. of the adjective सौम्य (taddhita from सोम)
  5. सौम्यतराsaumyatarāmore gentlef. nom. sg. of सौम्यतर, comparative (taddhita -तर) of सौम्य; governs the ablative अशेषसौम्येभ्यः
  6. अशेषसौम्येभ्यःaśeṣasaumyebhyaḥthan all gentle thingsn. abl. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); ablative of comparison

Translation

conch-bearing, bow-bearing, having arrows, bhuśuṇḍī and iron club as weapons; gentle, more gentle than all gentle things, and exceedingly beautiful.

In readable Englishyou bear the conch and the bow, and your weapons are arrows, the bhuśuṇḍī and the iron club. Yet you are gentle — gentler than every gentle thing — and beautiful beyond measure.

‘Yet’ renders the contrast the verse makes by placing सौम्या straight after the weapons; the Sanskrit has only तु ‘and, moreover’.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सौम्यतराशेष saumyatarāśeṣa → सौम्यतरा + अशेष(सौम्येभ्यः)

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    ā + a → ā. Two words are fused, so the line looks like one long compound; it is not one.

  • सौम्येभ्यस्त्वतिसुन्दरी saumyebhyastvatisundarī → अशेषसौम्येभ्यः + तु + अतिसुन्दरी

    visarga and vowel sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34); इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    Visarga before t becomes s; then u before a becomes v (तु + अति → त्वति).

  • परिघायुधा parighāyudhā → परिघ + आयुधा

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + ā → ā.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • बाणभुशुण्डीपरिघायुधा bāṇabhuśuṇḍīparighāyudhā

    bahuvrīhi containing an itaretara dvandva (बाणभुशुण्डीपरिघ)

    Vigraha

    “she whose weapons are arrows, bhuśuṇḍī and iron club”

    Members

    Vigraha

    Members

    Vigraha

    Literally

    surpassingly beautiful
Morphology & anvaya

  • सौम्यतरा saumyatarā

    Comparative in -तर (taddhita) on सौम्य, feminine -तरा. The thing surpassed stands in the ablative: सौम्यतरा अशेषसौम्येभ्यः ‘gentler than all gentle things’.

  • सौम्या saumyā

    Taddhita from सोम ‘the moon (Soma)’ with vṛddhi of the first syllable: ‘of the moon’s nature’, hence cool, mild, benign — the opposite of घोरा in 1.80.

Anvaya · prose order

(त्वं) शङ्खिनी चापिनी बाणभुशुण्डीपरिघायुधा (असि)। सौम्या, अशेषसौम्येभ्यः सौम्यतरा, अतिसुन्दरी तु (असि)।

(tvaṃ) śaṅkhinī cāpinī bāṇabhuśuṇḍīparighāyudhā (asi) | saumyā, aśeṣasaumyebhyaḥ saumyatarā, atisundarī tu (asi) |

The weapon-list of 1.80 ends; the second line sets a gentle triad against it. The ablative अशेषसौम्येभ्यः is taken with the comparative सौम्यतरा, which requires one. It can also be read with अतिसुन्दरी (‘more beautiful than all gentle things’); the comparative is the stronger claim on it.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The arming of the Goddess is completed — conch, bow, arrows, bhuśuṇḍī and iron club — and in the same breath she is called gentle, gentler than all gentle things, surpassingly beautiful. The terrible one of 1.80 (घोरा) and the gentle one here (सौम्या) are one.

Traditional interpretation

The pairing of the fierce (घोर) and the gentle (सौम्य) is basic to the Śākta picture of the Goddess: the same Devī is worshipped in terrible and benign forms. This hymn states the pairing outright before the stories of chapters 2–13 show it in action.

Modern reflection

A modern reflection: the hymn does not ask the reader to choose between a gentle and a fierce divinity. Protection and tenderness are offered as aspects of one care.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has सौम्या as name 910. The adjective is common; the shared word shows a shared idiom of praise, not a borrowing.

  9. क्वचित्kvacitanywhereindeclinable (indefinite adverb of place: क्व + चित्)
  10. वस्तुvastuthing, entityn. nom. sg. of वस्तु (u-stem)
  11. सदसत्sadasatexistent or non-existentn. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies वस्तु
  12. वाvāor, whetherindeclinable (disjunctive particle)
  13. अखिलात्मिकेakhilātmikeO Self of all, O you whose nature is everythingf. voc. sg. of अखिलात्मिका; compound (see Samāsa)

Translation

Of the higher and the lower the highest, you alone are the supreme Īśvarī. And whatever thing (there is) anywhere, existent or non-existent, O Self of all —

In readable EnglishHighest of all things high and low, you alone are the supreme Sovereign. And whatever thing there is, anywhere, whether it is or is not, O Soul of all —

The second line is completed by 1.83 (‘of all that, you are the power’).

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • यच्च yacca → यत् + च

    consonant sandhi (palatal assimilation) · स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    Final t before c becomes c.

  • क्वचिद्वस्तु kvacidvastu → क्वचित् + वस्तु

    consonant sandhi (voicing) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39)

    Final t before the voiced v becomes d. The same change gives सदसद्वा. In किंचित्क्वचित्, t before the unvoiced k stays t (खरि च, 8.4.55).

  • सदसद्वाखिलात्मिके sadasadvākhilātmike → सदसत् + वा + अखिलात्मिके

    consonant and vowel sandhi · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    t → d before v; then ā + a → ā (वा + अखिल → वाखिल).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • परापराणाम् parāparāṇām

    itaretara dvandva

    Members
    पर + अपर
    Vigraha
    पराणि च अपराणि च परापराणि, तेषाम् parāṇi ca aparāṇi ca parāparāṇi, teṣām
    Literally
    “of the higher and the lower”
    In the verse
    of all things, high and low; the Goddess is the highest even among the highest
    Alternative
    पर and अपर can also be taken as the transcendent and the immanent (the supreme and the manifest), so ‘supreme over both the transcendent and the manifest’. The compound is the same dvandva either way.

  • परमेश्वरी parameśvarī

    karmadhāraya

    Members
    परमा + ईश्वरी
    Vigraha
    परमा चासौ ईश्वरी च paramā cāsau īśvarī ca
    Literally
    “the supreme sovereign lady”
    In the verse
    the supreme Īśvarī, the Goddess as ruler of all; internal sandhi a + ī → e (आद्गुणः, 6.1.87), the feminine first member taking its masculine form

  • सदसत् sadasat

    samāhāra dvandva (neuter singular), here used as an adjective of वस्तु

    Members
    सत् + असत्
    Vigraha
    सत् च असत् च sat ca asat ca
    Literally
    “being-and-non-being”
    In the verse
    whatever is, or is not; with वा the two are alternatives: ‘existent or non-existent’

  • अखिलात्मिके akhilātmike

    bahuvrīhi (with the samāsānta suffix -क; feminine -इका)

    Members
    अखिल + आत्मन्
    Vigraha
    अखिलम् आत्मा यस्याः सा अखिलात्मिका, तत्सम्बुद्धौ akhilam ātmā yasyāḥ sā akhilātmikā, tatsambuddhau
    Literally
    “O you whose self is the whole”
    In the verse
    O you who are the self of everything — the same formation as स्वरात्मिका (1.73) and मात्रात्मिका (1.74)
Morphology & anvaya

  • किंचित् kiṃcit

    The interrogative किम् with the particle चित् becomes an indefinite: ‘anything’. With the relative यत् it generalises: यत् किंचित् ‘whatever at all’. क्वचित् (क्व ‘where?’ + चित्) is the adverb ‘anywhere’.

  • अखिलात्मिके akhilātmike

    Vocative singular of an ā-stem feminine: the final ā becomes e (अखिलात्मिका → अखिलात्मिके), as in देवि from देवी with shortening.

Anvaya · prose order

(हे) अखिलात्मिके, त्वम् एव परापराणां परमा परमेश्वरी (असि)। यत् च किंचित् सत् असत् वा वस्तु क्वचित् (अस्ति) —

(he) akhilātmike, tvam eva parāparāṇāṃ paramā parameśvarī (asi) | yat ca kiṃcit sat asat vā vastu kvacit (asti) —

The first line is a complete statement. The second opens a relative clause (यत् … वस्तु) whose correlative तस्य सर्वस्य comes in 1.83.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Brahmā moves from listing names to a claim about everything: she is the highest over high and low alike, and the second line begins to say that whatever exists, or does not exist, belongs to her. The sentence finishes in 1.83.

Traditional interpretation

सत् and असत् are often explained in Indian thought as the manifest (the effect) and the unmanifest (the cause). Read so, the verse leaves nothing, manifest or latent, outside the Goddess.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has 790 परापरा, 396 परमेश्वरी and 661 सदसद्रूपधारिणी (‘bearing the forms of being and non-being’). The concepts are the same; the formulations belong to each text.

Verse 1.83

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

तस्य सर्वस्य या शक्तिः सा त्वं किं स्तूयसे तदा।यया त्वया जगत्स्रष्टा जगत्पात्यत्ति यो जगत्॥⁠८३⁠॥

tasya sarvasya yā śaktiḥ sā tvaṃ kiṃ stūyase tadā |yayā tvayā jagatsraṣṭā jagatpātyatti yo jagat ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

tasya · sarvasya · yā · śaktiḥ · sā · tvam · kim · stūyase · tadāyayā · tvayā · jagatsraṣṭā · jagat · pāti · atti · yaḥ · jagat

Word by word

  1. तस्यtasyaof thatpronoun तद्, n. gen. sg.; correlative of यत् in 1.82
  2. सर्वस्यsarvasyaof allpronominal adjective सर्व, n. gen. sg.; agrees with तस्य
  3. याyāwhichrelative pronoun यद्, f. nom. sg.
  4. शक्तिःśaktiḥpower, energyf. nom. sg. of शक्ति (i-stem; √शक् + ktin)
  5. साsāthat (power)pronoun तद्, f. nom. sg.; correlative of या
  6. त्वम्tvamyousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, nom. sg.
  7. किम्kimhow? (rhetorical)interrogative किम्, used adverbially: ‘how, in what way’
  8. स्तूयसेstūyaseare you praised, can you be praised√स्तु (adādi, 2U, ‘to praise’), karmaṇi prayoga, laṭ (present), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana
  9. तदाtadāthen, in that caseindeclinable (adverb of time, here inferential)
  10. ययाyayāby whomrelative pronoun यद्, f. instr. sg.; agent of नीतः in 1.84
  11. त्वयाtvayāby yousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, instr. sg.; in apposition to यया
  12. जगत्स्रष्टाjagatsraṣṭācreator of the worldm. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate in the relative clause of यः
  13. जगत्jagatthe worldn. acc. sg. of जगत्; object of पाति
  14. पातिpātiprotects√पा (adādi, 2P, ‘to protect’), laṭ, prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  15. अत्तिattidevours√अद् (adādi, 2P, ‘to eat’), laṭ, prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  16. यःyaḥhe whorelative pronoun यद्, m. nom. sg.; correlative of सः in 1.84
  17. जगत्jagatthe worldn. acc. sg.; object of अत्ति

Translation

Of all that, the power which (it has) — that (power) you (are). How then are you to be praised? By whom — by you — he who (is) the creator of the world, (who) protects the world, (who) devours the world,

In readable Englishof all that, you are the power. How then can anyone praise you? You, by whom he who creates the world, sustains the world and devours the world

The sentence continues into 1.84: ‘— even he has been brought under the sway of sleep’.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सा त्वं किं स्तूयसे sā tvaṃ kiṃ stūyase → सा + त्वम् + किम् + स्तूयसे

    anusvāra · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra, twice.

  • जगत्पात्यत्ति jagatpātyatti → जगत् + पाति + अत्ति

    vowel sandhi (yaṇ) · इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    i before a becomes y (पाति + अत्ति → पात्यत्ति). The t of जगत् stays unvoiced before p (खरि च, 8.4.55); the words are only written together.

  • यो जगत् yo jagat → यः + जगत्

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • जगत्स्रष्टा jagatsraṣṭā

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    जगत् + स्रष्टृ
    Vigraha
    जगतः स्रष्टा jagataḥ sraṣṭā
    Literally
    “the world’s emitter”
    In the verse
    the creator of the world
    Alternative
    It can also be read as two words, जगत् (acc.) + स्रष्टा, with the agent noun taking an object like a verb, which keeps the line’s three जगत् parallel (creates / protects / devours the world). The sense is the same; the printed text joins all three, so print decides nothing.
Morphology & anvaya

  • स्तूयसे stūyase

    Passive present of √स्तु: the root vowel lengthens before the passive marker -य- (स्तू-य-), with the ātmanepada second-person ending -से. ‘Are you praised?’ — here rhetorical: ‘how can you be praised?’

  • अत्ति atti

    √अद् (adādi) adds the ending directly to the root: अद् + ति → अत्ति, with d unvoiced before t.

  • जगत्स्रष्टा jagatsraṣṭā

    स्रष्टृ ‘creator’ is the agent noun (tṛc) of √सृज्; nom. sg. स्रष्टा. The root’s vowel and r change places (सृज् → स्रष्) before the suffix.

Anvaya · prose order

तस्य सर्वस्य या शक्तिः, सा त्वम् (असि)। तदा (त्वं) किं स्तूयसे? यया त्वया, यः जगत्स्रष्टा (यः) जगत् पाति (यः) जगत् अत्ति, (सः अपि निद्रावशं नीतः) —

tasya sarvasya yā śaktiḥ, sā tvam (asi) | tadā (tvaṃ) kiṃ stūyase? yayā tvayā, yaḥ jagatsraṣṭā (yaḥ) jagat pāti (yaḥ) jagat atti, (saḥ api nidrāvaśaṃ nītaḥ) —

Line one completes 1.82 with the correlative pair या … सा. Line two opens a long relative clause: यया त्वया is the agent of नीतः in 1.84, and यः … जगत् describes the one who was put to sleep.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The argument of the hymn is made plain: if she is the power (शक्ति) of everything that is, then every act — praise included — is already hers, and no praise can reach her. The second line names the one she has overcome: the god who creates, preserves and consumes the world, i.e. the sleeping Viṣṇu.

Traditional interpretation

In Śākta thought śakti is the power by which any being acts, inseparable from it. The verse applies the idea to the gods themselves: even the agent of creation, preservation and destruction acts through her, and when she withdraws (as sleep) he does not act at all.

Modern reflection

A modern reflection: the hymn admits its own limit. To say ‘how can you be praised?’ in the middle of praise is a way of keeping words honest about what they cannot hold.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) gives the three acts to the Goddess directly: 264 सृष्टिकर्त्री (creator), 266 गोप्त्री (protector), 268 संहारिणी (destroyer). The Devī Māhātmya keeps them with a god and makes her the power behind him.

Verse 1.84

‹›

so'pi nidrāvaśaṃ nītaḥ kastvāṃ stotumiheśvaraḥ |viṣṇuḥ śarīragrahaṇamahamīśāna eva ca ||

Word by word

  1. सःsaḥhepronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.; correlative of यः in 1.83
  2. अपिapievenindeclinable (emphatic particle)
  3. निद्रावशम्nidrāvaśaminto the power of sleepm. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); goal of नीतः
  4. नीतःnītaḥhas been led, broughtpast passive participle (kta) of √नी (bhvādi, 1U, ‘to lead’), m. nom. sg.; used as the finite verb
  5. कःkaḥwho?interrogative किम्, m. nom. sg.
  6. त्वाम्tvāmyousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, acc. sg.; object of स्तोतुम्
  7. स्तोतुम्stotumto praiseinfinitive (tumun) of √स्तु
  8. इहihahere, in this worldindeclinable (adverb of place)
  9. ईश्वरःīśvaraḥable, capable (lit. ‘master’)m. nom. sg. of ईश्वर; predicate of कः, construed with the infinitive
  10. विष्णुःviṣṇuḥViṣṇum. nom. sg. of विष्णु (u-stem); first subject of कारिताः in 1.85

  13. ईशानःīśānaḥĪśāna (Śiva)m. nom. sg. of ईशान (originally a present participle of √ईश् ‘to rule’)

Translation

— even he has been led into the control of sleep. Who here is able to praise you? Viṣṇu, I and Īśāna too, (have been made by you to undertake) the taking of bodies —

In readable English— even he has been brought under the sway of sleep. Who here has the power to praise you? Viṣṇu, I myself and Īśāna

The second line continues into 1.85: ‘have been made by you to take on bodies’.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सोऽपि so'pi → सः + अपि

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), आद्गुणः (6.1.87), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a becomes -o, and the following a is elided (avagraha).

  • कस्त्वां kastvāṃ → कः + त्वाम्

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

  • स्तोतुमिहेश्वरः stotumiheśvaraḥ → स्तोतुम् + इह + ईश्वरः

    vowel sandhi (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + ī → e (इह + ईश्वरः → इहेश्वरः); the m of स्तोतुम् joins the following vowel unchanged.

  • ईशान एव īśāna eva → ईशानः + एव

    visarga sandhi · भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17), लोपः शाकल्यस्य (8.3.19)

    -aḥ before a vowel other than a: the visarga becomes y, which is dropped, leaving the vowels apart.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • निद्रावशम् nidrāvaśam

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    निद्रा + वश
    Vigraha
    निद्रायाः वशः, तम् nidrāyāḥ vaśaḥ, tam
    Literally
    “the control of sleep”
    In the verse
    the sway of sleep; वशं नी ‘bring under control’ is an idiom

  • शरीरग्रहणम् śarīragrahaṇam

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    शरीर + ग्रहण
    Vigraha
    शरीरस्य ग्रहणम् śarīrasya grahaṇam
    Literally
    “the taking of a body”
    In the verse
    embodiment, assuming bodily form
Morphology & anvaya

  • नीतः nītaḥ

    Past passive participle of √नी used as a finite verb (‘has been led’). With नी the destination stays in the accusative in the passive (निद्रावशम्), while the person led becomes the subject (सः).

  • स्तोतुम् stotum

    Infinitive of purpose with ईश्वरः ‘able’: कः … स्तोतुम् ईश्वरः ‘who is able to praise?’

  • ईश्वरः īśvaraḥ

    Literally ‘master, lord’; with an infinitive it means ‘having power to’. The word picks up परमेश्वरी of 1.82: she is the Īśvarī, and no one is ईश्वर to praise her.

Anvaya · prose order

सः अपि निद्रावशं नीतः। इह त्वां स्तोतुं कः ईश्वरः? विष्णुः, अहम्, ईशानः एव च शरीरग्रहणं (त्वया कारिताः) —

saḥ api nidrāvaśaṃ nītaḥ | iha tvāṃ stotuṃ kaḥ īśvaraḥ? viṣṇuḥ, aham, īśānaḥ eva ca śarīragrahaṇaṃ (tvayā kāritāḥ) —

The first line completes the relative clause of 1.83 (यया त्वया … सः अपि … नीतः) and asks a rhetorical question. The second line names three subjects whose verb, कारिताः, comes in 1.85.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The creator, preserver and consumer of the world lies asleep by her power, so no one is fit to praise her. Brahmā then names the three gods — Viṣṇu, himself and Īśāna (Śiva) — and in the next verse says that their very bodies are her doing.

Traditional interpretation

Śākta readers take 1.84–85 as a foundation for the Goddess’s priority over the three gods: the three who create, preserve and dissolve are themselves made to take form by her. The speaker is Brahmā, one of the three, which gives the admission its weight.

Modern reflection

A modern reflection: the most capable figures in the story are shown to depend on a power they did not make. The hymn turns the gods’ own testimony into a lesson in humility.

Verse 1.85

‹›

kāritāste yato'tastvāṃ kaḥ stotuṃ śaktimān bhavet |sā tvamitthaṃ prabhāvaiḥ svairudārairdevi saṃstutā ||

kāritāḥ · te · yataḥ · ataḥ · tvām · kaḥ · stotum · śaktimān · bhavetsā · tvam · ittham · prabhāvaiḥ · svaiḥ · udāraiḥ · devi · saṃstutā

Word by word

  1. कारिताःkāritāḥhave been made (to undertake)past passive participle (kta) of the causative of √कृ (कारय-), m. nom. pl.; predicate of विष्णुः, अहम्, ईशानः (1.84), with शरीरग्रहणम् as retained object
  2. तेteby youenclitic form of युष्मद् (gen./dat. sg.), here in the sense of the agent of कारिताः
  3. यतःyataḥsince, becauseindeclinable (relative adverb: यद् + -तस्); correlative of अतः
  4. अतःataḥthereforeindeclinable (demonstrative adverb: इदम् + -तस्)
  5. त्वाम्tvāmyousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, acc. sg.; object of स्तोतुम्
  6. कःkaḥwho?interrogative किम्, m. nom. sg.
  7. स्तोतुम्stotumto praiseinfinitive (tumun) of √स्तु
  8. शक्तिमान्śaktimāncapable, having the powerm. nom. sg. of शक्तिमत् (possessive taddhita -मत् on शक्ति)
  9. भवेत्bhavetcould be√भू (bhvādi, 1P), vidhiliṅ (optative), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  10. साsāshe, that (one)pronoun तद्, f. nom. sg.; in apposition to त्वम्: ‘you, such as you are’
  11. त्वम्tvamyousecond-person pronoun युष्मद्, nom. sg.; subject of the imperative मोहय in 1.86
  12. इत्थम्itthamthus, in this wayindeclinable (adverb of manner)
  13. प्रभावैःprabhāvaiḥby (the telling of) your powersm. instr. pl. of प्रभाव
  14. स्वैःsvaiḥyour ownreflexive possessive adjective स्व, m. instr. pl.; agrees with प्रभावैः
  15. उदारैःudāraiḥexalted, noblem. instr. pl. of the adjective उदार; agrees with प्रभावैः
  16. देविdeviO Devīf. voc. sg. of देवी (final ī shortened)
  17. संस्तुताsaṃstutāpraisedpast passive participle (kta) of सम् + √स्तु, f. nom. sg.; agrees with सा त्वम्

Translation

since (we) have been made by you (to take bodies), therefore who could be able to praise you? You, (such as you are), thus praised, O Devī, by (the telling of) your own exalted powers,

In readable Englishhave been made by you to take on bodily form — so who could have the power to praise you? O Devī, praised in this way for your own exalted powers,

The first half finishes 1.84; the second half begins the request that 1.86 states.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • कारितास्ते kāritāste → कारिताः + ते

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s. The same change gives अतस्त्वां.

  • यतोऽतस्त्वां yato'tastvāṃ → यतः + अतः + त्वाम्

    visarga sandhi · अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a becomes -o and the following a is elided (avagraha): यतोऽतः. Then अतः before t becomes अतस्.

  • स्वैरुदारैर्देवि svairudārairdevi → स्वैः + उदारैः + देवि

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66)

    After a vowel other than a/ā (here ai), the visarga appears as r before a vowel and before a voiced consonant.

  • त्वमित्थं प्रभावैः tvamitthaṃ prabhāvaiḥ → त्वम् + इत्थम् + प्रभावैः

    anusvāra · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m joins the vowel of इत्थम्; the m of इत्थम् becomes anusvāra before p.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • कारिताः kāritāḥ

    Causative (णिच्) of √कृ, कारयति ‘makes (someone) do’, in the passive participle. In the passive of a causative the person made to act becomes the subject (विष्णुः, अहम्, ईशानः) and the thing done stays accusative (शरीरग्रहणम्). The plural masculine covers all three.

  • ते te

    The enclitic ते is formally genitive or dative singular of युष्मद्. Purāṇic and epic verse use it with past participles for the agent, ‘by you’; a genitive of the agent with the participle is the grammatical explanation. Reading ते as the plural pronoun ‘they (were made)’ is also possible, but it sits awkwardly with अहम्.

  • भवेत् bhavet

    Optative of possibility in a rhetorical question: कः … शक्तिमान् भवेत् ‘who could be able?’

  • शक्तिमान् śaktimān

    Possessive -मत् on शक्ति; nom. sg. masculine -मान्. The word echoes शक्तिः of 1.83: she is the शक्ति of all, so who is शक्तिमान् to praise her?

Anvaya · prose order

(विष्णुः अहम् ईशानः च शरीरग्रहणं) ते यतः कारिताः, अतः त्वां स्तोतुं कः शक्तिमान् भवेत्? (हे) देवि, सा त्वम् इत्थं स्वैः उदारैः प्रभावैः संस्तुता —

(viṣṇuḥ aham īśānaḥ ca śarīragrahaṇaṃ) te yataḥ kāritāḥ, ataḥ tvāṃ stotuṃ kaḥ śaktimān bhavet? (he) devi, sā tvam itthaṃ svaiḥ udāraiḥ prabhāvaiḥ saṃstutā —

The first line completes the sentence begun in 1.84 with a यतः … अतः (‘since … therefore’) pair. The second line opens a new sentence: सा त्वम् … संस्तुता is the subject of the imperatives in 1.86.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Brahmā ends the praise with its reason: the three gods owe even their bodies to her, so none of them can praise her adequately. The second line turns from praise to petition: ‘you, thus praised …’ leads straight into the request of 1.86.

Traditional interpretation

The hymn closes in the classical manner of a stotra: an admission that praise falls short, then the request. Here the praise has been nothing but a recital of her own powers (प्रभावैः स्वैः) — she is praised with what is already hers.

Modern reflection

A modern reflection: Brahmā asks only after acknowledging what he is. The order — recognition first, request second — is the shape of the whole hymn.

Verse 1.86

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

मोहयैतौ दुराधर्षावसुरौ मधुकैटभौ।प्रबोधं च जगत्स्वामी नीयतामच्युतो लघु॥⁠८६⁠॥

mohayaitau durādharṣāvasurau madhukaiṭabhau |prabodhaṃ ca jagatsvāmī nīyatāmacyuto laghu ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

मोहय · एतौ · दुराधर्षौ · असुरौ · मधुकैटभौप्रबोधम् · च · जगत्स्वामी · नीयताम् · अच्युतः · लघु

mohaya · etau · durādharṣau · asurau · madhukaiṭabhauprabodham · ca · jagatsvāmī · nīyatām · acyutaḥ · laghu

Word by word

  1. मोहयmohayadelude, bewildercausative of √मुह् (divādi, 4P, ‘to be confused’), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  2. एतौetauthese twopronoun एतद्, m. acc. du.
  3. दुराधर्षौdurādharṣauhard to assail, invinciblem. acc. du. of दुराधर्ष (दुर् + आ + √धृष् + kṛt -अ in the sense ‘hard to be done’)
  4. असुरौasurauthe two asurasm. acc. du. of असुर
  5. मधुकैटभौmadhukaiṭabhauMadhu and Kaiṭabham. acc. du.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to असुरौ
  6. प्रबोधम्prabodhamto waking, to wakefulnessm. acc. sg. of प्रबोध (प्र + √बुध्); goal retained with the passive नीयताम्
  7. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  8. जगत्स्वामीjagatsvāmīthe lord of the worldm. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to अच्युतः
  9. नीयताम्nīyatāmlet (him) be brought√नी (bhvādi, 1U, ‘to lead’), karmaṇi prayoga, loṭ (imperative), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  10. अच्युतःacyutaḥAcyuta, the Unfallen (Viṣṇu)m. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); subject of नीयताम्
  11. लघुlaghuquicklyn. acc. sg. of the adjective लघु ‘light, swift’, used adverbially

Translation

delude these two hard-to-assail asuras, Madhu and Kaiṭabha; and let Acyuta, lord of the world, be brought quickly to waking,

In readable Englishbewilder these two invincible asuras, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and let Acyuta, the lord of the world, be woken quickly,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • मोहयैतौ mohayaitau → मोहय + एतौ

    vowel sandhi (vṛddhi) · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88)

    a + e → ai.

  • दुराधर्षावसुरौ durādharṣāvasurau → दुराधर्षौ + असुरौ

    vowel sandhi (āv) · एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78)

    Final au before a vowel becomes āv.

  • नीयतामच्युतो लघु nīyatāmacyuto laghu → नीयताम् + अच्युतः + लघु

    visarga sandhi · ससजुषो रुः (8.2.66), हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced l becomes -o. The final m of नीयताम् joins the following vowel.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • मधुकैटभौ madhukaiṭabhau

    itaretara dvandva

    Members
    मधु + कैटभ
    Vigraha
    मधुः च कैटभः च madhuḥ ca kaiṭabhaḥ ca
    Literally
    “Madhu and Kaiṭabha”
    In the verse
    the two asuras, named as a pair; the dual counts both

  • जगत्स्वामी jagatsvāmī

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    जगत् + स्वामिन्
    Vigraha
    जगतः स्वामी jagataḥ svāmī
    Literally
    “owner of the world”
    In the verse
    lord of the world, i.e. Viṣṇu

  • अच्युतः acyutaḥ

    nañ tatpuruṣa

    Members
    न + च्युत
    Vigraha
    न च्युतः na cyutaḥ
    Literally
    “not fallen”
    In the verse
    the Unfailing One, a name of Viṣṇu
Morphology & anvaya

  • मोहय mohaya

    Causative stem मोहय- (√मुह् with guṇa + णिच्): ‘cause to be bewildered’. The same root gives महामोहा (1.78) and मोह in the king’s question (1.44) and Medhas’s answer (1.53, 1.55).

  • नीयताम् nīyatām

    Passive imperative: नी + -य- + ātmanepada ending -ताम्. With नी the person led becomes the subject (अच्युतः) and the destination stays accusative (प्रबोधम्).

  • दुराधर्षौ durādharṣau

    दुर्- ‘hard to’ with the action noun of आ + √धृष् ‘to assail’: ‘hard to attack’. Grammarians form such words with a special kṛt affix after दुर्, सु and ईषत्.

Anvaya · prose order

(हे देवि) एतौ दुराधर्षौ असुरौ मधुकैटभौ मोहय। जगत्स्वामी अच्युतः च लघु प्रबोधं नीयताम्।

(he devi) etau durādharṣau asurau madhukaiṭabhau mohaya | jagatsvāmī acyutaḥ ca laghu prabodhaṃ nīyatām |

Two requests: an active imperative to the Goddess (मोहय) and a passive imperative about Viṣṇu (नीयताम्), joined by च.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The request at last: two things, one for each side. Delude the asuras; wake Viṣṇu. Both are acts of the same power — the Goddess as Mahāmāyā clouds the asuras’ minds and, as Yoganidrā, releases the god.

Traditional interpretation

The dhyāna of Mahākālī in the Gita Press pāṭha sums up this scene: she is the one whom the lotus-born (Brahmā) praised, when Hari slept, for the slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha (यामस्तौत्स्वपिते हरौ कमलजो हन्तुं मधुं कैटभम्). The dhyāna is liturgical, but it is drawn from these verses.

Modern reflection

A modern reflection: the same power is asked both to confuse and to awaken. The text does not treat illusion and clarity as the work of rival powers.

Verse 1.87

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

बोधश्च क्रियतामस्य हन्तुमेतौ महासुरौ॥⁠८७⁠॥

bodhaśca kriyatāmasya hantumetau mahāsurau ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

बोधः · च · क्रियताम् · अस्य · हन्तुम् · एतौ · महासुरौ

bodhaḥ · ca · kriyatām · asya · hantum · etau · mahāsurau

Word by word

  1. बोधःbodhaḥawareness, wakefulnessm. nom. sg. of बोध (√बुध्); subject of क्रियताम्
  2. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  3. क्रियताम्kriyatāmlet (it) be made√कृ (tanādi, 8U), karmaṇi prayoga, loṭ (imperative), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  4. अस्यasyahis (Viṣṇu’s)pronoun इदम्, m. gen. sg.
  5. हन्तुम्hantumto killinfinitive (tumun) of √हन् (adādi, 2P)
  6. एतौetauthese twopronoun एतद्, m. acc. du.
  7. महासुरौmahāsuraugreat asurasm. acc. du.; compound (see Samāsa); object of हन्तुम्

Translation

and let his awareness be made, to kill these two great asuras.

In readable Englishand let him be roused to slay these two great asuras.

बोधः क्रियताम् (‘let awareness be made’) is rendered ‘let him be roused’.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • बोधश्च bodhaśca → बोधः + च

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34), स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40)

    Visarga before c becomes s, and s next to c becomes ś.

  • क्रियतामस्य kriyatāmasya → क्रियताम् + अस्य

    no change (final m before a vowel) · final m joins a following vowel

    Final m before a vowel is not changed to anusvāra; it is simply written with the vowel. The same in हन्तुमेतौ.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • महासुरौ mahāsurau

    karmadhāraya

    Members
    महत् + असुर
    Vigraha
    महान्तौ च तौ असुरौ च mahāntau ca tau asurau ca
    Literally
    “great asuras”
    In the verse
    the two mighty asuras; महत् takes the form महा- as the first member of a karmadhāraya, and महा + असुर gives महासुर (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, 6.1.101)
Morphology & anvaya

  • क्रियताम् kriyatām

    Passive imperative of √कृ: the root takes the form क्रि- before the passive -य- (क्रियते ‘is done’), with the ending -ताम्.

  • हन्तुम् hantum

    Infinitive of purpose: ‘(so that he may) kill’. The objects एतौ महासुरौ are accusative, governed by the infinitive.

Anvaya · prose order

अस्य बोधः च एतौ महासुरौ हन्तुं क्रियताम्।

asya bodhaḥ ca etau mahāsurau hantuṃ kriyatām |

A second passive imperative, parallel to नीयताम् in 1.86, with an infinitive of purpose.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The last line of Brahmā’s hymn repeats the second request with a purpose added: wake him so that he may kill the two. प्रबोध (1.86) and बोध here may simply be the same waking said twice, or बोध may mean awareness — knowing what must be done; the text does not decide.

Traditional interpretation

The hymn of Brahmā (1.73–87) is the first of the four great hymns of the Devī Māhātmya; the others come in chapters 4, 5 and 11. In the Śākta tradition it is recited as a hymn to the Goddess as Yoganidrā, the sleep of Viṣṇu.

Modern reflection

A modern reflection: the hymn ends with a practical request. Its long praise serves an urgent need, and it says so plainly.

ऋषिः उवाच।

ṛṣiḥ uvāca |

Subject and verb: a speaker label.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Brahmā’s hymn (1.73–87) is over, and the narrator returns: Medhas, telling King Suratha and the merchant Samādhi how the Goddess first appeared, in answer to the king’s question of 1.60–62.

Verse 1.89

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

एवं स्तुता तदा देवी तामसी तत्र वेधसा॥⁠८९⁠॥

evaṃ stutā tadā devī tāmasī tatra vedhasā ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

एवम् · स्तुता · तदा · देवी · तामसी · तत्र · वेधसा

evam · stutā · tadā · devī · tāmasī · tatra · vedhasā

Word by word

  1. एवम्evamthus, in this wayindeclinable (adverb of manner)
  2. स्तुताstutāpraisedpast passive participle (kta) of √स्तु, f. nom. sg.; agrees with देवी
  3. तदाtadāthenindeclinable (adverb of time)
  4. देवीdevīthe Goddessf. nom. sg. of देवी (ī-stem); subject of तस्थौ in 1.91
  5. तामसीtāmasīshe who is of tamas, the dark power (of sleep)f. nom. sg. of तामस (taddhita from तमस्, with vṛddhi; feminine -ई); in apposition to देवी
  6. तत्रtatrathereindeclinable (adverb of place)
  7. वेधसाvedhasāby Vedhas, the Ordainer (Brahmā)m. instr. sg. of वेधस् (s-stem); agent of स्तुता

Translation

Thus praised then there by Vedhas, the Devī Tāmasī —

In readable EnglishPraised in this way by Brahmā, the Ordainer, the Goddess who is the dark power of sleep

तामसी ‘of tamas’ is rendered ‘the dark power of sleep’ because in this scene she is Viṣṇu’s Yoganidrā (1.66, 1.69); the sentence runs on to 1.91.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • एवं स्तुता evaṃ stutā → एवम् + स्तुता

    anusvāra · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • तामसी tāmasī

    Taddhita in -अ with vṛddhi of the first vowel (तमस् → तामस ‘belonging to tamas’); the feminine takes -ई. Tamas is darkness, inertia — the quality of sleep.

  • वेधसा vedhasā

    Instrumental of वेधस् ‘disposer, ordainer’, an old name of Brahmā; s-stems keep the s before vowel endings (वेधसा, वेधसः).

Anvaya · prose order

एवं तदा तत्र वेधसा स्तुता तामसी देवी —

evaṃ tadā tatra vedhasā stutā tāmasī devī —

The subject with its participle and agent; the main verbs (निर्गम्य … तस्थौ) come in 1.90–91.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The hymn has its effect. Medhas names the Goddess here तामसी, ‘of tamas’: she is the dark, heavy power of sleep that holds Viṣṇu, the Yoganidrā Brahmā has just praised.

Traditional interpretation

The Gita Press pāṭha assigns the first carita to Mahākālī as presiding deity (its viniyoga and dhyāna); that assignment is liturgical tradition. तामसी is the word in the Purāṇa’s own text that the assignment most naturally connects with: the first manifestation is the Goddess under the guṇa of tamas.

Verse 1.90

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

विष्णोः प्रबोधनार्थाय निहन्तुं मधुकैटभौ।नेत्रास्यनासिकाबाहुहृदयेभ्यस्तथोरसः॥⁠९०⁠॥

viṣṇoḥ prabodhanārthāya nihantuṃ madhukaiṭabhau |netrāsyanāsikābāhuhṛdayebhyastathorasaḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

विष्णोः · प्रबोधनार्थाय · निहन्तुम् · मधुकैटभौनेत्रास्यनासिकाबाहुहृदयेभ्यः · तथा · उरसः

viṣṇoḥ · prabodhanārthāya · nihantum · madhukaiṭabhaunetrāsyanāsikābāhuhṛdayebhyaḥ · tathā · urasaḥ

Word by word

  1. विष्णोःviṣṇoḥof Viṣṇum. gen. sg. of विष्णु (u-stem); objective genitive with प्रबोधन-
  2. प्रबोधनार्थायprabodhanārthāyafor the purpose of awakeningm. dat. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); dative of purpose
  3. निहन्तुम्nihantumto slayinfinitive (tumun) of नि + √हन् (adādi, 2P)
  4. मधुकैटभौmadhukaiṭabhauMadhu and Kaiṭabham. acc. du.; itaretara dvandva (as in 1.86); object of निहन्तुम्
  5. नेत्रास्यनासिकाबाहुहृदयेभ्यःnetrāsyanāsikābāhuhṛdayebhyaḥfrom (his) eyes, mouth, nose, arms and heartn. abl. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); ablative of separation with निर्गम्य (1.91)
  6. तथाtathāand likewiseindeclinable (connective)
  7. उरसःurasaḥfrom (his) chestn. abl. sg. of उरस् (s-stem)

Translation

for the sake of awakening Viṣṇu, to slay Madhu and Kaiṭabha, from (his) eyes, mouth, nose, arms and heart, and likewise from (his) chest

In readable Englishso that Viṣṇu might wake and slay Madhu and Kaiṭabha, came forth from his eyes, mouth, nose, arms and heart, and from his breast,

‘Came forth’ is supplied from निर्गम्य at the start of 1.91; ‘his’ (Viṣṇu’s) is understood.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • हृदयेभ्यस्तथोरसः hṛdayebhyastathorasaḥ → हृदयेभ्यः + तथा + उरसः

    visarga and vowel sandhi (guṇa) · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34); आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    Visarga before t becomes s; then ā + u → o (तथा + उरसः → तथोरसः).

  • नेत्रास्य netrāsya → नेत्र + आस्य

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + ā → ā.

  • प्रबोधनार्थाय prabodhanārthāya → प्रबोधन + अर्थाय

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + a → ā.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • प्रबोधनार्थाय prabodhanārthāya

    caturthī tatpuruṣa (an अर्थ-compound, which grammarians treat as always compounded)

    Members
    प्रबोधन + अर्थ
    Vigraha
    प्रबोधनाय इदम् (प्रबोधनार्थम्), तस्मै prabodhanāya idam (prabodhanārtham), tasmai
    Literally
    “for the purpose of awakening”
    In the verse
    so that (Viṣṇu) might wake
    Alternative
    Also analysed as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, प्रबोधनस्य अर्थः, ‘the purpose of waking’, put in the dative. The sense is the same; the caturthī analysis is the grammarians’ usual one for अर्थ in this use. The same word-form, विबोधनार्थाय, stands in 1.70.

  • नेत्रास्यनासिकाबाहुहृदयेभ्यः netrāsyanāsikābāhuhṛdayebhyaḥ

    itaretara dvandva

    Members
    नेत्र + आस्य + नासिका + बाहु + हृदय
    Vigraha
    नेत्रे च आस्यं च नासिका च बाहू च हृदयं च, तेभ्यः netre ca āsyaṃ ca nāsikā ca bāhū ca hṛdayaṃ ca, tebhyaḥ
    Literally
    “from eyes, mouth, nose, arms and heart”
    In the verse
    from every seat of sleep in Viṣṇu’s body; उरस् (chest) follows outside the compound
Morphology & anvaya

  • निहन्तुम् nihantum

    Infinitive of नि + √हन्: the prefix नि- intensifies (‘strike down, slay’). It stands beside a dative of purpose (प्रबोधनार्थाय) with the same function: two purposes, waking and slaying.

  • उरसः urasaḥ

    Ablative singular of the s-stem उरस् ‘chest’. It is left outside the dvandva, joined by तथा — a common way of completing a list in verse.

Anvaya · prose order

(सा देवी) विष्णोः प्रबोधनार्थाय मधुकैटभौ निहन्तुं (च) नेत्रास्यनासिकाबाहुहृदयेभ्यः तथा उरसः (निर्गम्य) —

(sā devī) viṣṇoḥ prabodhanārthāya madhukaiṭabhau nihantuṃ (ca) netrāsyanāsikābāhuhṛdayebhyaḥ tathā urasaḥ (nirgamya) —

Two expressions of purpose and two ablatives of separation; the absolutive निर्गम्य that governs the ablatives comes at the start of 1.91.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The Goddess grants both requests of the hymn. She withdraws from Viṣṇu’s body, limb by limb — eyes, mouth, nose, arms, heart, chest — so that he wakes, and wakes in order to kill the two asuras.

Traditional interpretation

Brahmā had praised her as dwelling in Hari’s eyes (हरिनेत्रकृतालयाम्, 1.70); the eyes stand first here as she leaves. Sleep is pictured as a presence in the body that departs by every organ.

Verse 1.91

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

निर्गम्य दर्शने तस्थौ ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः।उत्तस्थौ च जगन्नाथस्तया मुक्तो जनार्दनः॥⁠९१⁠॥

nirgamya darśane tasthau brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ |uttasthau ca jagannāthastayā mukto janārdanaḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

निर्गम्य · दर्शने · तस्थौ · ब्रह्मणः · अव्यक्तजन्मनःउत्तस्थौ · च · जगन्नाथः · तया · मुक्तः · जनार्दनः

nirgamya · darśane · tasthau · brahmaṇaḥ · avyaktajanmanaḥuttasthau · ca · jagannāthaḥ · tayā · muktaḥ · janārdanaḥ

Word by word

  1. निर्गम्यnirgamyahaving come outabsolutive (ल्यप्) of निर् + √गम् (bhvādi, 1P, ‘to go’)
  2. दर्शनेdarśanein the sight (of), within viewn. loc. sg. of दर्शन
  3. तस्थौtasthaustood√स्था (bhvādi, 1P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  4. ब्रह्मणःbrahmaṇaḥof Brahmām. gen. sg. of ब्रह्मन् (n-stem); with दर्शने
  5. अव्यक्तजन्मनःavyaktajanmanaḥwhose birth is unmanifestm. gen. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies ब्रह्मणः
  6. उत्तस्थौuttasthaurose upउद् + √स्था, liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  7. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  8. जगन्नाथःjagannāthaḥthe lord of the worldm. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to जनार्दनः
  9. तयाtayāby herpronoun तद्, f. instr. sg.; agent of मुक्तः
  10. मुक्तःmuktaḥreleasedpast passive participle (kta) of √मुच् (tudādi, 6U, ‘to release’), m. nom. sg.
  11. जनार्दनःjanārdanaḥJanārdana (Viṣṇu)m. nom. sg.; a name of Viṣṇu; subject of उत्तस्थौ

Translation

having come out, (she) stood in the sight of Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest. And Janārdana, lord of the world, released by her, rose up

In readable Englishand stood before the eyes of Brahmā, whose birth is beyond knowing. Released by her, Janārdana, lord of the world, rose

‘Came forth’ was given in 1.90; the verse continues into 1.92 (‘from his serpent couch on the one ocean’).

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ → ब्रह्मणः + अव्यक्तजन्मनः

    visarga sandhi · अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a becomes -o and the following a is elided (avagraha).

  • जगन्नाथस्तया jagannāthastayā → जगन्नाथः + तया

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

  • मुक्तो जनार्दनः mukto janārdanaḥ → मुक्तः + जनार्दनः

    visarga sandhi · हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced j becomes -o.

  • जगन्नाथ jagannātha → जगत् + नाथ

    consonant sandhi inside a compound (nasalisation) · यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा (8.4.45)

    Final t before the nasal n becomes n. The rule is optional (जगद्नाथ is possible), but the nasal form is usual.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • अव्यक्तजन्मनः avyaktajanmanaḥ

    bahuvrīhi (अव्यक्त itself a nañ tatpuruṣa: न व्यक्तम्)

    Members
    अव्यक्त + जन्मन्
    Vigraha
    अव्यक्तं जन्म यस्य सः, तस्य avyaktaṃ janma yasya saḥ, tasya
    Literally
    “of him whose birth is unmanifest”
    In the verse
    of Brahmā, whose origin is beyond perception
    Alternative
    Also read as a vyadhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi, अव्यक्तात् जन्म यस्य सः, ‘whose birth is from the Unmanifest (avyakta, primal nature)’. Both readings are found for this epithet of Brahmā; the first keeps the members in the same case and is the simpler analysis.

  • जगन्नाथः jagannāthaḥ

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    जगत् + नाथ
    Vigraha
    जगतः नाथः jagataḥ nāthaḥ
    Literally
    “protector of the world”
    In the verse
    lord of the world, Viṣṇu
Morphology & anvaya

  • निर्गम्य nirgamya

    Absolutive with a prefix takes -य (ल्यप्) instead of -त्वा. With √गम् the root nasal may stay (निर्गम्य) or drop (निर्गत्य).

  • उत्तस्थौ uttasthau

    Perfect of √स्था: the reduplicated syllable is त — when a root begins with a sibilant + stop, the stop is repeated, without aspiration (थ् → त्): तस्थौ, with the ending -औ. With उद्, the d becomes t before t (खरि च, 8.4.55): उत्तस्थौ ‘rose’.

  • मुक्तः muktaḥ

    Past participle of √मुच्: च् becomes क् before त (मुच् + त → मुक्त). With the instrumental तया: ‘released by her’.

Anvaya · prose order

(सा) निर्गम्य अव्यक्तजन्मनः ब्रह्मणः दर्शने तस्थौ। तया मुक्तः जगन्नाथः जनार्दनः च उत्तस्थौ।

(sā) nirgamya avyaktajanmanaḥ brahmaṇaḥ darśane tasthau | tayā muktaḥ jagannāthaḥ janārdanaḥ ca uttasthau |

Two clauses joined by च, each ending in the perfect of √स्था — तस्थौ (she stood) and उत्तस्थौ (he rose).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Two movements answer each other: she comes out and stands where Brahmā can see her (तस्थौ), and Viṣṇu, freed, rises (उत्तस्थौ). The Goddess praised in the hymn is now visible to the one who praised her.

Traditional interpretation

Medhas had said that the Goddess, though eternal, is spoken of as ‘born’ whenever she appears for the gods’ work (1.65–66). This is the first such appearance: not a birth, but a coming forth from where she already was.

Verse 1.92

एकार्णवेऽहिशयनात्ततः स ददृशे च तौ।मधुकैटभौ दुरात्मानावतिवीर्यपराक्रमौ॥⁠९२⁠॥

ekārṇave'hiśayanāttataḥ sa dadṛśe ca tau |madhukaiṭabhau durātmānāvativīryaparākramau ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

एकार्णवे · अहिशयनात् · ततः · सः · ददृशे · च · तौमधुकैटभौ · दुरात्मानौ · अतिवीर्यपराक्रमौ

ekārṇave · ahiśayanāt · tataḥ · saḥ · dadṛśe · ca · taumadhukaiṭabhau · durātmānau · ativīryaparākramau

Word by word

  1. एकार्णवेekārṇaveon the single ocean (the flood at the end of an age)m. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)
  2. अहिशयनात्ahiśayanātfrom the serpent-couchn. abl. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); ablative of separation with उत्तस्थौ (1.91)
  3. ततःtataḥthenindeclinable (adverb: तद् + -तस्)
  4. सःsaḥhe (Viṣṇu)pronoun तद्, m. nom. sg.
  5. ददृशेdadṛśesaw√दृश् (bhvādi, 1P, ‘to see’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, with an ātmanepada ending (ārṣa use; see Morph)
  6. चcaandindeclinable (conjunction)
  7. तौtauthose twopronoun तद्, m. acc. du.; object of ददृशे

  9. दुरात्मानौdurātmānauevil-mindedm. acc. du. of दुरात्मन्; compound (see Samāsa)
