Translation

from the serpent-couch on the single ocean. Then he saw those two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, evil-minded, of surpassing strength and valour,

In readable Englishfrom his serpent couch on the one ocean. Then he saw the two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, evil-hearted and of surpassing strength and prowess,

Textual verification / uncertain: Metre: the pāda मधुकैटभौ दुरात्मानौ is hypermetric (nine syllables) in every witness; no emendation is made. ददृशे is taken as active (‘saw’) with an ātmanepada ending, as the accusative तौ requires.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • एकार्णवेऽहिशयनात् ekārṇave'hiśayanāt → एकार्णवे + अहिशयनात्

    vowel sandhi (pūrvarūpa) · एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -e + a- → -e’-: the initial a is elided (avagraha).

  • शयनात्ततः śayanāttataḥ → अहिशयनात् + ततः

    no change · खरि च (8.4.55)

    Final t before the unvoiced t stays t; the two words are only written together.

  • ततः स ददृशे tataḥ sa dadṛśe → ततः + सः + ददृशे

    visarga sandhi (special rule for सः) · एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132)

    The visarga of सः is dropped before a consonant. ततः before s keeps its visarga (the optional s-assimilation is not used).

  • दुरात्मानावति durātmānāvati → दुरात्मानौ + अति(वीर्यपराक्रमौ)

    vowel sandhi (āv) · एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78)

    Final au before a vowel becomes āv.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • एकार्णवे ekārṇave

    karmadhāraya

    Members
    एक + अर्णव
    Vigraha
    एकः अर्णवः, तस्मिन् ekaḥ arṇavaḥ, tasmin
    Literally
    “in the one ocean”
    In the verse
    on the single ocean of the dissolution, when the world is all water (एकार्णवीकृते, 1.66)

  • अहिशयनात् ahiśayanāt

    karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa: ‘the serpent, which is the couch’)

    Members
    अहि + शयन
    Vigraha
    अहिः एव शयनम्, तस्मात् ahiḥ eva śayanam, tasmāt
    Literally
    “from the serpent-bed”
    In the verse
    from Śeṣa, the serpent on which Viṣṇu sleeps (आस्तीर्य शेषम्, 1.67)
    Alternative
    Also possible as a saptamī tatpuruṣa with शयन as an action noun, अहौ शयनम् ‘lying on the serpent’: ‘from (his) lying on the serpent’. The karmadhāraya fits the ablative of place better.

  • दुरात्मानौ durātmānau

    bahuvrīhi (prādi first member दुर्)

    Members
    दुर् + आत्मन्
    Vigraha
    दुष्टः आत्मा ययोः तौ duṣṭaḥ ātmā yayoḥ tau
    Literally
    “whose selves are bad”
    In the verse
    evil-hearted, wicked

  • अतिवीर्यपराक्रमौ ativīryaparākramau

    bahuvrīhi containing an itaretara dvandva (वीर्यपराक्रम) and the prefix अति

    Members
    अति + वीर्य + पराक्रम
    Vigraha
    वीर्यं च पराक्रमः च वीर्यपराक्रमौ; अतिशयितौ वीर्यपराक्रमौ ययोः तौ vīryaṃ ca parākramaḥ ca vīryaparākramau; atiśayitau vīryaparākramau yayoḥ tau
    Literally
    “whose strength and valour are surpassing”
    In the verse
    of exceeding might and prowess
Morphology & anvaya

  • ददृशे dadṛśe

    Perfect of √दृश् with reduplication (द-दृश्-) and the ātmanepada ending -ए. √दृश् is parasmaipada (active perfect ददर्श), and ददृशे normally means ‘was seen’. Here the subject is सः and the object तौ is accusative, so the sense must be active, ‘he saw’ — an epic (ārṣa) use of the middle ending.

  • दुरात्मानौ durātmānau

    Accusative dual of the n-stem आत्मन् at the end of a bahuvrīhi: -आनौ (strong stem).

Anvaya · prose order

(सः) एकार्णवे अहिशयनात् (उत्तस्थौ)। ततः सः दुरात्मानौ अतिवीर्यपराक्रमौ तौ मधुकैटभौ च ददृशे —

(saḥ) ekārṇave ahiśayanāt (uttasthau) | tataḥ saḥ durātmānau ativīryaparākramau tau madhukaiṭabhau ca dadṛśe —

The first two words complete 1.91 (‘rose … from the serpent-couch on the one ocean’). Then a new clause: subject सः, verb ददृशे, and the object तौ with its appositions running into the second line.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Viṣṇu rises from Śeṣa on the cosmic waters and, for the first time, sees the two asuras who were about to kill Brahmā. The verse sets the scene of the fight: one ocean, no land.

Traditional interpretation

The pāda मधुकैटभौ दुरात्मानौ has nine syllables, one more than the anuṣṭubh pāda; every witness reads it so (see corrections.json, metre notes). The text is kept as it stands.

Verse 1.93

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

क्रोधरक्तेक्षणावत्तुं ब्रह्माणं जनितोद्यमौ।समुत्थाय ततस्ताभ्यां युयुधे भगवान् हरिः॥⁠९३⁠॥

krodharaktekṣaṇāvattuṃ brahmāṇaṃ janitodyamau |samutthāya tatastābhyāṃ yuyudhe bhagavān hariḥ ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

क्रोधरक्तेक्षणौ · अत्तुम् · ब्रह्माणम् · जनितोद्यमौसमुत्थाय · ततः · ताभ्याम् · युयुधे · भगवान् · हरिः

krodharaktekṣaṇau · attum · brahmāṇam · janitodyamausamutthāya · tataḥ · tābhyām · yuyudhe · bhagavān · hariḥ

Word by word

  1. क्रोधरक्तेक्षणौkrodharaktekṣaṇauwhose eyes were red with angerm. acc. du.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies तौ (1.92)
  2. अत्तुम्attumto devourinfinitive (tumun) of √अद् (adādi, 2P, ‘to eat’)
  3. ब्रह्माणम्brahmāṇamBrahmām. acc. sg. of ब्रह्मन्; object of अत्तुम्
  4. जनितोद्यमौjanitodyamauwho had set about the attemptm. acc. du.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies तौ
  5. समुत्थायsamutthāyahaving risen upabsolutive (ल्यप्) of सम् + उद् + √स्था
  6. ततःtataḥthenindeclinable (adverb)
  7. ताभ्याम्tābhyāmwith those twopronoun तद्, m. instr. du.; instrumental of accompaniment with युयुधे (‘fought with’)
  8. युयुधेyuyudhefought√युध् (divādi, 4Ā, ‘to fight’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada
  9. भगवान्bhagavānthe Blessed Onem. nom. sg. of भगवत् (possessive -वत् on भग)
  10. हरिःhariḥHari (Viṣṇu)m. nom. sg. of हरि (i-stem); subject of युयुधे

Translation

with eyes red with anger, having set about devouring Brahmā. Having risen up, then, the Blessed Hari fought with the two

In readable Englishtheir eyes red with rage, bent on devouring Brahmā. Rising up, the Lord Hari then fought with them

The fight’s duration and manner follow in 1.94.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • क्रोधरक्तेक्षणावत्तुं krodharaktekṣaṇāvattuṃ → क्रोधरक्तेक्षणौ + अत्तुम्

    vowel sandhi (āv) · एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78)

    Final au before a vowel becomes āv; the m of अत्तुम् becomes anusvāra before b (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

  • ततस्ताभ्यां tatastābhyāṃ → ततः + ताभ्याम्

    visarga sandhi · विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    Visarga before t becomes s.

  • रक्तेक्षणा raktekṣaṇā → रक्त + ईक्षणौ

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + ī → e. Likewise जनित + उद्यम → जनितोद्यम (a + u → o).

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • क्रोधरक्तेक्षणौ krodharaktekṣaṇau

    bahuvrīhi (its first part क्रोधरक्त is a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa: क्रोधेन रक्ते)

    Members
    क्रोध + रक्त + ईक्षण
    Vigraha
    क्रोधेन रक्ते ईक्षणे ययोः तौ krodhena rakte īkṣaṇe yayoḥ tau
    Literally
    “whose eyes are red with anger”
    In the verse
    glaring with rage

  • जनितोद्यमौ janitodyamau

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    जनित + उद्यम
    Vigraha
    जनितः उद्यमः याभ्यां तौ janitaḥ udyamaḥ yābhyāṃ tau
    Literally
    “by whom an effort had been produced”
    In the verse
    having set about it, ready to strike
Morphology & anvaya

  • युयुधे yuyudhe

    Perfect ātmanepada of √युध्, reduplicated यु-युध्-; √युध् is conjugated in the middle (युध्यते). With the instrumental ताभ्याम् it means ‘fought with them’.

  • समुत्थाय samutthāya

    सम् + उद् + √स्था with ल्यप्: after उद् the s of स्था drops (उद् + स्था → उत्था), giving उत्थाय ‘having risen’.

  • अत्तुम् attum

    Infinitive of √अद्: अद् + तुम् with d unvoiced before t. In 1.68 the two were ready ‘to kill’ Brahmā (हन्तुम्); here they are ready ‘to devour’ him.

Anvaya · prose order

(तौ) क्रोधरक्तेक्षणौ ब्रह्माणम् अत्तुं जनितोद्यमौ (ददृशे)। ततः भगवान् हरिः समुत्थाय ताभ्यां युयुधे।

(tau) krodharaktekṣaṇau brahmāṇam attuṃ janitodyamau (dadṛśe) | tataḥ bhagavān hariḥ samutthāya tābhyāṃ yuyudhe |

The first line still describes the object of ददृशे (1.92); the second is a new sentence with an absolutive (समुत्थाय) and the main verb युयुधे.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The danger is at its height: the asuras, eyes red with fury, are about to eat Brahmā. Viṣṇu stands up and fights them himself.

Modern reflection

A modern reflection: the hymn’s two requests are now visible as events — the god is awake and acts. The Goddess has not fought; she has made the fight possible.

Verse 1.94

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि बाहुप्रहरणो विभुः।तावप्यतिबलोन्मत्तौ महामायाविमोहितौ॥⁠९४⁠॥

pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi bāhupraharaṇo vibhuḥ |tāvapyatibalonmattau mahāmāyāvimohitau ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

पञ्च · वर्षसहस्राणि · बाहुप्रहरणः · विभुःतौ · अपि · अतिबलोन्मत्तौ · महामायाविमोहितौ

pañca · varṣasahasrāṇi · bāhupraharaṇaḥ · vibhuḥtau · api · atibalonmattau · mahāmāyāvimohitau

Word by word

  1. पञ्चpañcafivenumeral पञ्चन्, n. acc. pl. (numerals five to nineteen have no gender distinction); qualifies वर्षसहस्राणि
  2. वर्षसहस्राणिvarṣasahasrāṇithousands of yearsn. acc. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); accusative of duration
  3. बाहुप्रहरणःbāhupraharaṇaḥwith his arms as weaponsm. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies विभुः
  4. विभुःvibhuḥthe all-pervading Lordm. nom. sg. of विभु (u-stem); in apposition to हरिः (1.93)
  5. तौtauthose twopronoun तद्, m. nom. du.; subject of उक्तवन्तौ (1.95)
  6. अपिapiand, in turnindeclinable (particle)
  7. अतिबलोन्मत्तौatibalonmattaumaddened by their excessive strengthm. nom. du.; compound (see Samāsa)
  8. महामायाविमोहितौmahāmāyāvimohitaudeluded by Mahāmāyām. nom. du.; compound (see Samāsa)

Translation

for five thousands of years, the all-pervading one, with his arms as weapons. And those two, maddened by excessive strength, deluded by Mahāmāyā,

In readable Englishfor five thousand years, the all-pervading Lord fighting with his bare arms. Then the two, drunk with their own great strength and deluded by Mahāmāyā,

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • बाहुप्रहरणो विभुः bāhupraharaṇo vibhuḥ → बाहुप्रहरणः + विभुः

    visarga sandhi · हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced v becomes -o.

  • तावप्यति tāvapyati → तौ + अपि + अति(बलोन्मत्तौ)

    vowel sandhi (āv and yaṇ) · एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78); इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    au before a becomes āv (तौ + अपि → तावपि); then i before a becomes y (अपि + अति → अप्यति).

  • बलोन्मत्तौ balonmattau → बल + उन्मत्तौ

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + u → o.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • वर्षसहस्राणि varṣasahasrāṇi

    ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa

    Members
    वर्ष + सहस्र
    Vigraha
    वर्षाणां सहस्राणि varṣāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi
    Literally
    “thousands of years”
    In the verse
    with पञ्च: five thousand years
    Alternative
    The printed text writes पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि as one; it could be taken as a single numeral compound (dvigu type). A dvigu proper is a collective singular, so with the plural ending the numeral is more naturally a separate word qualifying वर्षसहस्राणि, as here; the sense is unchanged.

  • बाहुप्रहरणः bāhupraharaṇaḥ

    bahuvrīhi

    Members
    बाहु + प्रहरण
    Vigraha
    बाहू एव प्रहरणे यस्य सः bāhū eva praharaṇe yasya saḥ
    Literally
    “he whose weapons are his arms”
    In the verse
    fighting with his bare arms

  • अतिबलोन्मत्तौ atibalonmattau

    tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa, with a prādi tatpuruṣa (अतिबल) as first member

    Members
    अतिबल + उन्मत्त
    Vigraha
    अतिबलेन उन्मत्तौ (अतिबलम् = अतिशयितं बलम्) atibalena unmattau (atibalam = atiśayitaṃ balam)
    Literally
    “maddened by excessive strength”
    In the verse
    drunk with their own power
    Alternative
    Also possible: अतिबलौ च उन्मत्तौ च, ‘exceedingly strong and maddened’ (karmadhāraya of two adjectives). The instrumental reading gives the cause of their madness, which the story bears out.

  • महामायाविमोहितौ mahāmāyāvimohitau

    tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa

    Members
    महामाया + विमोहित
    Vigraha
    महामायया विमोहितौ mahāmāyayā vimohitau
    Literally
    “deluded by the Great Māyā”
    In the verse
    bewildered by Mahāmāyā, as Brahmā had asked (मोहयैतौ, 1.86)
Morphology & anvaya

  • वर्षसहस्राणि varṣasahasrāṇi

    Accusative of extent of time: ‘for (five) thousands of years’.

  • महामायाविमोहितौ mahāmāyāvimohitau

    विमोहित is the past participle of the causative of वि + √मुह् (‘made to be bewildered’); the causative agent stands in the compound’s first member, महामाया.

Anvaya · prose order

(सः) विभुः बाहुप्रहरणः पञ्च वर्षसहस्राणि (ताभ्यां युयुधे)। अतिबलोन्मत्तौ महामायाविमोहितौ तौ अपि (केशवम् उक्तवन्तौ) —

(saḥ) vibhuḥ bāhupraharaṇaḥ pañca varṣasahasrāṇi (tābhyāṃ yuyudhe) | atibalonmattau mahāmāyāvimohitau tau api (keśavam uktavantau) —

The first line completes 1.93 (‘fought … for five thousand years’); the second gives the subject of a new sentence whose verb, उक्तवन्तौ, comes in 1.95.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The battle lasts five thousand years, Viṣṇu fighting with his arms alone, and is not decided by force. It turns when Mahāmāyā clouds the asuras’ minds — the first of Brahmā’s requests (1.86) fulfilled.

Traditional interpretation

The compound महामायाविमोहितौ takes up Medhas’s teaching: Mahāmāyā draws even the minds of the wise into delusion (1.55–56). The asuras are her first example in the stories.

Verse 1.95

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

उक्तवन्तौ वरोऽस्मत्तो व्रियतामिति केशवम्॥⁠९५⁠॥

uktavantau varo'smatto vriyatāmiti keśavam ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

उक्तवन्तौ · वरः · अस्मत्तः · व्रियताम् · इति · केशवम्

uktavantau · varaḥ · asmattaḥ · vriyatām · iti · keśavam

Word by word

  1. उक्तवन्तौuktavantausaidpast active participle (ktavatu) of √वच्, m. nom. du.; used as the finite verb, subject तौ (1.94)
  2. वरःvaraḥa boonm. nom. sg. of वर; subject of the passive व्रियताम्
  3. अस्मत्तःasmattaḥfrom usfirst-person pronoun अस्मद् with the suffix -तस् (ablative sense), indeclinable form
  4. व्रियताम्vriyatāmlet (it) be chosen√वृ (‘to choose’; वृङ्, kryādi 9Ā), karmaṇi prayoga, loṭ (imperative), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana
  5. इतिitithus (closing the quotation)indeclinable (quotative particle)
  6. केशवम्keśavamto Keśava (Viṣṇu)m. acc. sg. of केशव; the person addressed, accusative with a verb of speaking

Translation

said to Keśava: ‘Let a boon be chosen from us.’

In readable Englishsaid to Keśava, “Choose a boon from us.”

The passive ‘let a boon be chosen’ is rendered as an active imperative.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • वरोऽस्मत्तो varo'smatto → वरः + अस्मत्तः

    visarga sandhi · अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते (6.1.113), एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109)

    -aḥ before a becomes -o and the following a is elided (avagraha).

  • वरोऽस्मत्तो व्रियताम् varo'smatto vriyatām → अस्मत्तः + व्रियताम्

    visarga sandhi · हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    -aḥ before the voiced v becomes -o.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • उक्तवन्तौ uktavantau

    Past active participle in -वत् (ktavatu) of √वच्, with samprasāraṇa (वच् → उक्-): उक्तवत् ‘having said’. In narrative it does the work of a finite past verb: ‘(they) said’. Dual, for the two asuras.

  • अस्मत्तः asmattaḥ

    The suffix -तस् added to a pronoun stem gives an ablative adverb: अस्मत्तः ‘from us’, त्वत्तः ‘from you’ (1.62).

  • व्रियताम् vriyatām

    Passive imperative of √वृ ‘to choose’: the root becomes व्रि- before the passive -य-. ‘Let a boon be chosen from us’ is the courteous form of ‘choose a boon’.

Anvaya · prose order

(तौ) ‘अस्मत्तः वरः व्रियताम्’ इति केशवम् उक्तवन्तौ।

(tau) ‘asmattaḥ varaḥ vriyatām’ iti keśavam uktavantau |

The subject तौ is in 1.94; the quoted words are closed by इति, and केशवम् is the person addressed.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The delusion shows itself as pride: after five thousand years of combat the asuras, pleased with their opponent, offer him a boon — as though they were the gods and he the petitioner.

Traditional interpretation

The reversal is the point the tradition draws: a boon is a superior’s gift. In offering one to Viṣṇu the asuras act out the confusion that Mahāmāyā has worked in them (1.94).

Verse 1.96

Speaker
‹›

श्रीभगवानुवाच॥⁠९६⁠॥

śrībhagavānuvāca ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

श्रीभगवान् · उवाच

śrībhagavān · uvāca

Word by word

  1. श्रीभगवान्śrībhagavānthe Blessed Lord (Viṣṇu)m. nom. sg. of भगवत् with the honorific prefix श्री; subject of उवाच
  2. उवाचuvācasaid√वच् (adādi, 2P, ‘to speak’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada

Translation

The Blessed Lord said:

In readable EnglishThe Blessed Lord said:

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

No sandhi joins the words of this verse.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • श्रीभगवान् śrībhagavān

    Nominative singular of भगवत् ‘possessing fortune, blessed’ (भग + possessive -वत्): the strong stem -वन्त्, with the final consonants reduced and the vowel lengthened, gives -वान्.

Anvaya · prose order

श्रीभगवान् उवाच।

śrībhagavān uvāca |

Subject and verb: a speaker label.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Viṣṇu answers the asuras’ offer. Inside Medhas’s narration the text quotes the god directly, under the same label the Bhagavad Gītā uses for Kṛṣṇa’s speeches.

Verse 1.97

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

भवेतामद्य मे तुष्टौ मम वध्यावुभावपि॥⁠९७⁠॥

bhavetāmadya me tuṣṭau mama vadhyāvubhāvapi ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

भवेताम् · अद्य · मे · तुष्टौ · मम · वध्यौ · उभौ · अपि

bhavetām · adya · me · tuṣṭau · mama · vadhyau · ubhau · api

Word by word

  1. भवेताम्bhavetāmmay (you two) be√भू (bhvādi, 1P), vidhiliṅ (optative), prathama-puruṣa dvivacana, parasmaipada; third person because its subject is the noun उभौ
  2. अद्यadyatoday, nowindeclinable (adverb of time)
  3. मेmewith meenclitic form of अस्मद्, gen. sg.; construed with तुष्टौ
  4. तुष्टौtuṣṭaupleased, satisfiedpast participle (kta) of √तुष् (divādi, 4P, ‘to be content’), m. nom. du.
  5. ममmamaby mefirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg.; genitive of the agent with the gerundive वध्यौ
  6. वध्यौvadhyauto be slaingerundive (kṛtya, -य) from वध (the slaying-stem of √हन्), m. nom. du.; predicate of भवेताम्
  7. उभौubhaubothpronominal adjective उभ, m. nom. du.; subject
  8. अपिapiboth … indeedindeclinable (particle; with उभौ, ‘the two of you alike’)

Translation

(Since you are) pleased with me today, may you both be (persons) to be slain by me.

In readable EnglishIf you are pleased with me, then let both of you be slain by me today.

The participle तुष्टौ is rendered as a condition (‘if you are pleased’); the Sanskrit states it without a conjunction.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • भवेतामद्य bhavetāmadya → भवेताम् + अद्य

    no change (final m before a vowel) · final m joins a following vowel

    Final m before a vowel is written with it, not as anusvāra.

  • वध्यावुभावपि vadhyāvubhāvapi → वध्यौ + उभौ + अपि

    vowel sandhi (āv) · एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78)

    Final au before a vowel becomes āv, twice: वध्यौ + उभौ → वध्यावुभौ; उभौ + अपि → उभावपि.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • भवेताम् bhavetām

    Optative third-person dual. The subject is the pronominal adjective उभौ ‘both’, so the verb is third person even though Viṣṇu is speaking to the two asuras (‘may both (of you) be …’); an understood भवन्तौ ‘your honours’ would give the same person. The optative expresses a wish that is also a demand: it is the boon he names.

  • वध्यौ vadhyau

    Gerundive ‘to be killed, fit to be killed’, from वध, the form √हन् takes in several derivatives. With a gerundive the agent may stand in the genitive: मम वध्यौ ‘to be killed by me’.

  • तुष्टौ tuṣṭau

    Past participle of √तुष् in an active sense (‘satisfied’), with the genitive मे ‘with me’. It states the condition the asuras themselves have just declared.

Anvaya · prose order

(यतः युवाम्) अद्य मे तुष्टौ, (अतः) उभौ अपि मम वध्यौ भवेताम्।

(yataḥ yuvām) adya me tuṣṭau, (ataḥ) ubhau api mama vadhyau bhavetām |

A single optative clause; तुष्टौ is circumstantial (‘since you are pleased’), and the anvaya spells out the implied reason. Alternatively भवेताम् can be supplied twice: ‘may you be pleased with me; may you both be slain by me’.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Viṣṇu accepts the offer and asks the one thing that ends the war: that both asuras be killable by him. Their own boon becomes the instrument of their death.

Traditional interpretation

The motif of a boon turned against the giver recurs in the Purāṇas. Here it carries the chapter’s teaching: the asuras are undone not by Viṣṇu’s strength, which five thousand years did not make decisive, but by the delusion of Mahāmāyā.

Verse 1.98

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

किमन्येन वरेणात्र एतावद्धि वृतं मम॥⁠९८⁠॥

kimanyena vareṇātra etāvaddhi vṛtaṃ mama ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

किम् · अन्येन · वरेण · अत्र · एतावत् · हि · वृतम् · मम

kim · anyena · vareṇa · atra · etāvat · hi · vṛtam · mama

Word by word

  1. किम्kimwhat (is the use)?interrogative किम्, n. nom. sg.; with the instrumental: ‘what is gained by …?’
  2. अन्येनanyenaanother, any otherpronominal adjective अन्य, m. instr. sg.; agrees with वरेण
  3. वरेणvareṇaboonm. instr. sg. of वर; instrumental with किम् (‘what need of …’)
  4. अत्रatrahere, in this matterindeclinable (adverb of place)
  5. एतावत्etāvatthis much, just thispronominal adjective एतावत्, n. nom. sg.
  6. हिhiindeed, forindeclinable (emphatic/causal particle)
  7. वृतम्vṛtamchosenpast passive participle (kta) of √वृ (‘to choose’), n. nom. sg.; predicate of एतावत्
  8. ममmamaby me, my (choice)first-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg.; agent in the genitive with वृतम्

Translation

What (use is there) here of another boon? For this much (is) chosen by me.

In readable EnglishWhat need have I of any other boon? This alone is my choice.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • वरेणात्र vareṇātra → वरेण + अत्र

    vowel sandhi (savarṇa-dīrgha) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)

    a + a → ā.

  • वरेणात्र एतावद्धि vareṇātra etāvaddhi → अत्र + एतावत्

    hiatus (metrical licence) · वृद्धिरेचि (6.1.88) not applied

    a + e should give ai (अत्रैतावत्); the text leaves the vowels apart at the pāda break. Declared in sandhi_exceptions.

  • एतावद्धि etāvaddhi → एतावत् + हि

    consonant sandhi (voicing and aspiration) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (8.2.39), झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् (8.4.62)

    Final t becomes d before the voiced h, and the h then takes the aspiration of the stop: d + h → ddh.

Left unjoined

  • अत्र | एतावत् — The vowels stand apart at the pāda break (वरेणात्र | एतावद्धि): epic verse often leaves sandhi unapplied between the first and second pādas, and joining (अत्रैतावत्) would take a syllable from the line. A metrical licence, printed so in the Gita Press text.
Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • किम् kim

    किम् with an instrumental of the thing is an idiom for ‘what is the use of …?’: किम् अन्येन वरेण ‘what (good is) another boon?’

  • वृतम् vṛtam

    Past participle of √वृ ‘to choose’ (वृ + त), neuter to agree with एतावत्. With the genitive मम it reads ‘chosen by me’ or simply ‘my choice’.

Anvaya · prose order

अत्र अन्येन वरेण किम्? एतावत् हि मम वृतम्।

atra anyena vareṇa kim? etāvat hi mama vṛtam |

A rhetorical question and a statement; हि gives the reason (‘for this much is my choice’).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Viṣṇu closes off any bargaining: he wants nothing else. The asuras, bound by their offer, cannot refuse.

Traditional interpretation

The hiatus अत्र | एतावत् falls at the pāda break and is printed so in the Gita Press text; it is a licence of epic verse, not an error, and is kept.

Verse 1.100

Half-śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

वञ्चिताभ्यामिति तदा सर्वमापोमयं जगत्॥⁠१००⁠॥

vañcitābhyāmiti tadā sarvamāpomayaṃ jagat ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

वञ्चिताभ्याम् · इति · तदा · सर्वम् · आपोमयम् · जगत्

vañcitābhyām · iti · tadā · sarvam · āpomayam · jagat

Word by word

  1. वञ्चिताभ्याम्vañcitābhyāmby the two (who had been) deceivedpast passive participle (kta) of the causative √वञ्च् (वञ्चय- ‘to deceive’), m. instr. du.; agent of गदितः (1.101)
  2. इतिitithus, in this wayindeclinable (particle, here ‘so, thus’ referring back to Viṣṇu’s words)
  3. तदाtadāthenindeclinable (adverb of time)
  4. सर्वम्sarvamthe whole, allpronominal adjective सर्व, n. acc. sg.; qualifies जगत्
  5. आपोमयम्āpomayammade of water, all watern. acc. sg. of आपोमय (आपः ‘waters’ + taddhita -मय ‘consisting of’); predicate adjective with जगत्
  6. जगत्jagatthe worldn. acc. sg. of जगत्; object of विलोक्य (1.101)

Translation

By the two, thus deceived, then — the whole world (being) made of water —

In readable EnglishThus deceived, the two then looked and saw the whole world turned to water,

‘Looked and saw’ is supplied from विलोक्य at the start of 1.101; the instrumental agent is rendered as the subject.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • सर्वमापोमयं जगत् sarvamāpomayaṃ jagat → सर्वम् + आपोमयम् + जगत्

    anusvāra · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23)

    The m of सर्वम् joins the following vowel; the m of आपोमयम् becomes anusvāra before j.

  • आपोमयं āpomayaṃ → आपः + मयम्

    visarga sandhi inside a derived word · हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    The nominative plural आपः keeps its ending before the suffix -मय, and -aḥ before m becomes -o, as between words.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • आपोमयम् āpomayam

    -मय ‘consisting of, full of’ is normally added to a stem (अप् would give अम्मय or अप्मय). आपोमय is built on the plural आपः itself — an old formation also found in Vedic prose. ‘The whole world (was) water’.

  • वञ्चिताभ्याम् vañcitābhyām

    Past participle of वञ्चय- (causative of √वञ्च्, ‘cause to go astray’, i.e. deceive), instrumental dual: the two asuras, ‘deceived’ by the boon they had granted.

Anvaya · prose order

इति वञ्चिताभ्यां (ताभ्यां) तदा सर्वं जगत् आपोमयं (विलोक्य) —

iti vañcitābhyāṃ (tābhyāṃ) tadā sarvaṃ jagat āpomayaṃ (vilokya) —

A participial agent phrase and the object of an absolutive; the absolutive विलोक्य and the passive verb गदितः come in 1.101.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The asuras realise they have been caught by their own word. Looking about for a way out, they see that the whole world is water — the cosmic flood on which Viṣṇu slept (1.66–67).

Traditional interpretation

Who deceived them is left implicit: by Viṣṇu’s taking them at their word, and behind that by Mahāmāyā, who had bewildered them (1.94). The narrative makes the deception the Goddess’s work, done through the god.

Verse 1.101

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

विलोक्य ताभ्यां गदितो भगवान् कमलेक्षणः।आवां जहि न यत्रोर्वी सलिलेन परिप्लुता॥⁠१०१⁠॥

Padaccheda · the words separated

विलोक्य · ताभ्याम् · गदितः · भगवान् · कमलेक्षणःआवाम् · जहि · न · यत्र · उर्वी · सलिलेन · परिप्लुता

vilokya · tābhyām · gaditaḥ · bhagavān · kamalekṣaṇaḥāvām · jahi · na · yatra · urvī · salilena · pariplutā

Word by word

  1. विलोक्यvilokyahaving looked at, having seenabsolutive (ल्यप्) of वि + √लोक् (‘to look’)
  2. ताभ्याम्tābhyāmby the twopronoun तद्, m. instr. du.; agent of गदितः
  3. गदितःgaditaḥwas addressed, was toldpast passive participle (kta) of √गद् (bhvādi, 1P, ‘to speak’), m. nom. sg.; used as the finite verb
  4. भगवान्bhagavānthe Blessed Onem. nom. sg. of भगवत्; subject of गदितः
  5. कमलेक्षणःkamalekṣaṇaḥthe lotus-eyedm. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies भगवान्
  6. आवाम्āvāmus twofirst-person pronoun अस्मद्, acc. du.; object of जहि
  7. जहिjahislay!√हन् (adādi, 2P, ‘to strike, kill’), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  8. नnanotindeclinable (negative particle)
  9. यत्रyatrawhereindeclinable (relative adverb of place)
  10. उर्वीurvīthe earth (‘the broad one’)f. nom. sg. of उर्वी (feminine of उरु ‘wide’)
  11. सलिलेनsalilenawith watern. instr. sg. of सलिल
  12. परिप्लुताpariplutāflooded, overflowedpast passive participle (kta) of परि + √प्लु (bhvādi, 1Ā, ‘to float, flow’), f. nom. sg.; agrees with उर्वी

Translation

having looked, the lotus-eyed Blessed One was addressed by the two: ‘Slay us where the earth is not flooded with water.’

In readable Englishand they said to the lotus-eyed Lord, “Slay us where the earth is not flooded with water.”

The passive (‘was addressed by the two’) is rendered actively.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • ताभ्यां गदितो भगवान् tābhyāṃ gadito bhagavān → ताभ्याम् + गदितः + भगवान्

    anusvāra and visarga sandhi · मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23); हशि च (6.1.114), आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    Final m before g becomes anusvāra; -aḥ before the voiced bh becomes -o.

  • यत्रोर्वी yatrorvī → यत्र + उर्वी

    vowel sandhi (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + u → o.

  • कमलेक्षणः kamalekṣaṇaḥ → कमल + ईक्षणः

    vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87)

    a + ī → e.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • कमलेक्षणः kamalekṣaṇaḥ

    bahuvrīhi (with an implied comparison, ‘like’)

    Members
    कमल + ईक्षण
    Vigraha
    कमले इव ईक्षणे यस्य सः kamale iva īkṣaṇe yasya saḥ
    Literally
    “he whose eyes are like lotuses”
    In the verse
    the lotus-eyed Viṣṇu
Morphology & anvaya

  • जहि jahi

    Imperative second singular of √हन्: before the ending -हि the root is replaced by ज- (ज + हि → जहि). The asuras still speak as if commanding.

  • गदितः gaditaḥ

    Past passive participle of √गद् with the connecting vowel -इ-: ‘(was) spoken to’. The person addressed is the subject (भगवान्), the speakers the agent (ताभ्याम्).

  • विलोक्य vilokya

    Absolutive in -य after the prefix वि-. Its agent is the instrumental ताभ्याम्, the agent of the passive main verb — a regular construction.

Anvaya · prose order

(सर्वम् आपोमयं जगत्) विलोक्य ताभ्यां कमलेक्षणः भगवान् गदितः — ‘यत्र उर्वी सलिलेन परिप्लुता न (अस्ति, तत्र) आवां जहि।’

(sarvam āpomayaṃ jagat) vilokya tābhyāṃ kamalekṣaṇaḥ bhagavān gaditaḥ — ‘yatra urvī salilena pariplutā na (asti, tatra) āvāṃ jahi | ’

The first line completes 1.100 with a passive main verb (गदितः); the second is the asuras’ words, a command with a relative clause of place (यत्र … न).

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

The asuras try to slip their promise: since the whole world is water, a place ‘where the earth is not flooded’ seems not to exist. They grant the boon on a condition they think cannot be met.

Traditional interpretation

The Purāṇa recension (the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa as edited in GRETIL) has further lines after this verse that the Gita Press text does not carry; this edition follows the Gita Press 700 and adds nothing (see corrections.json, recension notes).

Verse 1.103

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

तथेत्युक्त्वा भगवता शङ्खचक्रगदाभृता।कृत्वा चक्रेण वै च्छिन्ने जघने शिरसी तयोः॥⁠१०३⁠॥

Padaccheda · the words separated

तथा · इति · उक्त्वा · भगवता · शङ्खचक्रगदाभृताकृत्वा · चक्रेण · वै · छिन्ने · जघने · शिरसी · तयोः

Word by word

  1. तथाtathāso (be it)indeclinable (adverb of manner; here assent)
  2. इतिitithus (closing the quotation)indeclinable (quotative particle)
  3. उक्त्वाuktvāhaving saidabsolutive (ktvā) of √वच्
  4. भगवताbhagavatāby the Blessed Onem. instr. sg. of भगवत्; agent of छिन्ने and of the absolutives उक्त्वा, कृत्वा

  7. चक्रेणcakreṇawith the discusn. instr. sg. of चक्र; instrument of छिन्ने
  8. वैvaiindeedindeclinable (emphatic particle)
  9. छिन्नेchinnewere cut offpast passive participle (kta) of √छिद् (rudhādi, 7U, ‘to cut’), n. nom. du.; agrees with शिरसी; used as the finite verb

Translation

Having said ‘So (be it)’, by the Blessed One, bearer of conch, discus and mace, having placed (them) on (his) loins, the two heads of the two were indeed cut off with the discus.

The passive is rendered actively. जघन, properly the hips or loins, is rendered ‘lap’: the one place above the water.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • तथेत्युक्त्वा tathetyuktvā → तथा + इति + उक्त्वा

    vowel sandhi (guṇa and yaṇ) · आद्गुणः (6.1.87); इको यणचि (6.1.77)

    ā + i → e (तथा + इति → तथेति); then i before u becomes y (इति + उक्त्वा → इत्युक्त्वा).

  • वै च्छिन्ने vai cchinne → वै + छिन्ने

    consonant sandhi (doubling of ch) · छे च (6.1.73), पदान्ताद्वा (6.1.76)

    After a word ending in a long vowel, initial ch may be written cch. The Gita Press writes the added c at the head of the next word.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

  • शङ्खचक्रगदाभृता śaṅkhacakragadābhṛtā

    upapada tatpuruṣa containing an itaretara dvandva (शङ्खचक्रगदा)

    Members
    शङ्ख + चक्र + गदा + भृत्
    Vigraha
    शङ्खः च चक्रं च गदा च शङ्खचक्रगदाः; ताः बिभर्ति इति शङ्खचक्रगदाभृत्, तेन śaṅkhaḥ ca cakraṃ ca gadā ca śaṅkhacakragadāḥ; tāḥ bibharti iti śaṅkhacakragadābhṛt, tena
    Literally
    “by the bearer of conch, discus and mace”
    In the verse
    by Viṣṇu, named by his emblems; -भृत् is √भृ ‘to bear’ with the zero kṛt affix (kvip) and an added t
Morphology & anvaya

  • छिन्ने chinne

    Past participle of √छिद्: after the root’s final d the t of the suffix becomes n and the d becomes n too (छिद् + त → छिन्न). Neuter dual -ए, agreeing with शिरसी: ‘the two heads were cut off’.

  • उक्त्वा uktvā

    Absolutive of √वच् with samprasāraṇa (व → उ) and k for c: उक्त्वा ‘having said’. With कृत्वा it gives two steps before the main act.

  • शिरसी śirasī

    Neuter dual of शिरस्: nominative and accusative are the same (शिरसी), so the one word serves both as the object of कृत्वा (‘having placed their heads’) and the subject of छिन्ने (‘the heads were cut off’). A neuter dual in -ī (like छिन्ने in -e) is pragṛhya and would stand unjoined before a vowel (ईदूदेद्द्विवचनं प्रगृह्यम्, 1.1.11); here a consonant follows, so no question of sandhi arises.

Anvaya · prose order

‘तथा’ इति उक्त्वा, शङ्खचक्रगदाभृता भगवता तयोः शिरसी जघने कृत्वा चक्रेण वै छिन्ने।

‘tathā’ iti uktvā, śaṅkhacakragadābhṛtā bhagavatā tayoḥ śirasī jaghane kṛtvā cakreṇa vai chinne |

A passive sentence: the subject शिरसी with its verb छिन्ने, the agent भगवता, and two absolutives (उक्त्वा, कृत्वा) sharing that agent. शिरसी does double duty as the object of कृत्वा.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Viṣṇu meets the condition exactly: the only ground not covered by water is his own body. He lays their heads on his lap and cuts them off with the discus. The asuras die by the terms of their own boon.

Traditional interpretation

The narrative turns the asuras’ cleverness against them, as the boon itself was turned (1.97). The cause, as the chapter has insisted, is Mahāmāyā’s delusion rather than force: five thousand years of fighting did not end the war, a confusion of mind did.

Modern reflection

A modern reflection: the asuras look for a loophole in the world and find none outside the one they are fighting. The story leaves no place that is not within the Lord’s reach.

Verse 1.104

Śloka · anuṣṭubh
‹›

एवमेषा समुत्पन्ना ब्रह्मणा संस्तुता स्वयम्।प्रभावमस्या देव्यास्तु भूयः शृणु वदामि ते॥⁠१०४⁠॥ऐं ॐ

evameṣā samutpannā brahmaṇā saṃstutā svayam |prabhāvamasyā devyāstu bhūyaḥ śṛṇu vadāmi te ||

Padaccheda · the words separated

एवम् · एषा · समुत्पन्ना · ब्रह्मणा · संस्तुता · स्वयम्प्रभावम् · अस्याः · देव्याः · तु · भूयः · शृणु · वदामि · ते

evam · eṣā · samutpannā · brahmaṇā · saṃstutā · svayamprabhāvam · asyāḥ · devyāḥ · tu · bhūyaḥ · śṛṇu · vadāmi · te

Word by word

  1. एवम्evamthus, in this wayindeclinable (adverb of manner)
  2. एषाeṣāshe, this (Goddess)pronoun एतद्, f. nom. sg.; subject
  3. समुत्पन्नाsamutpannāarose, appearedpast participle (kta) of सम् + उद् + √पद् (divādi, 4Ā, ‘to go’), f. nom. sg.; used as the finite verb
  4. ब्रह्मणाbrahmaṇāby Brahmām. instr. sg. of ब्रह्मन्; agent of संस्तुता
  5. संस्तुताsaṃstutāpraisedpast passive participle (kta) of सम् + √स्तु, f. nom. sg.
  6. स्वयम्svayamhimself, in personindeclinable (reflexive adverb); here emphasising ब्रह्मणा
  7. प्रभावम्prabhāvamthe power, the glorym. acc. sg. of प्रभाव; object of शृणु
  8. अस्याःasyāḥof thispronoun इदम्, f. gen. sg.; agrees with देव्याः
  9. देव्याःdevyāḥof the Goddessf. gen. sg. of देवी
  10. तुtunow, butindeclinable (particle marking a new topic)
  11. भूयःbhūyaḥfurther, againindeclinable (adverb; comparative of बहु in form)
  12. शृणुśṛṇuhear!√श्रु (svādi, 5P, ‘to hear’), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  13. वदामिvadāmiI (shall) tell√वद् (bhvādi, 1P, ‘to speak’), laṭ (present), uttama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
  14. तेteto youenclitic form of युष्मद्, dat. sg.

Translation

Thus she arose, praised by Brahmā himself. But hear further the power of this Goddess; I tell (it) to you.

In readable EnglishSo it was that she appeared, praised by Brahmā himself. Now hear more of this Goddess’s power; I shall tell you.

स्वयम् is taken with ब्रह्मणा (‘by Brahmā himself’). It can also be taken with the subject: ‘she appeared of her own accord’.

Textual verification / uncertain: स्वयम् may qualify ब्रह्मणा (‘by Brahmā himself’, chosen) or the Goddess (‘she arose of her own accord’); both readings are grammatical.

Sandhi & sandhi-viccheda

  • अस्या देव्यास्तु asyā devyāstu → अस्याः + देव्याः + तु

    visarga sandhi · भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (8.3.17), लोपः शाकल्यस्य (8.3.19); विसर्जनीयस्य सः (8.3.34)

    -āḥ before a voiced sound loses its visarga (अस्या देव्याः); before t the visarga becomes s (देव्यास्तु).

  • भूयः शृणु bhūyaḥ śṛṇu → भूयः + शृणु

    visarga sandhi (optional assimilation not applied) · खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः (8.3.15)

    Before ś the visarga may stay or become ś; the text keeps the visarga.

Samāsa & samāsa-vigraha

No compound in this verse needs analysis.

Morphology & anvaya

  • समुत्पन्ना samutpannā

    Past participle of सम् + उद् + √पद्: d + t → nn (पद् + त → पन्न). Used as a finite verb: ‘(she) arose’. The word picks up उत्पन्ना of 1.66.

  • शृणु śṛṇu

    Imperative of √श्रु (svādi): the root becomes शृ- before the class sign -नु, which becomes -णु after ṛ; the ending -हि is dropped after the u of the class sign.

  • वदामि vadāmi

    Present tense used for the immediate future: ‘I am going to tell you’. Medhas announces the next story (chapters 2–4).

Anvaya · prose order

एवम् एषा (देवी) स्वयं ब्रह्मणा संस्तुता समुत्पन्ना। अस्याः देव्याः प्रभावं तु भूयः शृणु, (अहं) ते वदामि।

evam eṣā (devī) svayaṃ brahmaṇā saṃstutā samutpannā | asyāḥ devyāḥ prabhāvaṃ tu bhūyaḥ śṛṇu, (ahaṃ) te vadāmi |

A closing summary (एवम् … समुत्पन्ना), then the transition to the next story: an imperative and a first-person present.

Śākta commentary

Direct textual meaning

Medhas closes the first story and opens the next. The ring is complete: he had said that the eternal Goddess is called ‘born’ (उत्पन्ना) when she appears for the gods’ purpose (1.65–66); now he says एवम् एषा समुत्पन्ना — ‘this is how she arose’. शृणु and ते are singular: he speaks to the king.

Traditional interpretation

This is the last mantra of chapter 1. In the Gita Press pāṭha it is followed by the bījas ऐं ॐ, closing the sampuṭa that ॐ ऐं opened in 1.1; they belong to the recitation, not to the Purāṇa. The colophon names the chapter मधुकैटभवधः, the Slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the first carita, which the pāṭha assigns to Mahākālī.

Comparative Śrīvidyā notes

Comparative Śākta / Śrīvidyā

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has a name for a goddess praised by the gods, 83 ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिदेवसंस्तुतवैभवा, ‘whose glory is praised by Brahmā, Upendra, Mahendra and the other gods’. The motif is shared; the Devī Māhātmya has just told one such praise in full.

❁

इति श्रीमार्कण्डेयपुराणे सावर्णिके मन्वन्तरे देवीमाहात्म्ये मधुकैटभवधो नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः॥

iti śrīmārkaṇḍeyapurāṇe sāvarṇike manvantare devīmāhātmye madhukaiṭabhavadho nāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ ||

Reflecting on the chapter

Two men who have lost everything, a king to his ministers and a merchant to his family, find that losing things has not loosened their hold on them. Medhas names the power behind that hold — Mahāmāyā — and, to show who she is, tells the first of the three stories: Brahmā’s praise of Yoganidrā, her withdrawal from the sleeping Viṣṇu, and the death of Madhu and Kaiṭabha. The chapter ends with a promise: more of her power is still to be told (1.104).

Verses for study and memorisation

  • 1.55Mahāmāyā deludes the world and draws even the wise into delusion.
  • 1.57She is the supreme knowledge, the eternal cause of liberation.
  • 1.64Eternal, the world her form: the definition of the Goddess in the frame story.
  • 1.73त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा — the opening of Brahmā’s hymn.
  • 1.75You are Sandhyā and Sāvitrī, the supreme mother; by you this universe is borne and created (continued in 1.76: protected, and consumed at the end).
  • 1.82Whatever thing exists anywhere, real or unreal — with 1.83: the power of all of it is you; how then can you be praised?
Vocabulary, constructions and insights

Principal vocabulary

  • महामायाmahāmāyāthe Great Māyā: the Goddess as the power that veils, binds and releases
  • योगनिद्राyoganidrāyogic sleep: the Goddess as Viṣṇu’s sleep between ages
  • ममत्वम्mamatvam‘mine-ness’, possessive attachment
  • मोहःmohaḥdelusion, bewilderment
  • विद्याvidyāknowledge that liberates
  • स्तुतिःstutiḥpraise, hymn
  • स्वाहाsvāhāthe offering-call to the gods; the Goddess named as it
  • स्वधाsvadhāthe offering-call to the ancestors
  • कालरात्रिःkālarātriḥthe night of time, of dissolution
  • तामसीtāmasīthe dark one, the Goddess of tamas
  • मन्वन्तरम्manvantaramthe age of a Manu
  • आश्रमःāśramaḥa sage’s hermitage

Important grammatical constructions

  • The perfect and the aorist as the narrative past (उवाच, बभूव, अभूत्, अद्राक्षीत्).
  • The speaker in the genitive with verbs of hearing (निशामय … गदतो मम, 1.2).
  • Long periodic sentences carried across several ślokas (1.12–16, 1.22–24, 1.51–55); the anvaya joins them.
  • Passive of a causative with an instrumental agent (तया सम्मोह्यते जगत्, 1.55).
  • The gerundive of obligation with न (विस्मयः न कार्यः, 1.54).
  • Hymn style: त्वम् with a predicate nominative, repeated in series (त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा …, 1.73), feminine vocatives, and compounds of praise.
  • Pūrvarūpa (-e/-o + a → avagraha) and -aḥ → -o are the commonest sandhis of the chapter.

Śākta insights

  • Attachment is a power, not only a fault: the wise are bound by the same Mahāmāyā as the birds (1.49–55).
  • The power that binds is the power that frees: she is vidyā and the cause of liberation, and also the cause of bondage (1.57–58).
  • The Goddess is eternal and unborn, yet is said to ‘arise’ whenever she appears for the gods’ purposes (1.64–65).
  • Even Viṣṇu, the sustainer, is subject to her: his waking is her withdrawal (1.88–90).
  • Brahmā’s hymn names her as everything that is — creation, sustenance and dissolution (1.75–77) — and as both gentle and terrible (1.80–82).

Śrīvidyā connections

The chapter shares names with the Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) — Mahāmāyā (215), Viṣṇumāyā (339), Kālarātri and others noted on the verses — and both texts treat the Goddess as the power behind Viṣṇu and Brahmā. These are shared Śākta ideas, not evidence that one text depends on the other; no specifically Śrīvidyā doctrine is stated in this chapter.

Sandhi patterns
  • -aḥ before voiced consonants → -o, and -aḥ before a → -o’ (the commonest junctions).
  • Pūrvarūpa: -e/-o + a- → avagraha (कथ्यतेऽष्टमः, सोऽचिन्तयत्).
  • Visarga → ś/s before c/t (हेतुश्च, कस्त्वम्).
  • n + l → ṃ̐l (भवाँल्लुब्धैः, 1.27); t + n → nn (तन्नात्र, 1.54); savarṇa-dīrgha and guṇa across words.
  • One declared hiatus: अत्र | एतावत् at the pāda break of 1.98.
Samāsa constructions
  • Ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣas throughout the narrative (सूर्यतनयः, क्षितिमण्डले).
  • Bahuvrīhis of epithet (महाभागः, चैत्रवंशसमुद्भवः).
  • Upapada tatpuruṣas with agent nouns (संसारस्थितिकारिणा, शङ्खचक्रगदाभृता).
  • Karmadhārayas of divine names (महामाया, योगनिद्रा, महाविद्या), and dvandvas in the hymn’s lists.
Grammatical observations
  • Several sentences run across verses; every such anvaya says so.
  • ददृशे (1.92) is read as active ‘saw’, an ārṣa use of the ātmanepada ending.
  • पञ्च is separated from वर्षसहस्राणि in the padaccheda (1.94): a dvigu would be singular.
  • The hypermetric pāda of 1.92 is kept as every witness has it.
Philosophical themes
  • Mamatā and moha
  • Mahāmāyā as bondage and liberation
  • Yoganidrā and the waking of Viṣṇu
  • Stuti as the turning point
Open questions
  • 1.78: महासुरी (Gita Press) / महेश्वरी (GRETIL, Freund) — check the printed book.
  • Interpretive doubts are flagged on 1.5, 1.22, 1.27, 1.43, 1.71, 1.74, 1.92 and 1.104.
